那天清晨，一队精锐重装骑兵浩浩荡荡驰出热那亚，铁甲胸铠在朝阳下熠熠生辉，沿着斯克里维亚河（Scrivia）谷的高地大路，朝诺维（Novi）和法奇诺的营地进发。队伍中央抬着一乘骡轿，法奇诺坐在轿中，心中反反复复咀嚼着世人的卑劣与忘恩负义，暗自寻思：他那位野心勃勃的伯爵夫人之所以对他屡屡不满，抱怨他终日戎马劳碌却只知为人作嫁、不为自身谋取权势，或许也并非全无道理。

一抵诺维，他便立刻派遣卡尔马尼奥拉率领一支精干的护卫队赶往卡萨莱，刻不容缓地将贝阿特丽切伯爵夫人接往亚历山德里亚。吉安·贾科莫既已留在法奇诺身边，他可绝不愿让西奥多把伯爵夫人扣作人质，用来与他讨价还价。

离开诺维三天后，法奇诺的大军抵达了维杰瓦诺（Vigevano）——虽因西奥多麾下那支三千人的部队留在了后方而有所减员，兵力却依然十分雄厚——并在城外重新扎下营寨。大军之所以在此驻留，主要是法奇诺的好胜心使然：在伤愈重新跨上马背之前，他绝不肯渡过提契诺河（Ticino），因为他定要持枪抵胯、威风凛凛地骑马开进米兰城。好在他随行队伍里如今有了一位名叫蒙贝利（Mombelli）的热那亚名医，此人素以精擅诊治痛风宿疾闻名；在他的悉心调理下，法奇诺的病情已大为好转。

一周过去，法奇诺已然彻底康复，全凭那位医生的苦口婆心劝阻，才暂且按捺住挥师东进的念头。不过在此期间，他虽未踏进米兰一步，米兰城里却有大批人马络绎不绝地赶来投奔他。

最先赶到营中的人里，便有韦内戈诺（Venegono）的急先锋普斯泰尔拉；他满怀切齿复仇之念，力劝法奇诺干脆绞死吉安·玛丽亚，自立为米兰公爵，并拍胸脯保证吉伯林派全党上下都会鼎力拥戴。法奇诺面无波澜地听完，不肯吐露半句承诺。

===Original===
Amongst the last to arrive was the Duke himself, in a rash trustfulness which revealed the desperate view he must take of his own case and of the helplessness to which his folly and faithlessness had reduced him. He came accompanied by his evil genius Antonio della Torre, the fop Lonate, the captain of his guard Bertino Mantegazza, and a paltry escort of a hundred lances.

With those three attending him he was received by Facino in the house of the Ducal Prefect of Vigevano.

“Your highness honours me by this proof of your trust in my integrity,” said Facino, bending to kiss the jewelled ducal hand.

“Integrity!” The Duke’s grotesque face was white, his red eyebrows drawn together in a scowl. “Is it integrity that brings you in arms against me, Facino?”

“Not against you, Lord Duke. Never yet have I stood in arms against your highness. It is upon your enemies that I make war. I have no aim but the restoration of peace to your dominions.”

“Fine words on the lips of a mutinous traitor!” sneered the Duke. He flung himself petulantly into a chair.

===Chinese===
最后一批赶来的人中，竟赫然包括公爵本人——他这般鲁莽轻信地只身前来，足见他对自身处境已抱持何等绝望的念头，也暴露出他自身的愚蠢与背信弃义究竟将他逼入了怎样束手无策的绝境。随他同行的，只有他的奸佞心腹安东尼奥·德拉托雷（Antonio della Torre）、纨绔佞臣洛纳泰、近卫队长贝尔蒂诺·曼泰加扎（Bertino Mantegazza），以及区区一百支长枪骑兵的微薄护卫。

就在这三人的簇拥下，公爵于维杰瓦诺公爵行政长官的宅邸中见到了法奇诺。

“殿下如此信任在下的赤胆忠心，实令在下不胜荣幸。”法奇诺说着，俯身吻了吻公爵戴满珠宝的手背。

“赤胆忠心！”公爵那张怪诞丑陋的脸孔惨白一片，两条红眉拧成一道怒结，“法奇诺，难道是赤胆忠心让你披坚执锐来跟我作对吗？”

“并非与您作对，公爵大人。在下从未举兵与殿下为敌。我讨伐的乃是您的仇敌。我别无所求，唯愿让您的领地重归太平。”

“从一个犯上作乱的叛徒嘴里说出来，可真是漂亮话！”公爵冷笑一声，赌气似的把自己重重摔进椅子里。

===Original===
“If your highness believed that, you would not dare to come here.”

“Not dare? God’s bones, man! Are these words for me? I am Duke of Milan.”

“I study to remember it, highness,” said Facino, and the rumblings of anger in his voice drove della Torre to pluck at his master’s sleeve.

Thus warned, Gian Maria changed the subject but not the tone. “You know why I am here?”

“To permit me, I hope, to place myself at your potency’s commands.”

“Ah! Bah! You make me sick with your fair words.” He grew sullen. “Come, man. What is your price?”

===Chinese===
“殿下若当真信这话，今日便不敢踏足此地了。”

“不敢？凭天主的圣骨起誓，你这狂徒！竟敢对我说这种话？我可是米兰公爵！”

“殿下，在下时刻铭记于心。”法奇诺答道，嗓音里隐隐滚动的怒雷，逼得德拉托雷急忙暗中扯了扯主上的衣袖。

经这一扯提醒，吉安·玛丽亚虽改口转了话锋，腔调却依旧傲慢：“你可知道我为何而来？”

“但愿是来恩准在下效力于权势显赫的殿下麾下，听候差遣。”

“呸！少拿你那些花言巧语来恶心我！”他沉下脸，满面阴郁，“痛快些，说吧，你的价码是多少？”

===Original===
“My price, highness? What does your highness conceive I have to sell?”

“A little patience with his magnificence, my lord,” della Torre begged.

“I thought I was displaying it,” said Facino. “Otherwise it might be very bad for everybody.” He was really growing angry.

And now the idiot Duke must needs go prodding him into fury.

“What’s that? Do you threaten me? Why, here’s an insolent dog!”

Facino turned livid with passion. A tall fellow among his captains, very noble-looking in cloth of silver under a blue houppelande, laughed aloud. The pale, bulging eyes of Gian Maria sought him out venomously.

===Chinese===
“我的价码，殿下？不知殿下以为在下手里有什么待价而沽之物？”

“大人，还请对尊贵的公爵殿下多包涵几分。”德拉托雷低声恳求道。

“我自以为已经够有耐心了，”法奇诺说，“否则在座各位只怕全都没好果子吃。”他是当真动了肝火。

偏偏这蠢笨不堪的公爵还要往枪口上撞，硬生生把他激得暴跳如雷。

“你说什么？你竟敢威胁我？好啊，真是一只目中无人的恶犬！”

法奇诺气得脸色铁青。就在这时，站在他麾下众将领当中的一个高大汉子突然放声大笑起来；那人一袭蓝色乌普朗德长袍（houppelande），内衬银线织锦衣袍，显得气宇轩昂。吉安·玛丽亚那双惨白凸出的眼珠顿时恶毒地朝他搜寻过去。

===Original===
“You laugh, knave?” he snarled, and came to his feet, outraged by the indignity. “What is here for laughter?”

Bellarion laughed again as he answered: “Yourself, Lord Duke, who in yourself are nothing. You are Duke of Milan at present by the grace of God and the favour of Facino Cane. Yet you do not hesitate to offend against both.”

“Quiet, Bellarion,” Facino growled. “I need no advocate.”

“Bellarion!” the Duke echoed, glaring malevolently. “I remember you, and remember you I shall. You shall be taught﻿ ﻿…”

“By God, it is your highness shall be taught!” Facino crashed into the threatening speech roaring like a thundergod. “Get you hence, back to your Milan until I come to give you the lesson that you need, and thank God that you are your father’s son and I have grace enough to remember it, for otherwise you’d never go hence alive! Away with you, and get yourself schooled in manners before we meet again or as God’s my life I’ll birch you with these hands.”

===Chinese===
“奴才，你笑什么？”他厉声咆哮，受此奇耻大辱，猛地站起身来，“这儿有什么好笑的？”

贝拉里翁又笑了一声，答道：“笑的便是公爵大人您自己——您本身分文不值，如今能坐稳这米兰公爵之位，全仰仗上帝的恩典与法奇诺·卡内的垂青。可您偏偏毫不顾忌，竟将这两位一并得罪。”

“闭嘴，贝拉里翁，”法奇诺低喝一声，“用不着你替我出头说话。”

“贝拉里翁！”公爵咬牙切齿地重复着这个名字，眼中射出怨毒的凶光，“我记住你了，我定会牢牢记住你的！迟早要教训教训你……”

“天主作证，该受教训的是殿下你自己！”法奇诺宛如雷神震怒般轰然打断了他的威胁，“给我滚回去，滚回你的米兰去！等着我亲临给你上这一堂你正欠缺的课。你该谢天谢地，亏得你还是你父亲的儿子，又亏得我还念着几分旧情——否则今日你休想活着走出这扇门！快给我滚，趁着咱们下回再见之前，先把礼数给我学周全了；不然凭天主起誓，我定要亲手拿桦条狠狠抽你一顿！”

===Original===
Terrified, cowering before that raging storm, the line of which had never yet broken about his ducal head, Gian Maria shrank back until his three companions were between himself and Facino. Della Torre, almost trembling, sought to pacify the angry condottiero.

“My lord! My lord! This is not worthy!”

“Not worthy! Is it worthy that I shall be called ‘dog’ by a cross-grained brat to whom I’ve played the foster-father? Out of my sight, sir! Out of my sight, all of you! The door, Bellarion! The Duke of Milan to the door!”

They went without another word, fearing, indeed, that another word might be their last. But they did not yet return to Milan. They remained in Vigevano, and that evening della Torre came seeking audience again of Facino to make the Duke’s peace with him, and Facino, having swallowed his rage by then, consented to receive his highness once more.

The young man came, this time well schooled in prudence, to announce that he was prepared to give Facino peaceful entrance into Milan and to restore him to his office of ducal governor. In short, that he was prepared to accord all that which he had no power to refuse.

===Chinese===
面对这场劈头盖脸砸下来的雷霆风暴——他贵为公爵，平生还从未领教过这等骇人的阵仗——吉安·玛丽亚吓得魂飞魄散，连连倒退缩身，直到把三个随从全都挡在自己与法奇诺之间。德拉托雷几乎浑身颤抖，战战兢兢地试图安抚这位盛怒的雇佣兵统帅：

“大人！大人！何至于此，实在有失体统！”

“有失体统！我像义父一般照拂拉扯着这么个性情乖戾的小畜生，他反倒张口骂我作‘犬’，这就有体统了么？给我滚出我的视线，阁下！统统滚出去！贝拉里翁，开门！请米兰公爵出门！”

那一行人再不敢多吐半个字，生怕多说一句便会丢了性命，灰溜溜地退了出去。不过他们并未就此返回米兰，而是继续留在维杰瓦诺。当晚，德拉托雷便再度求见法奇诺，代公爵前来求和；法奇诺此时也已咽下心头怒火，便答应再次接见公爵殿下。

这位年轻公爵再度登门时，已是乖乖学足了审慎恭顺的做派，当即宣称愿迎法奇诺和平入驻米兰，并恢复他公爵辅政总管之职——简言之，凡是他无力拒绝的条件，他一概应允。

===Original===
Facino’s answer was brief and clear. He would accept the office again, provided that it was bestowed upon him for a term of three years, and the bestowal guaranteed by an oath of fealty to be sworn upon his hands by the Syndics of the Grand Council. Further, the Castle of Porta Giovia was to be delivered into his keeping absolutely, and not only the Guelphic Sanseverino, who now held the office of Podestà, but all other Guelphs holding offices of State must be dismissed. Lastly, Antonio della Torre, whom Facino accused of being at the root of most of the trouble which had distracted Milan, must go into banishment together with Lonate.

This last was the condition that Gian Maria would not swallow. He swore it was a vile attempt to deprive him of all his friends.

Thus the conference ended inconclusively, and it was not until three weeks later that the Duke finally yielded, and accepted Facino’s terms in their entirety.

On the evening of Wednesday, the sixth of November of that year, attended by a large company, Facino Cane, Count of Biandrate, rode into Milan to resume his governorship, a governorship which he was resolved to render absolute this time. They entered the city in a downpour of rain, notwithstanding which the streets were thronged by the people who turned out to welcome the man in whom they beheld their saviour.

And in the Old Broletto, the young Duke, without a single friendly Guelph at hand to comfort him, sat listening to that uproar, gnawing his fingernails and shuddering with rage and spite.

===Chinese===
法奇诺的答复简明扼要、斩钉截铁：他可以重新出任此职，但前提是任期须定为三年，且须由大议会（Grand Council）的市政代表（Syndics）亲手向他宣誓效忠，以为担保；其次，波尔塔焦维亚城堡（Castle of Porta Giovia）须毫无保留地交由他全权掌管，不仅眼下担任执政官的归尔甫派分子圣塞韦里诺（Sanseverino），其余一切身居国家要职的归尔甫派成员也必须悉数罢黜；最后，被法奇诺直指为米兰连年动荡祸根的安东尼奥·德拉托雷，必须与洛纳泰一同放逐出境。

唯独最后这一条，吉安·玛丽亚死活咽不下去。他赌咒发誓地说，这是存心剥夺他身边所有忠心友朋的卑劣企图。

于是这场会谈不欢而散，未能达成协议；直到三周之后，公爵才终于彻底屈服，全盘接受了法奇诺的所有条件。

那年十一月六日星期三的傍晚，比安德拉泰伯爵法奇诺·卡内在一支浩大随从队伍的簇拥下，骑马开入米兰城，重掌辅政大权——而这一次，他已铁了心要把这权力握得绝对而稳固。他们入城时正值瓢泼大雨倾盆而下，即便如此，街道两旁依旧挤满了倾城而出的百姓，争相欢呼迎迓这位在他们眼中堪称救星的人物。

而在旧布罗莱托宫里，那位年轻的公爵身边连一个可堪慰藉的归尔甫派亲信也没有，只得独自坐在宫中聆听窗外山呼海啸般的欢呼声，一边狠狠啃噬着自己的指甲，一边气得浑身发抖、恨毒入骨。

===Original===
It becomes necessary, however, to remember, lest we should be swept along by this stream of Viscontean history, that this present chronicle is concerned not with the fortunes of Milan, but with those of Bellarion, and that in these Facino Cane and Gian Maria Visconti are concerned only to the extent of the part they bore in moulding them.

In the confused pages of old Corio you may read in detail, though you may not always clearly understand, the events that followed upon Facino’s triumphant return to Milan. You will gather that the strength in which he was known to be gave pause to Malatesta’s plans to seize the Duchy; that in fact the arch-Guelph chose to content himself with his usurpation of the lordship of Brescia and Bergamo, and in Bergamo he remained until Facino went to seek him there some two years later. If he did not go before, it was because other more immediate and active enemies of Milan claimed his attention. Vignate was in arms again, as were also Estorre Visconti and his nephew Giovanni Carlo, and a host of lesser insurgents, chief of whom was the Duke’s own brother, that Filippo Maria Visconti who was Count of Pavia. By the Ghibellines who had fled to him from Milan during the days of Malatesta and Boucicault’s domination, Filippo Maria had been flattered into believing that he was that party’s only hope in Northern Italy. His ambition thus aroused, he was ready to take advantage of the general distraction, and to appropriate for himself the ducal chlamys. To this purpose was he arming when Facino returned to Milan, and news of his preparations reached Facino whilst he was suppressing the various rebellious outbreaks in the Milanese, stamping out the embers of revolt in such places as Desio and Gorgonzola. Only when he had restored order, established a proper administration, and so brought back tranquillity to that harassed land, did he turn his attention to the menace of the enemies farther afield. And the first of these was Filippo Maria. He marched on Pavia, carried the city by assault and put it to sack, choosing of all nights in the year for that operation the night of Christmas.

That sack of Pavia is one of the most unsparing and terrible in the terrible history of sacks, and the deed remains a blot upon the fame of a soldier who, although rough and occasionally even brutal in his ways, was yet a leader of high principles and a high sense of duty.

Thereafter he dealt with Filippo Maria much as he had dealt with his ducal brother. He appointed himself governor of the young man’s dominions, filled the offices of State with men in his own confidence and completely stripped the Count of authority.

The fat, flabby young Prince submitted in a singularly apathetic fashion. He was of solitary, studious habits, a recluse, almost savagely shy, shunning the society of men because of his excessive consciousness of his own grotesque ugliness.

The spark of ambition that had been struck from him having been thus summarily quenched, he retired to his books again, and let Facino have his way with the State, nor complained so long as Facino left him in the enjoyment of the little that was really necessary to his eremitic ways.

===Chinese===
然而在此却须牢记，免得我们被维斯孔蒂家族这段滚滚史潮裹挟而去：眼下这部编年记所关切的，并非米兰一城的兴衰浮沉，而是贝拉里翁的命运遭际；法奇诺·卡内与吉安·玛丽亚·维斯孔蒂在书中所占的分量，也仅仅止于他们参与塑造贝拉里翁命运的那一部分。

在老史学家科里奥（Corio）那部头绪纷繁的史卷里，诸位固然可以读到法奇诺凯旋重返米兰之后的种种详尽经过——纵使读来未必总能理清其中脉络。从字里行间不难看出，他那公认的雄厚实力迫使马拉泰斯塔不得不暂且搁置夺取公国的图谋；事实上，这位归尔甫派的魁首索性知足常乐，只守着自己篡夺而来的布雷西亚（Brescia）与贝加莫（Bergamo）领主之位，安居贝加莫不曾轻动，直到约莫两年后法奇诺亲自找上门去。法奇诺之所以未曾早早兴师问罪，全因米兰尚有更为迫近、更为猖獗的心腹大患亟待他前去平定。维尼亚泰（Vignate）再度揭竿而起，埃斯托雷·维斯孔蒂（Estorre Visconti）及其侄子乔瓦尼·卡洛（Giovanni Carlo）亦起兵响应，更有大群大大小小的叛乱分子蜂拥作乱，而其中为首者竟是公爵的亲弟弟——帕维亚伯爵菲利波·玛丽亚·维斯孔蒂。当年马拉泰斯塔与布西科（Boucicault）把持米兰朝政之时，大批逃往帕维亚投奔他的吉伯林派人士百般阿谀吹捧，把菲利波·玛丽亚哄得真以为自己是该派在北意大利唯一的希望。野心既被撩拨起来，他便随时准备趁着四海鼎沸之际，将公爵的紫袍揽入自己怀中。法奇诺重返米兰之时，他正是怀着这般图谋加紧备战；而当法奇诺忙着平定米兰领地内各处叛乱、在德西奥（Desio）与戈尔贡佐拉（Gorgonzola）等地逐一扑灭反叛余烬之际，菲利波·玛丽亚整军备战的消息也传到了他耳中。直到肃清乱党、建立起妥善的政务秩序、使这片饱受摧残的土地重归安宁之后，法奇诺才掉转目光，去应对更远处的强敌威胁。而这头一个要收拾的，便是菲利波·玛丽亚。他挥师直扑帕维亚，强攻破城，继而纵兵洗劫全城——而且一年之中所有夜晚里，竟偏偏挑中了圣诞夜来干这桩勾当。

帕维亚那场浩劫，堪称人类洗劫城市这一惨烈史上最毫不留情、最骇人听闻的暴行之一；这一行径，也为这位将领的声名留下了永远的污点——尽管他平时行事粗犷、偶尔甚至失之残暴，骨子里却仍是一位抱持崇高原则、深怀责任感的统帅。

此后，他处置菲利波·玛丽亚的法子，便如法炮制了他先前对待那位公爵兄长的手段：他自任这位年轻亲王领地的总管，将朝中各要职悉数安插上自己信赖的心腹，彻底架空了这位伯爵的全部实权。

那位肥胖松弛的年轻亲王，竟以一种异乎寻常的麻木冷漠逆来顺受了。他生性孤僻好学，宛如隐士，且近乎病态地怯于见人，只因对自身怪诞丑陋的容貌过分敏感，平生最避讳与外人往来。

心中那点刚刚迸发出来的野心火花既被如此干脆利落地扑灭，他便重又退回到自己的书堆之中，任由法奇诺去摆布国政；只要法奇诺还留给他那点维持隐士般清静生活所真正必需的微薄用度，他便一声也不吭。

===Original===
Facino made now of Pavia his headquarters, coming to dwell in the great castle itself, and bringing thither from Alessandria his Countess. And with the Countess of Biandrate came also the Princess Valeria of Montferrat to rejoin at last her brother who had continued throughout in Facino’s train. The Princess had left Casale with the Countess when Carmagnola appeared there as Facino’s envoy with an escort. Her going had been in the nature of a flight, whose object had been first to rejoin her cherished brother, and second, to remove herself from the power of her uncle, which, in all the circumstances made clear by Carmagnola, seemed prudent. It is possible that she may also have hoped by her presence near Facino to stimulate him into the fulfilment of the threat against the Regent on which he had parted from him in Genoa.

But Facino had still more immediate matters to rectify before coming to the affair of the Lord Theodore. The Regent must wait his turn.

He moved against Canturio in the following May, and made short work of it. The campaign against Crema followed, and meanwhile Bellarion, with a condotta increased to fifteen hundred men and supported by Koenigshofen, had marched out of Milan to deal with the rebellious Bignate, whom in the end he finally and definitely defeated. That done he returned to Milan, where, ever since Facino’s descent upon Pavia, he had held the position of Facino’s deputy, and had earned respect and even affection by the equable wisdom of his rule.

All this in greater detail you will find set forth by Corio and Fra Serafino of Imola, and it is Fra Serafino who tells us that Facino, determined that Bellarion should not suffer by the loyalty which had made him refuse the County of Asti, had constrained Gian Maria to create him Count of Gavi, and the Commune of Milan to enlist the services of his condotta for two years at a stipend of thirty thousand ducats monthly.

===Chinese===
法奇诺就此将帕维亚定为自己的大本营，亲自迁入那座宏伟的城堡居住，并把伯爵夫人从亚历山德里亚接了过来。随同比安德拉泰伯爵夫人一同前来的，还有蒙费拉托的瓦莱里娅公主，她终于得以与始终留在法奇诺随行队伍中的弟弟团聚。当日卡尔马尼奥拉奉法奇诺之命率领护卫出使卡萨莱时，公主便已随同伯爵夫人一道动身离开。她此行无异于一场出逃，一则是为了与她珍爱无比的弟弟重逢，二则也是为了摆脱她叔父的控制——在卡尔马尼奥拉向她挑明全部局势之后，此举无疑显得尤为明智。此外，她或许还存着几分指望，盼着近在法奇诺身旁，能催促他兑现当日在热那亚与那位摄政王分道扬镳时立下的狠话。

然而，在找西奥多大人算账之前，法奇诺手头还有更火烧眉毛的要务亟待料理。那位摄政王，还得排队等着轮到自己。

次年五月，法奇诺进兵攻打坎图里奥（Canturio），三下五除二便将其攻克。随后便是征讨克雷马（Crema）之役；在此期间，贝拉里翁统领已扩充至一千五百人的雇佣兵团，在柯尼希斯霍芬的协助下领兵开出米兰，前去征剿屡叛不驯的维尼亚泰（原文作 Bignate），最终将其彻底击败。大功告成之后，他凯旋回到米兰——自打法奇诺南下突袭帕维亚以来，他便一直以法奇诺副手的身份留守治理米兰，凭借宽严相济、公允明智的施政赢得了全城敬重，乃至深受爱戴。

凡此种种的详尽始末，皆可见诸科里奥与伊莫拉（Imola）的塞拉菲诺修士之笔下；也正是塞拉菲诺修士告诉我们，法奇诺决意不让贝拉里翁因那份曾令他毅然辞却阿斯蒂伯爵领（County of Asti）的忠义而吃亏，遂迫使吉安·玛丽亚敕封他为加维伯爵（Count of Gavi），并令米兰公社（Commune of Milan）签下他这支雇佣兵团效力两年，月俸高达三万杜卡特金币。

## IV The Count of Pavia / 第四章 帕维亚伯爵

===Original===
In the vast park of Pavia the trees stood leafless and black against the white shroud of snow that covered the chilled earth. The river Ticino gurgled and swirled about the hundred granite pillars which carried the great roofed bridge, five hundred feet in length, spanning its grey and turgid waters. Beyond this, Pavia the Learned reared above white roofs her hundred snow-capped towers to the grey December sky, and beyond the city, isolated, within the girdle of a moat that was both wide and deep, stood the massive square castle, pink as coral, strong as iron, at once impregnable fortress and unrivalled palace, one of the great monuments of Viscontian power and splendour, described by Petrarch as the princeliest pile in Italy.

The pride of the place was the library, a spacious square chamber in one of the rectangular towers that rose at each of the four corners of the castle. The floor was of coloured mosaics, figuring birds and beasts, the ceiling of ultramarine star-flecked in gold, and along the walls was ranged a collection of some nine hundred manuscript parchment volumes bound in velvet and damask, or in gold and silver brocades. Their contents contained all that was known of theology, astrology, medicine, music, geometry, rhetoric, and the other sciences. This room was the favourite haunt of the lonely, morose, and studious boy, the great Gian Galeazzo’s younger son, Filippo Maria Visconti, Count of Pavia.

He sat there now, by the log fire that hissed and spluttered and flamed on the cavernous hearth, diffusing warmth and a fragrance of pine throughout the chamber. And with him at chess sat the Lord Bellarion Cane, Count of Gavi, one of the newfound friends who had invaded his loneliness, and broken through the savage shyness which solitude and friendlessness had set about him like a shell.

The others, the dark and handsome Countess of Biandrate, the fair and now almost ethereal Princess of Montferrat, and that sturdier counterpart of herself, her brother, were in the background by one of the two-light windows with trefoil arches springing from slender monials.

===Chinese===
在帕维亚（Pavia）广袤的林苑里，大地上覆盖着一层冷寂的白雪裹尸布，脱尽叶片的枯树黝黑如墨，映衬在其间。提契诺河（Ticino）灰浊湍急的河水咕嘟奔涌，绕着那上百根花岗岩石柱旋流而过——石柱之上，架着一座长达五百英尺的宏大有顶廊桥，横跨江面。过桥之后，便是“博学之城”帕维亚，积雪压顶的百座高塔越过皑皑屋顶，直指十二月灰蒙蒙的天空；再往城外去，便见一座巍峨的方形城堡孤悬于又宽又深的护城河环抱之中，城墙色如珊瑚粉，坚如百炼铁，既是固若金汤的要塞，又是举世无双的宫殿，乃是维斯孔蒂家族（Visconti）威权与荣华的赫赫丰碑之一，连彼特拉克（Petrarch）也曾赞其为“全意大利最为宏丽堂皇的王侯宫堡”。

整座城堡最引以为傲的所在，便是藏书室。它设在城堡四角耸立的四座矩形高塔之一中，是一间宽敞方正的厅堂。地面铺着彩色镶嵌画，绘满珍禽异兽；穹顶涂成群青底色，其间点缀着金色繁星；四壁排满约莫九百卷羊皮纸手抄典籍，或以天鹅绒与锦缎装帧，或以金银织锦包面。书中囊括了世间所知的神学、占星术、医学、音乐、几何、修辞及其他诸般学问。这间静室，正是孤独、阴郁又嗜读不倦的少年——伟人吉安·加莱阿佐（Gian Galeazzo）的幼子、帕维亚伯爵菲利波·玛丽亚·维斯孔蒂（Filippo Maria Visconti）——平日最爱流连的去处。

此刻他便坐在那里，守着那座洞窟般深阔的壁炉。炉中木柴嘶嘶作响，噼啪爆裂，腾起熊熊火舌，将融融暖意与松木清香散满全室。与他对弈国际象棋的，正是加维（Gavi）伯爵贝拉里翁·卡内（Bellarion Cane）大人——正是这位新近结识的友人，闯入了他孤寂的天地，打破了离群索居、形单影只为他筑起的那层野兽般怯生避人的硬壳。

其余几人——肤色微深却美艳动人的比安德拉泰（Biandrate）伯爵夫人、容颜清丽而近来愈发显得飘逸如仙的蒙费拉托（Montferrat）公主，以及生得与姐姐相貌酷似却更显敦实健朗的弟弟——正聚在后方一扇双联窗旁，纤细石柱上托起的三叶形拱券将冬光引入室中。

===Original===
The Princess was bending low over a frame, embroidering in red and gold and blue an altar-cloth for San Pietro in Ciel d’Oro. The Countess was yawning over a beautifully illuminated copy of Petrarch’s “Trionfo d’Amore”. The boy sat idle and listless between them, watching his sister’s white tapering fingers as they flashed to and fro.

Presently he rose, sauntered across to the players, drew up a stool, and sat down to watch the game over which they brooded silently.

A crutch lay beside Bellarion, and his right leg was thrust out stiff and unbending, to explain why he sat here on this day of late December playing chess, whilst the campaign against Malatesta continued to rage in the hills of Bergamo. He was suffering the penalty of the pioneer. Having already demonstrated to his contemporaries that infantry, when properly organised and manoeuvred, can hold its own in the field against cavalry, he had been turning his attention to artillery. Two months ago he had mounted a park of guns under the walls of Bergamo with the intention of breaching them. But at the outset of his operations a bombard had burst, killing two of his bombardiers and breaking his thigh, thus proving Facino’s contention that artillery was a danger only to those who employed it.

The physician Mombelli, who still continued in Facino’s train, had set the bone, whereafter Bellarion had been carefully packed into a mule litter, and by roads, which torrential rains had reduced to quagmires, he had been despatched to Pavia to get himself mended. His removal from the army was regretted by everybody with two exceptions: Carmagnola, glad to be relieved of a brother captain by comparison with whose military methods his own were constantly suffering in the general esteem; and Filippo Maria, when he discovered in Bellarion a chess-player who was not only his equal but his master, and who in other ways won the esteem of that very friendless boy. The Princess Valeria was dismayed that this man, who out of unconquerable prejudice she continued to scorn and mistrust, should become for a season her fellow inquiline. And it was in vain that Gian Giacomo, who in the course of his reformation had come to conceive a certain regard for Bellarion, sought to combat his sister’s deep-rooted prejudice.

===Chinese===
公主正低俯在绣绷上，用红、金、蓝三色丝线为圣彼得金天教堂（San Pietro in Ciel d’Oro）绣制祭坛帷布。伯爵夫人则百无聊赖地打着哈欠，漫不经心地翻着一卷彩绘精美的彼特拉克诗集《爱之凯旋》（*Trionfo d’Amore*）。少年坐在两人中间，百无聊赖、意兴阑珊，只顾看着姐姐那双白皙纤长的玉指在绣面上往来穿梭。

没过多久，他站起身，信步踱到棋桌旁，拉过一张凳子坐下，静静观起这盘双方正默然苦思的棋局。

贝拉里翁手边放着一根拐杖，右腿笔直伸出，僵硬得无法弯曲——这正是为何在十二月下旬的今日，征讨马拉泰斯塔（Malatesta）的战事仍在贝加莫（Bergamo）群山间如火如荼地进行，他却坐在此处下棋的缘故。他是在为自己的开拓之举吃苦头。此前，他已向世人证明，步兵只要编制得法、调度有方，在野战中便能与骑兵分庭抗礼；那之后，他又把心思转向了火炮。两个月前，他在贝加莫城墙下架起一排火炮，打算轰塌城垣。谁知炮击方才打响，一门射石炮便轰然炸膛，当场炸死了两名炮手，也震断了他的大腿骨——倒恰好印证了法奇诺（Facino）一贯的论调：火炮这玩意儿，只伤用炮之人。

一直随侍在法奇诺军中的御医蒙贝利（Mombelli）为他接好了断骨，随后人们小心翼翼地将贝拉里翁抬进一乘骡轿，沿着被瓢泼大雨冲成泥潭的道路，送往帕维亚休养疗伤。他这一离开大军，人人莫不扼腕惋惜，唯独两人例外：一个是卡尔马尼奥拉（Carmagnola），他巴不得少了个同袍将领——每次两人的用兵之道被人拿来一比，他在众人眼中的声望便要相形见绌；另一个便是菲利波·玛丽亚，因为他发觉贝拉里翁棋艺精湛，不仅与自己旗鼓相当，更胜过自己一筹，还在诸多方面赢得了这个孤僻少年由衷的敬重。至于瓦莱里娅（Valeria）公主，得知这个她怀着难以克制的成见而始终鄙夷防备的人竟要暂且与自己同栖一处，不禁大感懊恼。吉安·贾科莫（Gian Giacomo）自打痛改前非以来，渐渐对贝拉里翁生出几分敬意，可任凭他怎么劝说，终究撼不动姐姐心中那股根深蒂固的偏见。

===Original===
When he insisted that it was by Bellarion’s contriving that he had been removed from his uncle’s control, she had been moved to vehement scorn of his credulity.

“That is what the trickster would have us think. He no more than carried out the orders of the Count of Biandrate. His whole life bears witness to his false nature.”

“Nay, now, Valeria, nay. You’ll not deny that he is what all Italy now proclaims him: one of the greatest captains of his time.”

“And how has he made himself that? Is it by knightly qualities, by soldierly virtues? All the world knows that he prevails by guile and trickery.”

“You’ve been listening to Carmagnola,” said her brother. “He would give an eye for Bellarion’s skill.”

“You’re but a boy,” she reminded him with some asperity.

===Chinese===
每当他坚称自己能摆脱叔父的挟制全赖贝拉里翁暗中筹谋，她便对他这般轻信嗤之以鼻，言语间满是鄙夷。

“那正是这奸诈之徒想让我们信以为真的说辞。他不过是奉了比安德拉泰伯爵之命行事罢了。他一生的所作所为，足可证明他生性虚伪狡诈。”

“话不能这么说，瓦莱里娅，万万不可。全意大利如今都公认他是当今最伟大的统帅之一，这一点你总不能否认吧。”

“那他是怎么爬到这一步的？难道凭的是骑士风度、军人美德吗？天下人谁不知道，他赢靠的全是诡计和耍弄心机。”

“你准是听信了卡尔马尼奥拉的话，”她弟弟说道，“换作他，就算剜掉一只眼珠子，也恨不得换来贝拉里翁的本事。”

“你不过是个孩子罢了。”她语气颇带锋芒地提醒他。

===Original===
“And Carmagnola, of course, is a handsome man.”

She crimsoned at the sly tone. On odd visits to Pavia, Carmagnola had been very attentive to the Princess, employing all a peacock’s arts of self-display to dazzle her.

“He is an honest gentleman,” she countered hotly. “It is better to trust an upright, honest soldier than a sly schemer whose falsehood has been proven to us.”

“If he schemes my ruin for my uncle’s profit, he goes about it oddly, neglecting opportunities.”

She looked at him with compassion. “Bellarion never aims where he looks. It is the world says that of him, not I.”

===Chinese===
“而卡尔马尼奥拉嘛，自然是个英俊潇洒的美男子。”

听出他话里的狡黠调侃，她双颊登时飞红。卡尔马尼奥拉几次顺道来帕维亚时，对公主可谓殷勤备至，浑身解数使尽，犹如孔雀开屏般极力炫耀卖弄，想叫她眼花缭乱。

“他是个光明磊落的君子，”她激愤地反驳道，“与其相信一个早已在我们面前露出狡诈嘴脸的阴险谋士，倒不如信赖一位正直坦荡的军人。”

“倘若他真想替我叔父谋利、图谋毁我，那他行事也未免太古怪了些，竟放着大好机会不管不顾。”

她怜悯地望了弟弟一眼。“贝拉里翁眼睛望着哪儿，手上的剑却从不刺向哪儿。这话可不是我编的，天下人都这么说他。”

===Original===
“And at what do you suspect that he is aiming now?”

Her deep eyes grew thoughtful. “What if he serves our uncle to destroy us, only so that in the end he may destroy our uncle to his own advantage? What if he should aim at a throne?”

Gian Giacomo thought the notion fantastic, the fruit of too much ill-ordered brooding. He said so, laughing.

“If you had studied his methods, Giannino, you would not say that. See how he has wrought his own advancement. In four short years this son of nobody, without so much as a name of his own has become the Knight Bellarion, the Lord Bellarion of the Company of the White Dog, and now the Lord Count of Gavi holding the rich lands of Gavi in feud.”

===Chinese===
“那你怀疑他眼下究竟图谋什么？”

她幽深的双眸凝思起来。“倘若他眼下替咱们叔父效命来毁掉我们，到头来只是为了趁势再毁掉叔父、成全他自己呢？倘若他图谋的是一顶王冠呢？”

吉安·贾科莫觉得这想法简直荒诞不经，纯属胡思乱想、郁结过度所致，便笑着把这话说了出来。

“吉安尼诺（Giannino），你若是仔细琢磨过他的手段，就不会说这话了。瞧瞧他是怎样步步高升的吧。短短四年光景，这么个无名无姓、不知谁家所出的野小子，竟一路成了贝拉里翁骑士、白犬军团（Company of the White Dog）主帅贝拉里翁大人，如今更成了加维伯爵大人，坐拥富庶的加维封邑。”

===Original===
One there was who might have told her things which would have corrected her judgment, and that was Facino’s Countess. For the Lady Beatrice knew the truth of those events in Montferrat which were at the root of the Princess Valeria’s bitter prejudice, of which also she was aware.

“You hate him very bitterly,” the Countess told her once when Bellarion had been the subject of their talk.

“Would not you, if you were in my place?”

And the Countess, looking at her with those long indolent eyes of hers, an inscrutable smile on her red lips, had answered with languorous slowness: “In your place it is possible that I should.”

The tone and the smile had intrigued the Princess for many a day thereafter. But either she was too proud to ask what the Countess had meant, or else afraid.

===Chinese===
在场本有一人足可道出某些内情、纠正她的偏见，那便是法奇诺的伯爵夫人。因为蒙费拉托当年那场风波的真相，贝阿特丽切夫人（Lady Beatrice）原是心知肚明的，而瓦莱里娅公主刻骨成见的根源也正在于此——这一点，夫人同样一清二楚。

“你恨他恨得真切呢，”有一次两人谈起贝拉里翁时，伯爵夫人曾对她这样说道。

“换作您处在我的位置上，难道会不恨吗？”

伯爵夫人用她那双慵懒狭长的眼睛凝望着她，红唇边浮起一抹莫测高深的笑意，懒洋洋地慢声答道：“若我在你的位置上，说不定还真会恨呢。”

那番语调与那抹笑容，在此后许多天里一直令公主暗暗费解、悬念于心。然而她要么是自尊心太强，要么是心存畏怯，终究不曾开口追问伯爵夫人话中究竟何意。

===Original===
When after some eight weeks abed, Bellarion had begun to hobble about the castle, and it was impossible for the Princess entirely to avoid him, she was careful never to be alone where he might so surprise her, using him when they met in the company of others with a distant, frigid courtesy, which is perhaps the most piercing of all hostility.

If it wounded Bellarion, he gave no sign. He was﻿—and therein lay half the secret of his strength﻿—a very patient man. He was content to wait for the day when by his contriving the reckoning should be presented to the Marquis Theodore, and she should know at last whose servant he really was. Meanwhile, he modelled his demeanour upon her own. He did not seek her company, nor indeed that of any in the castle save Filippo Maria, with whom he would spend long hours at chess or instructing him out of his own deep learning supported by one or another of the treatises in that fine library.

Until the coming of Bellarion, the Count of Pavia had believed himself a strong chess-player. Bellarion had made him realise that his knowledge of the game was elementary. Where against former opponents he had swept to easy triumphs, he now groaned and puffed and sweated over the board to lessen the ignominy of his inevitable defeats.

Today, however, he was groaning less than usual. He had piled up a well-supported attack on Bellarion’s flank, and for the first time in weeks﻿—for these games had begun whilst Bellarion was still abed﻿—he saw victory ahead. With a broad smile he brought up a bishop further to strengthen the mass of his attack. He saw his way to give check in three and checkmate in four moves.

===Chinese===
在卧床休养了约莫八周之后，贝拉里翁终于能拄杖在城堡里蹒跚走动。公主虽已无法彻底避开他，却处处留心绝不独处，免得被他撞个正着；每逢众人在场避无可避时，她便待之以疏离冰冷的礼貌——世上种种敌意之中，或许正以这种最是刺骨伤人。

倘若这刺痛了贝拉里翁，他也未曾流露半分。他是个极有耐心的人——他一身本领的秘诀，半数正在于此。他甘愿静静等待那一天到来：待他一手布下的局瓜熟蒂落，向西奥多侯爵（Marquis Theodore）清算总账之时，她自会明白他究竟是谁的忠仆。在此期间，他只效法她的做派以礼相待，既不去讨她的欢心，也不亲近城堡里的旁人，唯独与菲利波·玛丽亚相伴，常常一坐便是好几个钟头，不是对弈象棋，便是取那座富丽藏书室里的各色典籍为佐证，以自己渊博的学识悉心点拨这位少年亲王。

在贝拉里翁到来之前，帕维亚伯爵一直自诩棋艺高强。贝拉里翁却让他明白，自己对棋道的领悟其实不过皮毛。以往对阵旁人时，他向来所向披靡、轻松取胜；如今俯首棋盘，却只得唉声叹气、喘着粗气满头大汗，只盼输得别太难堪。

然而今日，他的叹气声却比往常少得多。他在贝拉里翁的侧翼层层推进、布下了援兵雄厚的凌厉攻势；数周以来——自贝拉里翁尚未下床时两人便开始对弈了——他头一回在棋盘上望见了胜机。他嘴角咧开得意的笑容，提上一枚主教，进一步厚实进攻阵势。他已算清了棋路：三步将军，四步绝杀。

===Original===
Although only in his twentieth year, he was of a hog-like bulk. Of no more than middle height, he looked tall when seated, for all the length of him was in his flabby, paunchy body. His limbs were short and shapeless. His face was as round as the full moon and as pale. A great dewlap spread beneath his chin, and his neck behind hung in loose fat folds upon his collar, so that the back of his head, which was flat, seemed to slope inwards towards the crown. His short black hair was smooth and sleek as a velvet cap, and a fringe of it across his forehead descended almost to the heavy black eyebrows, thus masking the intellectual depth of the only noble feature of that ignoble countenance. Of his father all that he had inherited physically was the hooked, predatory nose. His mouth was coarsely shaped and its lines confirmed the impression of cruelty you gathered from the dark eyes which were small and lacklustre as a snake’s. And the impression was a true one, for the soul of this shy, morose young Prince was not without its share of that sadic cruelty which marked all the men of his race.

To meet the bishop’s move, Bellarion advanced a knight. The Prince’s laugh rang through the silent room. It was a shrill almost womanish laugh, and it was seldom heard. High-pitched, too, was the voice that followed.

“You but delay the inevitable, Bellarion,” he said, and took the knight.

But the move of the knight, which had appeared purely defensive to the Prince in his intentness upon his own attack, had served to uncover the file of Bellarion’s queen. Supports had been previously and just as cunningly provided. Bellarion advanced his hand, a long beautiful hand upon which glowed a great carved sapphire set in brilliants﻿—the blue and white that were his colours. Forth flashed his queen across the board.

“Checkmate, Lord Prince,” said Bellarion quietly, and sank back smiling into the brocaded chair.

===Chinese===
他虽年仅十九、未及弱冠，身形却已肥硕臃肿如豕。他身高不过中等，落座时却显得颇为高大，只因他浑身的长度全长在那具松垮挺凸的肥硕躯干上。他的四肢短粗无形；一张脸圆得像满月，又一样苍白无血色；下巴底下垂着一大块肥肉赘袋，后颈上的肥褶一层层松垮垮地压在衣领上，使得那扁平的后脑勺仿佛斜斜往头顶收进去一般。一头乌黑短发服帖油亮，宛如一顶天鹅绒小帽，额前齐齐垂下一道刘海，几乎遮到浓重的黑眉，将这张俗鄙面孔上唯一称得上高贵特征的深邃饱满天庭掩了大半。生父相貌中唯一遗传给他的，便是那只如猛禽般尖钩的鹰鼻。他嘴唇轮廓粗笨，唇角线条更坐实了那双如蛇目般细小无光的黑眼睛所透出的残忍印象。而这印象绝非虚妄：在这位怯懦阴沉的少年亲王灵魂深处，确也流淌着维斯孔蒂一族男子共有的那股嗜虐残酷的血性。

面对主教进逼，贝拉里翁只推上一枚骑士。亲王的笑声骤然在静谧的房间里响起。那是一种尖细得近乎女气的笑声，平日里极少听闻；紧随其后响起的嗓音，同样尖锐刺耳。

“你不过是在拖延避无可避的败局罢了，贝拉里翁。”他一边说着，一边吃掉了那枚骑士。

殊不知亲王一心扑在自己的攻势上，以为那枚骑士走得纯粹是为防守，却未曾察觉这一步恰恰让贝拉里翁皇后的纵线豁然敞开。后援子力也早已同样刁钻地埋伏妥当。贝拉里翁探出他那双修长俊美的手——指上那枚镶嵌在一圈碎钻中的硕大雕花蓝宝石正熠熠生辉，蓝白两色正是他的徽色——执起皇后，寒光一闪般直贯棋盘。

“将死了，亲王殿下。”贝拉里翁平静地说完，含笑仰靠回锦缎座椅里。

===Original===
Filippo Maria stared unbelieving at the board. The lines of his mouth drooped, and his great pendulous cheeks trembled. Almost he seemed on the point of tears.

“God rot you, Bellarion! Always, always is it the same! I plan and build and whilst you seem to do no more than defend, you are preparing a death-stroke in an unexpected quarter.” Between jest and earnest he added: “You slippery rogue! Always you defeat me by a trick.”

The Princess Valeria looked up from her embroidery on the word. Bellarion caught the movement and the glance in his direction. He knew the thought behind, and it was that thought he answered.

“In the field, my opponents use the same word to decry me. But those who are with me applaud my skill.” He laughed. “Truth is an elusive thing, highness, as Pontius Pilate knew. The aspect of a fact depends upon the angle from which you view it.”

Filippo Maria sat back, his great chin sunk to his breast, his podgy white hands gripping the arms of his chair, his humour sullen.

“I’ll play no more today,” he said.

===Chinese===
菲利波·玛丽亚难以置信地死死盯着棋盘。他的嘴角一下子耷拉下来，两腮肥垂的肉也跟着微微发颤，简直像是下一刻就要掉出眼泪。

“老天烂了你的心肺，贝拉里翁！次次都是这样，次次如此！我辛辛苦苦谋篇布局，你表面上只顾着招架退守，暗地里却偏从叫人意想不到的角落递出绝杀一击！”他又半真半假地加了一句，“你个滑头鬼！每回赢我都靠耍诡计！”

听见这词儿，瓦莱里娅公主从绣活上抬起头来。贝拉里翁捕捉到了她的动作与投向自己的目光，心中明镜似的知晓她心里转着什么念头，于是答的正是她那番心思。

“在战场上，我的敌手也爱拿这个词来贬损我。可与我并肩作战的人，倒都赞我用兵如神。”他轻笑了一声，“殿下，真理原是捉摸不定的东西，本丢·彼拉多（Pontius Pilate）早就明白这个道理。一桩事实究竟是什么模样，全看您从哪个角度去瞧它。”

菲利波·玛丽亚向后仰坐回去，肥硕的下巴抵进胸口，一双白胖的小手紧紧攥住椅背扶手，神情阴郁沉闷。

“今天不下了。”他说。

===Original===
The Countess rose and crossed the room with a rustle of stiff brocade of black and gold.

“Let me remove the board,” she said. “A vile, dull game. I wonder that you can waste such hours upon it.”

Filippo Maria raised his beady eyes. They kindled as they observed her, raking her generous yet supple lines from head to foot. It was not the first time that the watchful Bellarion had seen him look so at Facino’s lady, nor the first time that he had seen her wantonly display herself to provoke that unmistakable regard. She bent now to the board, and Filippo’s smouldering glance was upon the warm ivory beauty of her neck, and the swell of her breast revealed by the low-cut gown.

“It is human to despise what we do not understand,” Bellarion was answering her.

“You would defend the game, of course, since you excel in it. That is what you love, Bellarion; to excel; to wield mastery.”

“Do we not all? Do not you, yourself, madonna, glory in the power your beauty gives you?”

===Chinese===
伯爵夫人站起身，身上那袭黑底织金的硬挺锦袍飒飒作响，踱步穿过房间。

“让我把棋盘收了吧，”她说道，“真是乏味透顶的蠢玩意儿。真难为你们竟能在这上头耗上好几个钟头。”

菲利波·玛丽亚抬起他那双绿豆似的小眼睛。目光落在她身上时，眼底骤然亮起火光，从头到脚细细扫视着她那丰腴却又柔韧婀娜的身段。眼观六路的贝拉里翁，早已不是头一回见他这般垂涎地盯着法奇诺的夫人，也不是头一回见这位夫人卖弄风情、故意招惹那道再明白不过的目光了。此刻她俯身去端棋盘，菲利波炽热阴燃的视线便直勾勾盯在了她温润如象牙般的雪白颈项，以及低领长裙下微露的丰盈酥胸上。

“人对于自己不解其妙的事物，向来免不了轻慢几分。”贝拉里翁正在回答她。

“您当然要替这游戏辩护了，谁叫您精于此道呢。您爱的正是这个，贝拉里翁——事事压人一头，处处凌驾掌控。”

“难道世人不都如此吗？夫人，就连您自己，不也正为美貌赐予您的权势而得意自豪么？”

===Original===
She looked at Filippo. Her heavy eyelids drooped. “Behold him turned courtier, my lord. He perceives beauty in me.”

“He would be blind else,” said the fat youth, greatly daring. And the next moment in a reaction of shyness a mottled flush was staining his unhealthy pallor.

Lower drooped the lady’s eyelids, until a line of black lashes lay upon her cheek.

“The game,” Gian Giacomo interposed, “is a very proper one for princes. Messer Bellarion told me so.”

===Chinese===
她转向菲利波，沉甸甸的眼帘微微一垂。“殿下您瞧，他也学起宫廷弄臣的嘴脸来了。他竟瞧出我美貌来了。”

“若不然，他便是个瞎子了。”肥硕少年鼓足莫大勇气说道。可话刚出口，怯懦的本性立时反扑回来，他那病态苍白的脸上登时涌起一片斑驳潮红。

伯爵夫人的眼帘垂得更低了，直到一排乌黑的长睫毛宛如羽扇般轻轻覆在脸颊上。

“这棋局，”吉安·贾科莫插口道，“极合乎王侯君主来下。贝拉里翁先生亲口对我这么说的。”

===Original===
“He means, child,” Filippo answered him, “that it teaches them a bitter moral: that whilst a State depends upon the Prince﻿—the Prince himself is entirely dependent upon others, being capable in his own person of little more than his meanest pawn.”

“To teach that lesson to a despot,” said Bellarion, “was the game invented by an Eastern philosopher.”

“And the most potent piece upon the board, as in the State, is the queen, symbolising woman.” Thus Filippo Maria, his eyes full upon the Countess again.

Bellarion laughed. “Aye! He knew his world, that ancient Oriental!”

===Chinese===
“孩子，他的意思是，”菲利波接过话头，“这棋教会君王一桩苦涩的道理：一国之安危虽系于君主一身，可君主本人却完全仰仗他人之力，单凭一己之身，能耐并不比棋盘上最微贱的小卒高出多少。”

“昔日那位东方哲人创制此棋，”贝拉里翁接道，“正是为了给专制暴君上一堂这样的课。”

“而棋盘上威力最大的棋子，一如邦国之中，乃是象征着女人的皇后。”菲利波·玛丽亚如此说着，一双眼睛又牢牢盯在了伯爵夫人身上。

贝拉里翁朗声一笑。“可不是！那位东方古哲真是洞悉世情啊！”

===Original===
But he did not laugh as the days passed, and he observed the growing lechery in the beady eyes with which the Count of Pavia watched the Lady Beatrice’s every movement, and the Lady Beatrice’s provocative complacency under that vigilance.

One day, at last, coming upon the Countess alone in that library, Bellarion unmasked the batteries he had been preparing.

He hobbled across to the arched window by which she was seated, and leaning against its monial, looked out upon the desolate park. The snows had gone, washed away by rains, and since these had come a frost under which the ground lay now as grey and hard as iron.

“They will be feeling the rigours of the winter in the camp under Bergamo,” he said, moving, as ever, obliquely to the attack.

===Chinese===
然而随着日子一天天过去，他却再也笑不出来了。他分明瞧见帕维亚伯爵那双小眼睛里日渐滋长的淫邪欲火，紧盯着贝阿特丽切夫人的一举一动；更瞧见贝阿特丽切夫人在这般虎视眈眈之下，竟显出一副欲拒还迎、沾沾自喜的挑逗神态。

终于有一天，贝拉里翁撞见伯爵夫人独自一人待在藏书室里，于是果断亮出了自己暗中蓄势已久的火炮。

他一瘸一拐地走到她所坐的拱窗边，靠着石窗棂，望向窗外荒凉萧瑟的林苑。积雪早已被连日阴雨冲刷殆尽，雨后又降下严霜，整片大地如今冻得灰沉坚硬，犹如生铁。

“贝加莫城下的大营里，将士们眼下怕是正饱尝隆冬严寒之苦呢。”他开口说道，一如既往地采取迂回侧击的战术。

===Original===
“They will so. Facino should have gone into winter quarters.”

“That would mean recommencing in the spring a job that is half done already.”

“Yet with his gout and the infirmities of age, it might prove wiser in the end.”

“Each age has its own penalties, madonna. It is not only the elderly among humanity who need compassion.”

“Wisdom oozes from you like sweat from another.” There was a tartness in her accents. “If I were your biographer, Bellarion, I should write of you as the soldier-sage, or the philosopher-at-arms.”

===Chinese===
“那是自然。法奇诺原该按兵收拢去过冬营才是。”

“那样一来，眼看已近半成的功业，明年开春岂不是又要从头再来？”

“可他毕竟身患痛风，年迈体衰，真要算起长远账来，退入冬营倒未必不明智。”

“人生在世，哪个年纪没有各自的苦楚呢，夫人。世上需要怜悯的，绝不止垂垂老矣之人。”

“您身上真是满嘴渗出圣贤大道理，跟旁人满身冒汗似的。”她话音里带了几分酸涩尖刻，“贝拉里翁，若由我来为您立传，定要称您一声‘戎装圣哲’，或是‘披甲哲人’。”

===Original===
Propped on his crutch and his one sound leg, Bellarion considered her, his head on one side, and fetched a sigh.

“You are very beautiful, madonna.”

She was startled. “God save us!” she cried. “Does the soldier-sage contain a mere man, after all?”

“Your mouth, madonna, is too sweetly formed for acids.”

“The choicest fruits, sir, have an alloy of sharpness. What else about me finds favour in your eyes?”

“In my eyes! My eyes, madonna, are circumspect. They do not prowl hungrily over another’s pastures.”

===Chinese===
贝拉里翁拄着拐杖、单凭那条好腿支撑着身子，歪着头端详了她片刻，轻轻叹了口气。

“您生得真是极美，夫人。”

她微微一惊。“老天爷保佑！”她叫道，“敢情这位戎装圣哲骨子里，到底也还是个凡夫俗子？”

“夫人，您的樱唇生得如此娇美动人，实在不该吐出酸刻言语。”

“阁下，顶上乘的佳果里往往也掺着几分酸脆滋味呢。我身上还有哪处入了您的法眼？”

“入我的眼！夫人，我这双眼睛素来谨守本分，从不馋涎欲滴地去窥伺旁人的田园。”

===Original===
She looked at him between anger and apprehension, and slowly a wave of scarlet came to stain her face and bosom, to tell him that she understood. He lowered himself carefully to a chair, thrusting out his damaged leg, to the knee-joint of which articulation was only just beginning to return.

“I was saying, madonna, that they will be feeling the rigours of the winter in the camp under Bergamo. There was a hard frost last night, and after the frost there will be rains under which the hills thereabouts will melt in mud.” He sighed again. “You would regret, madonna, to exchange for that the ease and comfort of Pavia.”

“You have the fever again. I am not thinking of making that exchange.”

“No. I am thinking of it for you.”

“You! Saint Mary! And do you dispose of me?”

“It will be cold up there, madonna. But you need cooling. Coolness restores judgment. It will bring you back to a sense of duty to your lord.”

===Chinese===
她望向他的眼神里交织着怒意与惶惑，一抹绯红缓缓爬上她的脸颊与酥胸——这已足够告诉他，她听懂了他的弦外之音。他小心翼翼地矮身坐进一张椅子里，伸直那条伤腿——直到近来，他这膝关节才刚恢复些许屈伸。

“我方才正说到，夫人，贝加莫城下的军营里眼下正饱受严冬之苦。昨夜下了好一场重霜，霜后便是阴雨，到时那一带的山岭都要化作一片泥泞。”他又叹了口气，“夫人，若是舍了帕维亚的安逸舒适去受那份罪，您定会懊悔不已吧。”

“您怕是又烧糊涂了。我可没想过要去做这般交换。”

“不错，是我替您想着呢。”

“您！圣母玛利亚呀！我的去留几时轮到您来发落了？”

“山那头确实天寒地冻，夫人。可您眼下正需要凉快凉快。心凉了，神智才会清醒。这寒气能教您重新想起自己对夫君主君应尽的本分。”

===Original===
She came to her feet beside him, quivering with anger. Almost he thought her intention was to strike him.

“Have you come here to spy upon me?”

“Of course. Now you know why I broke my leg.”

She looked unutterable scorn. “The Princess Valeria is right in her opinion of you, in her disdain of you.”

His eyes grew sad. “If you were generous, madonna﻿—nay, if you were merely honest﻿—you would not embrace her opinions; you would correct them; for you have the knowledge that would suffice to do so. But you are not honest. If you were, there would be no need for me to speak now in defence of the honour of your absent lord.”

===Chinese===
她猛地在他身旁站起身，气得浑身直抖。他几乎以为她真要抬手扇自己一耳光。

“您跑到这儿来，就是为了暗中监视我？”

“当然了。现在您总算明白我干嘛要摔断一条腿了吧。”

她脸上露出难以言喻的鄙夷。“瓦莱里娅公主对您的看法、对您的轻蔑，真是一点儿不错。”

他的眼神黯淡下来，透出几分悲凉。“夫人，您哪怕有一分厚道——不，哪怕仅仅有一分诚实——就不会附和她的偏见，而会替我澄清是非，因为您明知内情，足可还我清白。可您并不诚实。您若诚实，今日我又何必在此开口，为您那位远在阵前的夫君捍卫清誉呢？”

===Original===
“Is it for you to say I am not honest?” There was now more of sorrow than indignation in her voice, and tears were gathering in her eyes, to deepen their sapphire hue. “God knows I have been honest with you, Bellarion. It is this very honesty you abuse in your present misjudgment of me. Oh! Me miserable!” It was the cry of a wounded soul. She sank down again into her chair. Self-pity welled in her to drown all else. “I am to be starved of everything. If ever woman was pitiable, I am that woman; and you, Bellarion, you of all living men that know my heart, can find for me only cruelty and reproach!”

It moved him not at all. The plea was too inconsequent and illogical, and the display of a lack of reason repelled him like a physical defect.

“Your plaint, madonna, is that Facino will not make you a duchess. He may do so yet if you are patient.”

Her tears had suddenly ceased.

“You know something!” she exclaimed in a hushed voice.

===Chinese===
“几时轮到您来指责我不诚实了？”她嗓音里的怒意此刻已化作满腔委屈，泪水涌上眼眶，将那双蓝宝石般的眸子映得愈发深湛，“天主明鉴，贝拉里翁，我对您可曾有过半句虚言？恰恰是我这份坦诚，反倒让您趁机拿来这般冤枉我、曲解我。天哪！我真是命苦！”那声哀叹宛如一颗受创灵魂发出的悲鸣。她重新跌坐回椅中，一腔自怜汹涌泛滥，淹没了其余一切。“我命中注定什么都得不到，只能活活渴死。普天之下若有哪个女子最堪怜悯，那便是我；而您，贝拉里翁，这世上最知我心事的人，偏偏只肯给我冷酷与苛责！”

这番哭诉丝毫未能打动他。她的申辩太过颠三倒四、毫无逻辑，而这种全无理性的做派令他厌恶，简直像见了肢体残缺一般。

“夫人，您所怨所叹的，无非是法奇诺迟迟未曾让您当上公爵夫人。您若肯沉住气耐心等待，他日后未必不能成全您。”

她的眼泪骤然止住了。

“您莫非知道什么内情！”她压低嗓音急呼道。

===Original===
The rogue fooled her with that illusion, whilst refraining from using words which might afterwards be turned against him.

“I know that you will lose the chance if meanwhile you should cease to be Facino’s wife. If you were so mad as to become the leman of another, you know as well as I do that the Lord Facino would put you from him. What should you be then? That is why I am your friend when I think of the camp at Bergamo for you.”

Slowly she dried her eyes. Carefully she removed all stains of tears. It consumed a little time. Then she rose and went to him, and took his hand.

“Thank you, Bellarion, my friend.” Her voice was hushed and tender. “You need have no fear for me.” She paused a moment. “What﻿ ﻿… what has my lord said to you of his intent?”

“Nay, nay,” he laughed, “I betray no confidences.” The trickster’s tone was a confidence in itself. He swept on. “You bid me have no fear for you. But that is not enough. Princes are reckless folk. I’d not have you remain in jeopardy.”

===Chinese===
这狡猾的家伙便拿这般幻象将她哄住了，嘴上却滴水不漏，绝不落下半句日后可能反被拿来作把柄的话头。

“我知道的是，倘若在此期间您不再是法奇诺的妻子，您便会彻底断送这桩机缘。您若是糊涂到去做了旁人的外室情妇，您自己心里再明白不过，法奇诺大人定会将您一脚休弃。到那时，您又算得了什么？正因如此，我替您盘算着去贝加莫大营，才是真正为您着想的朋友之举。”

她缓缓拭干眼角，仔仔细细地将脸上泪痕抹净，着实费了些工夫。随后她起身走到他面前，执起他的手。

“谢谢您，贝拉里翁，我的好朋友。”她的声音轻柔而温存，“您大可不必为我担心。”她略微一顿，“我家主君……他曾向您透露过什么打算么？”

“使不得，使不得，”他笑道，“我可不能泄露他人私下托付的密语。”这骗子说话的腔调本身就活脱脱像是在泄露机密了。他顺势往下说道：“您叫我不必为您担心。可光有这句话还不够。王公贵族都是些肆意妄为的主儿，我绝不能眼睁睁看您留在险境之中。”

===Original===
“Oh! But Bergamo!” she cried out. “To be encamped in winter!”

“You need not go so far, nor under canvas. In your place, madonna, I should retire to Melegnano. The castle is at your disposal. It is pleasanter than Pavia.”

“Pleasanter! In that loneliness?”

“It is the company here that makes it prudent. And you may take the Princess Valeria and her brother with you. Come, come, madonna. Will you trifle with fate at such a time? Will you jeopardise a glorious destiny for the sake of an obese young lordling?”

===Chinese===
“天哪！可去贝加莫！”她惊呼起来，“大冬天住在野地帐篷里！”

“您用不着去那么远，也不必住帐篷。夫人，若我处您的位置，便动身退居梅莱尼亚诺（Melegnano）。那里的城堡任您调遣居住，比帕维亚还要惬意得多。”

“惬意！在那等荒僻寂寞的所在？”

“正因这里的人太危险，避开才算稳妥。您还可以请瓦莱里娅公主和她弟弟一同前去作伴。行了，行了，夫人，值此紧要关头，您难道真要拿自己的命运当儿戏？难道真要为了这么个肥头大耳的年轻小公爷，断送一桩锦绣辉煌的前程？”

===Original===
She considered, her face fretful. “Tell me,” she begged again, “what my lord has divulged to you of his intentions?”

“Have I not said enough already?”

The entrance of Filippo Maria at that moment saved him the need of further invention. It perturbed him not at all that the Prince’s round white face should darken at the sight of them so close and fond. She was warned. Her greed of power and honour would curb her wantonness and ensure her withdrawal to Melegnano as he urged. Bellarion glowed with the satisfaction of a battle won, nor troubled about the deceit he had practised.

===Chinese===
她蹙眉思忖着，脸上满是焦灼。“告诉我吧，”她再度央求道，“我夫君究竟向您吐露了些什么心思？”

“难道我说得还不够明白么？”

恰在此时，菲利波·玛丽亚推门而入，省得他再费唇舌编造下去。见两人靠得如此之近、举止如此亲昵，亲王那张白胖圆脸登时沉了下来，贝拉里翁却毫不挂怀。他已经向她敲响了警钟。她对权势与尊荣的贪欲自会勒住她那颗轻狂放纵的心，驱使她按他的敦促退往梅莱尼亚诺。贝拉里翁心中涌起一股打赢一场胜仗般的惬意畅快，至于方才那番瞒天过海的欺哄，他压根儿不曾放在心上。

## V Justice / 第五章 正义

===Original===
The Epiphany mummeries were long overpast, the iron hand of winter was withdrawn from the land, and in the great forest of Pavia, where Gian Galeazzo had loved to hunt, the trees were breaking into bud before Bellarion’s condition permitted him to think of quitting the ease of Filippo Maria’s castle. His leg had mended well, the knee-joint had recovered its suppleness, and only a slight limp remained.

He spoke of returning to Bergamo. “This lotus-eating has endured too long already,” he told the Prince in answer to the latter’s remonstrances; for Filippo Maria was reluctant to part with one who in many ways had beguiled for him the tedium of his lonely life, rendered lonelier than ever before by the withdrawal of the Countess of Biandrate, who had gone with the Montferrine Princess to Melegnano.

But it was not written that Filippo Maria should be left alone; for on the very eve of Bellarion’s intended departure, Facino himself was borne into the Castle of Pavia, crippled by an attack of gout of a severity which had compelled him to leave his camp just as he was preparing to reap the fruits of his long and patient siege.

He had lost weight, and his face out of which the healthy tan had departed was grey and drawn. His hair from fulvid that it had been was almost white. But the spirit within remained unchanged, indomitable, and intolerant of this enforced inertia of the flesh.

===Chinese===
主显节（Epiphany）的化装嬉戏早已散场，严冬的铁腕已从大地上悄然松开；在吉安·加莱阿佐生前最爱纵马驰骋的帕维亚大森林里，林木也已抽枝吐芽，直到这时，贝拉里翁的伤势才总算好转，让他得以考虑离开菲利波·玛丽亚城堡中那方安逸的栖身之地。他的伤腿愈合得颇为妥帖，膝关节恢复了柔韧灵活，只余下一点微跛。

他提起了返回贝加莫（Bergamo）的打算。面对菲利波·玛丽亚亲王的再三挽留，他说道：“这般沉醉安逸、流连忘返的日子，已经过得够久了。”亲王实在舍不得他离去——在他孤寂寥落的生活里，贝拉里翁不知用多少法子替他排遣了无尽烦闷；何况自从比安德拉泰伯爵夫人陪着蒙费拉托公主迁往梅莱尼亚诺（Melegnano）后，这孤寂便愈发深重了。

然而天意似乎不愿让菲利波·玛丽亚落得形单影只；就在贝拉里翁动身的前夕，法奇诺本人竟被人抬进了帕维亚城堡。他遭逢了一场凶猛剧烈的痛风发作，痛得动弹不得，眼看漫长而耐心的围城战正要收获硕果，却硬生生被迫离开了军营。

他清减了许多，昔日那张健康黝黑的脸庞已然失去血色，变得灰败而憔悴；原本黄褐色的头发也几乎全白了。可他骨子里的精气神儿却丝毫未变，依旧百折不挠，绝不容忍这副皮囊被迫陷入半分懈怠。

===Original===
He was put to bed immediately on his arrival, for he was in great pain and swore that the gout, which he called by all manner of evil names, had got into his stomach.

“Mombelli warned me there was danger of it.”

“Where is Mombelli?” Bellarion asked. He stood with Filippo Maria by the canopied bed in a spacious chamber in the northern tower, adjacent to the Hall of Mirrors.

“Mombelli, devil take his soul, left me a month ago, when I seemed well, to go to Duke Gian Maria who desired to appoint him his physician. I’ve sent for him again to the Duke. Meanwhile some Pavese doctor will be required to give me ease.” He groaned with pain. Then, recovering, rapped out his orders to Bellarion. “It’s a mercy you are recovered, for you are needed at Bergamo. Meanwhile Carmagnola commands there, but he has my orders to surrender his authority to you on your arrival.”

It was an order which Carmagnola did not relish, as he plainly showed when Bellarion reached the camp two days later. But he dared not disobey it.

Bellarion examined the dispositions, but changed nothing. He carried forward the plans already made by Facino. The siege could be tightened no further, and, considering the straits to which Malatesta must be reduced, there could be little point in wasting lives on an assault.

===Chinese===
他一到城堡便被扶上床榻，此刻正痛得死去活来，嘴里将那痛风用尽各种恶毒脏话咒骂了一通，咬定这病邪已经攻进了肠胃里。

“蒙贝利（Mombelli）早警告过我，说有这等凶险。”

“蒙贝利在哪儿？”贝拉里翁问道。他正与菲利波·玛丽亚一同站在北塔楼一间宽敞的寝室里，紧挨着镜厅（Hall of Mirrors），守在法奇诺的华盖大床边。

“蒙贝利这厮，魔鬼收了他的魂去吧！一个月前我瞧着还硬朗，他就离开我去投吉安·玛丽亚公爵了，说是公爵有意委任他当御医。我已经派人去公爵那儿催他回来了。眼下先找个帕维亚的郎中来，替我止止痛吧。”他痛苦地呻吟了一声，随即定神缓过劲来，干脆利落地向贝拉里翁下令：“万幸你伤愈了，贝加莫那头正少不了你。眼下暂由卡尔马尼奥拉统领军务，不过我已经传令下去，你一到营中，他便须将帅印交托于你。”

这道将令显然极不合卡尔马尼奥拉的心意，两天后贝拉里翁抵达军营时，他把这份不满明明白白写在了脸上；只是他到底不敢抗命。

贝拉里翁细细察看了各处布防，一处也未改动，只是循着法奇诺既定的方略稳步推进。这座围城已然铁桶般严丝合缝，再无收紧的余地；况且算算马拉泰斯塔必定已陷入山穷水尽之境，强攻城池白白折损士卒性命，实在毫无意义。

===Original===
A week after Bellarion’s coming there rode into the great camp of green tents under the walls of Bergamo, a weary, excited fellow all splashed with mud from the fury of his riding.

Brought, by the guards who had checked his progress, to Facino’s large and handsomely equipped pavilion, pitched beside the racing waters of the Serio, this slight, swarthy, fierce-eyed man proved to be that stormy petrel, Giovanni Pusterla of Venegono.

Bellarion rose from the couch, covered by a black bearskin on which he had been reclining, and closed the beautifully illuminated copy of Juvenal’s *Satires*, which had been a parting gift from Filippo Maria. His gesture dismissed the Swiss halberdiers, who had ushered in this visitor. The very name of Venegono was of ill omen, and ill-omened was the man’s haggard countenance now, and his own announcement.

“I bring evil tidings, Lord Count.”

“You are consistent,” said Bellarion. “A great quality.”

===Chinese===
贝拉里翁到任一周之后，贝加莫城墙下那片连绵的绿色大营里，驰入了一名策马狂奔而来、浑身溅满泥浆的来客；他神情既倦怠又亢奋。

巡哨卫兵将他拦下，押送至法奇诺那座陈设讲究、宽大华丽的中军大帐——大帐就扎在奔腾湍急的塞里奥河（Serio）畔。近前一看，这名身形瘦削、肤色黝黑、眼神凶悍的汉子，竟是那个向来如同暴风海燕般哪儿有祸乱便往哪儿钻的煞星——韦内戈诺（Venegono）的乔瓦尼·普斯泰尔拉（Giovanni Pusterla）。

贝拉里翁原本斜倚在铺着黑熊皮的躺榻上，此时起身合上了手中那部装帧彩绘精美绝伦的尤维纳利斯《讽刺诗集》（Juvenal’s *Satires*）——那是菲利波·玛丽亚赠予他的临别礼物。他挥手屏退了领人进来的瑞士戟兵。单是“韦内戈诺”这个名号便透着不祥，更何况此刻这人一张憔悴枯槁的脸，以及他一开口便道出的来意，无一不透着凶兆。

“伯爵大人，我带来了坏消息。”

“你倒是一贯如此，”贝拉里翁说道，“这可真是个难得的品格。”

===Original===
Venegono stared at him. “Give me to drink,” he begged. “God! How I thirst. I have ridden from Pavia without pause save to change horse at Caravaggio.”

“From Pavia!” Bellarion’s tone and manner changed; apprehension showed in both. But not on that account was he neglectful of the needs of his guest. On an ample square table in mid-tent stood a jug of wine and some beautiful drinking-cups, their bowls of beaten gold, their stems of choicely wrought silver, beside a dish of sweetmeats, bread, and a small loaf of cheese. Bellarion poured a cup of strong red Valtelline. Venegono drained it.

“Aye, I am consistent, as you say. And so is that hellspawn Gian Maria Visconti. Of his consistency, mine. By your leave.”

He flung himself wearily into the cushioned faldstool by the table, and set down his cup. Bellarion nodded, and resumed his seat on the bearskin.

“What has happened in Pavia?”

“In Pavia nothing. Nothing yet. I rode there to warn Facino of what is happening in Milan, but Facino﻿ ﻿… The man is ill. He could do nothing if he would, so I come on to you.” And now, leaning forward, and scarcely pausing to draw breath, he launched the news he had ridden so desperately to bring. “Della Torre is back in Milan, recalled by Gian Maria.”

===Chinese===
韦内戈诺直勾勾地盯着他。“给我口水喝吧，”他央求道，“天主啊！我渴得快冒烟了。我从帕维亚一路飞马赶来，除了在卡拉瓦乔（Caravaggio）换了趟马，半刻也不曾歇过。”

“从帕维亚来的！”贝拉里翁的语气和神色骤然一变，字里行间顿时流露出几分忧虑。不过他并未因此疏忽了待客之道。大帐正中的宽大方桌上摆着一壶美酒和几只精致酒杯——杯盏由锤锻纯金打就，杯柄则是精雕细琢的纯银——一旁还放着一盘蜜饯果脯、面包和一小块乳酪。贝拉里翁斟了满满一杯浓烈的瓦尔泰利纳红酒（Valtelline），韦内戈诺接过一饮而尽。

“不错，正如你所说，我一贯如此。吉安·玛丽亚·维斯孔蒂那地狱孽种也同样一贯如此。正因他本性难改，我才改不了这副样子。恕我失礼了。”

他疲惫不堪地一屁股跌进桌旁的软垫折叠椅里，放下酒杯。贝拉里翁点了点头，回到黑熊皮躺榻上落座。

“帕维亚出什么事了？”

“帕维亚倒还没事，眼下还没。我原本骑马赶去那儿，是要向法奇诺报信，告诉他米兰正在生出什么变故，可法奇诺他……他人病倒了。有心也无力，所以我才一路赶来找你。”说着，他身子前倾，连口气也顾不上喘匀，便一股脑儿抛出了他拼死飞驰而来的急报，“德拉托雷回米兰了，是吉安·玛丽亚召他回去的。”

===Original===
Bellarion waited, but nothing further came.

“Well, man?” he asked. “Is that all?”

“All? Does it mean so little to you that you ask that? Don’t you know that this damned Guelph, whom Facino banished when he should have hanged him, has been throughout the inspirer of all the evil that has been wrought against Facino and against all the Ghibellines of Milan? Don’t you understand that his return bodes ill?”

“What can he do? What can Gian Maria do? Their wings are clipped.”

“They are growing fresh ones.” Venegono came to his feet again, his weariness forgotten in his excitement. “Since della Torre’s secret return a month ago, orators have been sent to Theodore of Montferrat, to the battered Vignati, to the Esti, and even to Estorre Visconti, to invite them into a league.”

Bellarion laughed. “Let them league. If they are so mad as to do so, Facino will smash their league into shards when this Bergamo business is over. You forget that under his hand is the strongest army in Italy today. We muster over twelve thousand men.”

===Chinese===
贝拉里翁静静等着下文，对方却住了口。

“怎么，阁下？”他问道，“就这些？”

“就这些？难道这消息在你眼里竟如此无足轻重，你才会这么问？你难道不知道，那个该千刀万剐的归尔甫派分子——法奇诺当年就该吊死他，却只将他流放——一直以来正是幕后唆使一切歹毒勾当、处处与法奇诺和米兰全体吉伯林派作对的祸根吗？你难道不明白，他这一回来，准没好事？”

“他能掀出什么风浪？吉安·玛丽亚又能做什么？他们的羽翼早已被剪断了。”

“他们正在长出新的羽翼呢。”韦内戈诺一时激动，连疲惫都忘了，猛地站起身来，“自从德拉托雷一个月前秘密潜回米兰，他们已经四下派出使节，去找蒙费拉托的西奥多、被打得元气大伤的维尼亚蒂家族（Vignati）、埃斯特家族（Esti），甚至还找上了埃斯托雷·维斯孔蒂（Estorre Visconti），邀他们结盟共谋大事。”

贝拉里翁笑了起来：“随他们结盟去好了。他们若真蠢到敢这么干，等贝加莫这档子事一了结，法奇诺便会把他们的同盟砸得粉碎。你莫忘了，如今握在他手里的，可是全意大利最精锐强悍的一支大军。我们麾下足足有一万两千多人。”

===Original===
“My God! I seem to be listening to Facino himself.” Venegono slobbered in his excitement, his eyes wild. “It was thus he answered me.”

“Why, then, have troubled to come to me?”

“In the hope that you would see what he will not. You talk as if the army were all. You forget that Gian Maria is a thing of venom, like the emblem of his accursed house. Where there is venom and the will to use it, beware the occasion. If anything should happen to Facino, what hope will remain for the Ghibellines of Milan?”

“What should happen to Facino? At what are you hinting, man?”

Venegono looked at him between rage and compassion. “Where is Mombelli?” he asked. “Why is he not with Facino now that Facino needs him? Do you know?”

“But is he not with Facino? Has he not yet arrived?”

===Chinese===
“我的天主啊！听你这话，简直像在听法奇诺亲口说话一样！”韦内戈诺激动得唾沫横飞，两眼发狂地圆睁着，“他当时也是这么打发我的。”

“那你又何必费神跑来找我？”

“还不是指望你能看清他不愿正视的祸患！你张口闭口仿佛兵马便是一切，却忘了吉安·玛丽亚本就是个满腹毒液的毒物，正像他那受诅咒家族的纹章一样！既有毒液，又有下毒的狠心，就得提防他找着可乘之机。万一法奇诺有个三长两短，米兰的吉伯林派还剩下什么指望？”

“法奇诺能出什么事？你这话里到底藏着什么暗示？”

韦内戈诺看着他，神情既焦躁愤懑，又夹杂着几分怜悯：“蒙贝利在哪儿？”他问道，“如今法奇诺正需要他，他为什么不在法奇诺身边？你可知道？”

“怎么，他还没到法奇诺身边吗？还没赶到帕维亚？”

===Original===
“Arrived? Why was he ever withdrawn? To be made physician to the Duke. A pretext, my friend, to deprive Facino of his healing services. Do you know that since his coming to Milan he has not been seen? There are rumours that he is dead, that the Duke has murdered him.”

Bellarion considered. Then he shrugged. “Your imagination fools you, Venegono. If Gian Maria proposed to strike Facino, he would surely attempt something more active and effective.”

“It may be little, I confess. But it is a straw that points the way of the wind.”

“A straw, indeed,” Bellarion agreed. “But in any case, what do you require of me? You have not told me that.”

“That you take a strong detachment of your men and repair at once to Milan to curb the Duke’s evil intentions and to deal with della Torre.”

“For that my lord’s orders would be necessary. My duty is here, Venegono, and I dare not neglect it. Nor is the matter so urgent. It can wait until Bergamo has been reduced, which will not be long.”

===Chinese===
“赶到？当初又为什么要把他调走？说是封他当公爵御医——那不过是个幌子罢了，我的朋友，真正的用意是要断了法奇诺身边的良医照料！你可知道，自从他进了米兰城，就再也没人见过他的踪影？外头都在传言他已经死了，说是被公爵害死了。”

贝拉里翁思忖片刻，随即耸了耸肩：“韦内戈诺，你是自己吓唬自己罢了。吉安·玛丽亚倘若真打算对法奇诺下手，势必会用更直接、更狠辣的手段。”

“我承认这事兴许不算大，可一根草芥虽微，却能指明风往哪边吹。”

“的确只是一根草芥，”贝拉里翁点头道，“不过话又说回来，你究竟想让我做什么？你还没跟我明说呢。”

“我要你立刻率领一支精锐人马赶赴米兰，压住公爵的歹心，顺道收拾了德拉托雷。”

“这事须得有我家主公的将令才行。韦内戈诺，我的职责在此，岂敢擅离职守。况且此事也远没到火烧眉毛的地步，尽可以等攻下贝加莫再从长计议——那也用不了几天了。”

===Original===
“Too long, it may be.”

But not all the passionate pleading with which he now distressed Bellarion could turn the latter from his clear duty, or communicate to him any of the vague alarms which agitated Venegono. And so, at last, he went his ways in despair, protesting that both Bellarion and Facino were beset with the blindness of those whom the gods wish to destroy.

Bellarion, however, saw in Venegono’s warning no more than an attempt to use him for the execution of a private vengeance. Three days later he thought he had confirmation of this. It came in a letter bearing Facino’s signature, but penned in the crabbed and pointed hand of the Countess, who had been summoned from Melegnano to minister to her lord. It informed Bellarion that the physician Mombelli had come at last in response to Facino’s request, and that Facino hoped soon to be afoot again. Indeed, there was already a perceptible improvement in his condition.

“So much for Venegono’s rumours that Mombelli has been murdered,” said Bellarion to himself, and laughed at the scaremongering of that credulous hothead.

But he thought differently when after another three days a second letter reached him signed by the Countess herself.

“My lord begs you to come to him at once,” she wrote. “He is so ill that Messer Mombelli despairs of him. Do not lose a moment, or you may be too late.”

===Chinese===
“只怕等不得那几天了。”

然而，任凭他接下来如何慷慨激昂、苦苦哀求地搅扰贝拉里翁，终究既没能动摇贝拉里翁那明明白白的职责操守，也没能把心里那些莫名恐慌传染给他半分。于是到最后，韦内戈诺只能绝望离去，临行前还愤愤声称，贝拉里翁和法奇诺二人正如那句古谚所言——天欲使其灭亡，必先令其昏聩盲目。

可在贝拉里翁看来，韦内戈诺这番警告无非是想借他的手去报一己私仇罢了。三天之后，他更觉自己的判断得到了印证——营中送来了一封信，落款虽是法奇诺的签名，字迹却出自伯爵夫人那手局促尖峭的笔法；原来她已奉召从梅莱尼亚诺赶回帕维亚侍奉夫君病榻。信中告诉贝拉里翁，名医蒙贝利总算应法奇诺之召赶到了，法奇诺指望不日便能重新下地行走；事实上，他的病况已经明显好转。

“什么蒙贝利已被谋害的谣言，就这么不攻自破了。”贝拉里翁自言自语着，不禁对那个轻信传言、爱惹事生非的莽夫好笑起来。

然而又过了三天，当第二封由伯爵夫人亲笔署名的信送到他手里时，他再也笑不出来了。

“我家夫君恳请你即刻赶来，”她在信中写道，“他病势骤危，连蒙贝利先生（Messer Mombelli）都已束手无策。万勿耽搁片刻，否则恐再难见最后一面。”

===Original===
He was more deeply stirred by that summons than by anything he could remember. If those who accounted him hard and remorselessly calculating could have seen him in that moment, the tears filming his eyes at the very thought of losing this man whom he loved, they must have formed a gentler opinion of his nature.

He sent at once for Carmagnola, and ordered a strong horse to be saddled and twenty lances to prepare to ride with him. Ride with him, however, they did not. They followed. For he rode like one possessed of devils. In three hours he covered the forty miles of difficult road that lay between Bergamo and Pavia, leaving one horse foundered and arriving on a second one that was spent by the time he reached Filippo Maria’s stronghold. Down he flung from it in the great courtyard, and, staggering and bespattered, he mounted the main staircase so wide and of such shallow steps that it was possible to ascend it on horseback.

Without pausing to see the Prince, he had himself conducted straight to Facino’s chamber, and there under the damask-hung canopy he found his adoptive father supine, inert, his countenance leaden-hued, looking as if he were laid out in death, save for his stertorous breathing and the fire that still glowed in the eyes under their tufted, fulvid brows.

Bellarion went down on his knees beside the bed, and took, in both his own that were so warm and strong, the cold, heavy hand that lay upon the coverlet.

The grey head rolled a little on its pillow; the ghost of a smile irradiated the strong, rugged face; the fingers of the cold hand faintly pressed Bellarion’s.

===Chinese===
记忆之中，还从没有任何一件事像这封催命般的急信那样深深撼动过他的心弦。倘若那些向来认定他铁石心肠、冷酷算计的人此刻能亲眼瞧见他——单是一想到即将失去这位自己深敬深爱的人，泪水便已悄然蒙住了他的双眼——他们对他的天性必定会生出柔和许多的评判。

他立时召来卡尔马尼奥拉，同时传令备好一匹健马，再点二十名枪骑兵随自己一同出发。可真上了路，那二十名骑兵哪里跟得上，只能远远缀在后头——他简直像着了魔般一路狂飙。短短三个钟头里，他便跑完了贝加莫到帕维亚之间那四十英里难行的道路，半途活活累垮了一匹坐骑，换乘第二匹赶到菲利波·玛丽亚的城堡时，那匹马也已是强弩之末。他在宽阔的中庭里翻身下马，满身泥污、步履踉跄地奔上那座宽敞平缓得连骑马都能登临的主楼梯。

他连停下来去见亲王一面的工夫都不顾，直接让人引着进了法奇诺的寝室。在织锦绸缎垂挂的华盖之下，他只见自己的义父仰卧在床，一动不动，面色如铅般死灰；若非喉间还在发出粗重的喘息，若非那双浓密黄褐的剑眉之下双眸仍燃着一点幽微火光，简直就像是已经停放好的亡人遗体。

贝拉里翁跪倒在床榻边，用自己那双温暖有力的手，紧紧握住了搭在床罩上那只冰凉沉重的手掌。

枕上那颗花白的头颅微微侧动了一下；一抹恍若幽魂般的笑意掠过那张坚毅粗犷的脸庞；冰凉的手指轻轻回握了握贝拉里翁的手。

===Original===
“Good lad, you have lost no time,” he said, in a weak, rasping voice. “And there is no time to lose. I am sped. Indeed, my body’s dead already. Mombelli says the gout is mounting to my heart.”

Bellarion looked up. Beyond the bed stood the Countess, fretful and troubled. At the foot was Mombelli, and in the background a servant.

“Is this so?” he asked the physician. “Can your skill avail nothing here?”

“He is in God’s hands,” said Mombelli, mumbling indistinctly.

“Send them away,” said Facino, and his eyes indicated Mombelli and the servant. “There is little time, and I have things to tell you. We must take order for what’s to follow.”

===Chinese===
“好孩子，你一点没耽搁，”他声音微弱而沙哑地说道，“也没有工夫好耽搁了。我不行了。说真的，我这副身子骨早已死了大半。蒙贝利说，痛风已经攻心了。”

贝拉里翁抬起头。床榻对面站着神色焦灼忧戚的伯爵夫人，床尾站着蒙贝利，更后头还侍立着一名仆人。

“真是如此吗？”他转头问那名御医，“难道以你的医术，竟半点回天之力都没有了？”

“全凭天主圣意了。”蒙贝利嘴里含混不清地嘟囔道。

“让他们退下，”法奇诺说着，眼神朝蒙贝利和那名仆人示意了一下，“时候不多了，我有话要嘱咐你。身后之事，我们必须早作安排。”

===Original===
The orders did not amount to very much. He required of Bellarion that he should afford the Countess his protection, and he recommended to him also Filippo Maria.

“When Gian Galeazzo died, he left his sons in my care. I go to meet him with clean hands. I have discharged my trust, and dying I hand it on to you. Remember always that Gian Maria is Duke of Milan, and whatever the shortcomings he may show, for your own sake if not for his, practise loyalty to him, as you would have your own captains be loyal to you.”

When at last, wearied, and announcing his desire to rest, Facino bade him go, Bellarion found Mombelli pacing in the Hall of Mirrors, and sent him to Facino.

“I shall remain here within call,” he said, and oblivious of his own fatigue he paced in his turn that curious floor whereon birds and beasts were figured in mosaics under the gaudy flashing ceiling of coloured glass, whence the place derived its name.

There Mombelli found him a half-hour later, when he emerged.

===Chinese===
他的嘱托其实并不繁多。他要求贝拉里翁务必要护卫伯爵夫人的周全，又将菲利波·玛丽亚托付给了他。

“当年吉安·加莱阿佐临终之时，把两个儿子托孤给我。如今我两手清白地去见他了。我已尽心竭力完成重托，临死前，我将这份担子交到你手里。永远记住，吉安·玛丽亚才是米兰公爵；无论他有多少不堪之处，哪怕不为他，只为你自己，也要对他尽忠——就像你指望你麾下的将校对你忠心耿耿一样。”

终于，法奇诺露出了倦意，表示想歇息一会儿，打发他出去。贝拉里翁退出来时，正撞见蒙贝利在镜厅里来回踱步，便打发他进去侍疾。

“我就在这儿候着，有事随叫随到。”他说完，浑然忘却了一身疲惫，反倒接替蒙贝利踱起步来。他脚下踩着嵌有飞禽走兽马赛克图案的奇巧地面，头顶上是彩色玻璃拼就、流光溢彩得近乎俗艳的穹顶——这镜厅之名便是由此而来。

半个钟头后，蒙贝利从寝室里走出来时，见他仍在厅中等候。

===Original===
“He sleeps now,” he said. “The Countess is with him.”

“It is not yet the end?” Bellarion asked.

“Not yet. The end is when God wills. He may linger for some days.”

Bellarion looked sharply at the doctor, considered him, indeed, now for the first time since his arrival. This Mombelli was a man of little more than thirty-five. He had been vigorous of frame, inclining a little to portliness, rubicund if grave of countenance with strong white teeth and bright dark eyes. Bellarion beheld now an emaciated man upon whose shrunken frame a black velvet gown hung in loose folds. His face was pale, his eyes dull; but oddest of all the very shape of his face had changed; his jaw had fallen in, so that nose and chin were brought closer like those of an old man, and when he spoke he hissed and mumbled indistinctly over toothless gums.

“By the Host, man! What has happened to you?”

Mombelli shrank visibly from the questions and from the stern eyes that seemed to search his very soul.

===Chinese===
“他睡下了，”蒙贝利说道，“伯爵夫人在里头守着。”

“还没到最后那一刻吧？”贝拉里翁问道。

“还没有。寿数几何全由天主定夺，他或许还能再撑上几天。”

贝拉里翁眼神一凛，锐利地打量起这位医生来——说起来，这还是他打从抵达后头一回正眼审视对方。这个蒙贝利不过三十五岁出头的年纪，从前体格健壮，略显富态，面容虽严肃却红润饱满，生着一口坚固雪白的牙齿和一双乌亮有神的眼睛。可眼下落在贝拉里翁眼里的，却是一个骨瘦如柴的干瘪汉子，身上那件黑天鹅绒长袍空荡荡地垂挂出层层褶皱。他脸色惨白，眼神浑浊黯淡；最古怪的是他连整张脸的轮廓都走了形，双颊深深凹陷下去，使得鼻尖与下巴凑得极近，活脱脱像个风烛残年的老翁；开口说话时，无牙的牙床直漏风，发出含混不清的嘶嘶含糊声。

“圣体在上！你这是怎么搞成这副模样的？”

蒙贝利被他这一问和那双仿佛要洞穿肺腑的严厉目光逼得浑身一缩，惊恐之色溢于言表。

===Original===
“I﻿ ﻿… I﻿ ﻿… have been ill,” he faltered. “Very ill. It is a miracle I am alive today.”

“But your teeth, man?”

“I have lost them as you see. A consequence of my disease.”

A horrible suspicion was sprouting in Bellarion’s mind, nourished by the memory of the rumour of this man’s death which Venegono had reported. He took the doctor by the sleeve of his velvet gown, and drew him towards one of the double windows. His shrinking, his obvious reluctance to undergo this closer inspection, were so much added food to Bellarion’s suspicion.

“How do you call this disease?” he asked.

Clearly, from his hesitancy, Mombelli had been unprepared for the question. “It﻿ ﻿… it is a sort of podagric affection,” he mumbled.

===Chinese===
“我……我……病了一场，”他结结巴巴地支吾道，“病得很重。今天还能活着，简直是个奇迹。”

“可你的牙呢，先生？”

“如你所见，全掉光了。都是那场恶疾落下的病根。”

一个令人毛骨悚然的疑念在贝拉里翁心头骤然滋生，而韦内戈诺提过的那桩关于此人已死的传闻，恰如养料般瞬间让这疑念疯长起来。他一把攥住医生天鹅绒长袍的袖口，将他拖到一扇双开窗前。对方那副畏缩闪躲、显然不愿凑近亮光让人细看的模样，更是一下子坐实了贝拉里翁心中的猜疑。

“你管这病叫什么名字？”他逼问道。

从他那副支支吾吾的反应看，蒙贝利显然没料到对方会这么问。“这……这是一种痛风类的病症。”他含含糊糊地应付道。

===Original===
“And your thumb? Why is that bandaged?”

Terror leapt to Mombelli’s eyes. His toothless jaws worked fearfully. “That? That is naught. An injury.”

“Take off the bandage. Take it off, man. I desire to see this injury. Do you hear me?”

At last Mombelli with shaking fingers stripped the bandage from his left thumb, and displayed it naked.

Bellarion went white, and his eyes were dreadful. “You have been tortured, master doctor. Gian Maria has subjected you to his Lent.”

This Lent of Gian Maria’s invention was a torment lasting forty days, on each of which one or more teeth were torn from the patient’s jaws, then day by day a finger nail, whereafter followed the eyes and finally the tongue, whereupon the sufferer being rendered dumb and unable to confess what was desired, he was shown at last the mercy of being put to death.

===Chinese===
“那你的大拇指呢？为什么裹着绷带？”

惊骇瞬间窜上了蒙贝利的眼底，他那张没牙的嘴唇抖得不成样子：“那个？那个不算什么，碰伤了而已。”

“解开绷带。给我解开！我要亲眼看看这处伤。你听见没有？”

蒙贝利终于伸出颤巍巍的手指，一圈圈解下左手大拇指上的布条，将伤处赤裸裸地露了出来。

贝拉里翁霎时面如白纸，一双眼睛森寒骇人：“医生大人，你受过酷刑了。吉安·玛丽亚对你动用了他的‘大斋期（Lent）’酷刑。”

这套由吉安·玛丽亚独创的“大斋期”，乃是一种绵延四十日的惨烈刑罚：头些日子每天从受刑者嘴里硬生生拔掉一颗或几颗牙齿，继而日复一日地拔去一根手指甲，再往后便是剜去双眼，最后割掉舌头；待受刑者彻底成了哑巴、再也无法吐出半个他们想要的供词时，才大发慈悲将他一杀了之。

===Original===
Mombelli’s livid lips moved frantically, but no words came. He reeled where he stood until he found the wall to steady him, and Bellarion watched him with those dreadful, searching eyes.

“To what end did he torture you? What did he desire of you?”

“I have not said he tortured me. It is not true.”

“You have not said it. No. But your condition says it. You have not said it, because you dare not. Why did he do this? And why did he desist?” Bellarion gripped him by the shoulders. “Answer me. To what did the torments undergone suffice to constrain you? Will you answer me?”

“O God!” groaned the physician, sagging limply against the wall, and looking as if he would faint.

But there was no pity in Bellarion’s face. “Come with me,” he said, and it was almost by main force that he dragged the wretched doctor across that hall out to the gallery, and down the wide steps to the great court. Here under the arcade some men-at-arms of Facino’s bodyguard were idling. Into their hands Bellarion delivered Mombelli.

===Chinese===
蒙贝利惨青的嘴唇疯狂地翕动着，却半个字也吐不出来。他站立不稳，踉跄着摸到墙壁才勉强撑住身子；贝拉里翁则始终用那双森冷迫人的利眼紧盯着他。

“他折磨你究竟是为了什么？他逼你替他干什么？”

“我没说过他折磨我。不是真的！”

“你是没说，没错。可你这副鬼样子替你全招了！你不说，是因为你不敢说！他为什么对你下这等毒手？后来又为什么住了手？”贝拉里翁一把揪住他的双肩，“回答我！那些酷刑究竟逼得你屈从了什么勾当？你到底说不说！”

“天主啊！”御医哀号一声，整个人软绵绵地顺着墙壁瘫滑下去，眼看就要昏厥。

然而贝拉里翁脸上没有一丝怜悯。“跟我走。”他冷冷吐出三个字，几乎是硬生生拽着这个可怜虫穿过镜厅、走出长廊，一路拖下宽阔的台阶来到大庭院。拱廊下正有几名法奇诺亲兵队的披甲卫士闲站着，贝拉里翁一把将蒙贝利推到他们手里。

===Original===
“To the question chamber,” he said shortly.

Mombelli, shattered in nerve and sapped of manhood by his sufferings, cried out, piteously inarticulate. Pitilessly Bellarion waved him away, and the soldiers bore him off, screaming, to the stone chamber under the northeastern tower. There, in the middle of the uneven stone floor, stood the dread framework of the rack.

Bellarion, who had followed, ordered them to strip him. The men were reluctant to do the office of executioners, but under the eyes of Bellarion, standing as implacable as the god of wrath, they set about it, nevertheless, and all the while the broken man’s cries for mercy filled that vaulted place with an ever-mounting horror. At the last, half-naked, he broke from the men’s hands and flung himself at Bellarion’s feet.

“In the name of the sweet Christ, my lord, take pity on me! I can bear no more. Hang me if you will, but do not let me be tortured again.”

Bellarion looked down on the grovelling, slobbering wretch with an infinite compassion in his soul. But there was no sign of it on his countenance or in his voice.

===Chinese===
“押进刑讯室。”他言简意赅地吩咐道。

蒙贝利早被连番酷刑折磨得神经溃散、骨气尽丧，此刻只能发出几声含混凄厉的哀鸣。贝拉里翁冷酷地一挥手，士兵们便架起一路尖叫的御医，拖进了东北角塔楼底下的石室。就在那间凹凸不平的石板地中央，赫然矗立着一具令人望而生畏的拉肢刑架。

随后跟进来的贝拉里翁下令扒光他的衣裳。卫士们本不大情愿干这种刽子手的差事，可在贝拉里翁的目光逼视下——他宛如怒火之神般冷峻无情地立在一旁——他们也只得动起手来；其间那崩溃之人的求饶声充斥着整座拱顶石室，让惨厉骇人的气氛节节攀升。到头来，被扒得半裸的蒙贝利挣脱士兵的钳制，扑通一声跪倒在贝拉里翁脚下。

“看在仁慈基督的份上，大人，可怜可怜我吧！我实在受不住了！您要绞死我便绞死我吧，千万别再对我用刑了！”

贝拉里翁低头俯视着脚下这名匍匐战栗、涕泪横流的凄惨之人，心底涌起无限怜悯；然而他的神色与声调里，却半点也不曾流露出来。

===Original===
“You have but to answer my question, sir, and you shall have your wish. You shall be hanged without further suffering. Why did the Duke torture you, and why did the torture cease when it did? To what importunities did you yield?”

“Already you have guessed it, my lord. That is why you use me so! But it is not just. As God’s my witness, it is not just. What am I but a poor man caught in the toils of the evil desires of others? As long as God gave me the strength to resist, I resisted. But I could bear no more. There was no price at which I would not have purchased respite from that horror. Death I could have borne had that been all they threatened. But I had reached the end of my endurance of pain. Oh, my lord, if I were a villain there would have been no torture to endure. They offered me bribes, bribes great enough to dazzle a poor man, that would have left me rich for the remainder of my days. When I refused, they threatened me with death unless I did their infamous will. Those threats I defied. Then they subjected me to this protracted agony which the Duke impiously calls his Lent. They drew my teeth, brutally with unutterable violence, two each day until all were gone. Broken and most starved as I was, distracted by pain, which for a fortnight had been unceasing, they began upon my fingernails. But when they tore the nail from my left thumb, I could bear no more. I yielded to their infamy.”

Bellarion made a sign to the men, and they pulled Mombelli to his feet. But his eyes dared not meet the terrible glance of Bellarion.

“You yielded to their demands that, under the pretence of curing him, you should poison my Lord Facino. That is the thing to which you yielded. But when you say ‘they’ whom do you mean?”

“The Duke Gian Maria and Antonio della Torre.”

===Chinese===
“先生，你只要回答我的问题，便能如你所愿——不必再受皮肉之苦，直接给你个绞刑的痛快。公爵为何对你用刑？刑罚又为何偏在半途停止？你究竟是在什么威逼之下屈服的？”

“大人，您心里其实早就猜到了，所以才会这般待我！可这不公道啊！天主作证，这实在太不公道了！我不过是个落入他人歹毒算计网罗里的可怜虫罢了！只要天主还赐我一分气力抗拒，我就死撑着不肯就范。可我实在熬不住了！为了换取片刻喘息、逃离那人间炼狱，叫我付出什么代价我都肯啊！若是他们只拿一死相逼，我倒也受得住；可痛苦已经把我碾磨到了极限。啊，大人，倘若我真是个奸恶之徒，又何至于遭这等活罪？他们先是重金贿赂我，那数目大得足以晃花一个穷人的眼，够我下半辈子荣华富贵。我拒绝了，他们便威胁说若不依从这桩卑劣勾当就处死我，我也凛然不惧。于是他们便对我施以那套连绵不绝的惨刑——就是公爵亵渎神明地称作‘大斋期’的恶刑。他们残暴无情、令人发指地每天生拔我两颗牙齿，直到满口牙一颗不剩。等到我筋疲力尽、几近饿毙、被整整十四天昼夜不停的剧痛折磨得神志迷乱时，他们又开始拔我的手指甲。当他们把左手大拇指的指甲生生撕下来那一刻，我再也扛不住了——我终究还是屈从了他们的无耻之举。”

贝拉里翁朝卫士们使了个眼色，他们便把蒙贝利架起身来。只是他再也不敢直视贝拉里翁那道凛冽可畏的目光。

“你屈从了他们的要求，借着替我家法奇诺大人治病的幌子，暗中下毒谋害他——这就是你屈服后干的勾当。不过，你口口声声说的‘他们’，究竟是指谁？”

“吉安·玛丽亚公爵和安东尼奥·德拉托雷（Antonio della Torre）。”

===Original===
Bellarion remembered Venegono’s warning﻿—“He is a thing of venom, like the emblem of his house.”

“Poor wretch!” said Bellarion. “You deserve some mercy, and you shall have it, provided you can undo what you have done.”

“Alas, my lord!” Mombelli groaned, wringing his hands in a passion of despair. “Alas! There is no antidote to that poison. It works slowly gradually corroding the intestines. Hang me, my lord, and have done. Had I been less of a coward, I would have hanged myself before I did this thing. But the Duke threatened that if I failed him the torture should be resumed and continued until I died of sheer exhaustion. Also he swore that my refusal would not save my Lord Facino, whom he would find other means of despatching.”

Bellarion stood between loathing and compassion. But there was no thought in his mind of hanging this poor wretch, who had been the victim of that malignant Duke.

He uttered an order in cold, level tones: “Restore him his garments and place him in confinement until I send for him again.”

On that he departed from that underground chamber, and slowly, thoughtfully made his way above.

===Chinese===
贝拉里翁猛然想起了韦内戈诺的那句警告——“他本就是个毒物，正像他家族的纹章一样。”

“可怜人！”贝拉里翁说道，“你也配得上几分宽宥；只要你能挽回自己犯下的恶果，我便饶你一条生路。”

“唉，大人啊！”蒙贝利绝望地搓绞着双手哀号道，“唉！那毒药根本没有解药！它毒性发作得慢，会一点一点腐烂人的肠胃。大人，还是绞死我，让我了断了吧。当初我若稍微少一分怯懦，在动手前就该自缢身亡的。可公爵扬言，倘若我敢违逆他，便要重新用刑，直到把我活活折磨得气绝力竭为止。况且他还赌咒发誓，说就算我不从，也救不了法奇诺大人，他自会另寻法子取他性命。”

贝拉里翁站在原地，心中厌恶与悲悯交织。不过他打从一开始便没真想过要绞死这个可怜虫——归根结底，他也是那名歹毒公爵刀俎下的受害者。

他用冷静平缓的语气下令道：“把衣裳还给他穿上，好生看押起来，等我再传唤。”

说罢，他转身离开那间地牢石室，脚步沉缓而思绪翻涌地拾级而上。

===Original===
By the time he reached the courtyard his resolve was taken, though his neck should pay for it: Gian Maria should not escape. For the first and only time in those adventurous years of his did he swerve from the purpose by which he laid his course, and turn his hand to a task that was not more or less directly concerned with its ultimate fulfilment.

And so, without pausing for rest or food, you behold him once more in the saddle, riding hard for Milan on that Monday afternoon.

He conceived that he bore thither the first news of Facino’s moribund condition.

But rumour had been ahead of him by a day and a half, and the rumour ran, not that Facino was dying, but that he was already dead.

===Chinese===
待他走出庭院时，主意已然拿定，纵然搭上自己这条性命也在所不惜：绝不能让吉安·玛丽亚逍遥法外。在他那段波澜壮阔的历险岁月里，这是头一回，也是唯一一回，他偏离了平日里一以贯之的行事准绳，转而亲手去办一桩与自己终极抱负并无直接干系的差事。

于是，顾不上歇脚也顾不上果腹，你瞧他又一次跨上了马鞍，就在那个周一的午后，策马疾驰直奔米兰而去。

他原以为，自己是带着法奇诺弥留垂危的第一手消息赶往那座城池的。

殊不知流言早已抢在他前头传了一天半——而且坊间盛传的并非法奇诺危在旦夕，而是他已经撒手人寰。

===Original===
In all the instances history affords of poetic justice to give pause to those who offend against God and Man, none is more arresting than that of the fate of Gian Maria Visconti. Already on the previous Friday word had reached the Duke, not only from Mombelli, but from at least one of the spies he had placed in his brother’s household, that the work of poisoning was done and that Facino’s hours were numbered. Gloating with della Torre and Lonate over the assurance that at last the ducal neck was delivered from that stern heel under which so long it had writhed like the serpent of evil under the heel of Saint Michael, Gian Maria had been unable to keep the knowledge to himself. About the court on that same Friday night he spoke unguardedly of Facino as dead or dying, and from the court the news filtered through to the city and was known to all by the morning of Saturday. And that news carried with it a dismay more utter and overwhelming than any that had yet descended upon Milan since Gian Maria had worn the ducal crown. Facino, when wielding the authority of ducal governor, had been the people’s bulwark against the extortions, brutalities, and criminal follies of their Duke. When absent and deposed from power, he had still been their hope, and they had possessed their soul as best they could against the day of his return, which they knew must dawn. But Facino dead meant an unbridling of the Duke’s bestiality, a free charter to his misrule, and for his people an outlook of utter hopelessness. It may be that they exaggerated in their own minds this calamity. It was for them the end of the world. Despair settled that morning upon the city. The Duke would have laughed if it had been reported to him, because he lacked the wit to perceive that when men are truly desperate catastrophes ensue.

And at once, whilst the great mass of the people were stricken by horror into a dull inertia, there were those who saw that the situation called for action. Of these were members of the leading Ghibelline families of Bagio, of del Maino, Trivulzi, Aliprandi, and others. There was that Bertino Mantegazza, captain of the ducal guard whose face the Duke had one day broken with his iron gauntlet, and fiercest and most zealous of all there was that Giovanni Pusterla of Venegono, whose family had suffered such deep and bitter wrongs at the Duke’s hands.

There was no suspicion in the mind of any that the Duke himself was responsible for the death of Facino. It was simply that Facino’s death created a situation only to be met by the destruction of the Duke. And this situation the Duke himself had been at such hideous pains to bring about.

===Chinese===
翻遍史册中令逆天害理之徒心惊胆寒的因果报应之例，再没有比吉安·玛丽亚·维斯孔蒂的结局更触目惊心的了。早在前一个星期五，便已有消息传进公爵耳中——不仅来自蒙贝利，还来自他安插在弟弟府邸里的至少一名暗探——说是下毒之事已然功成，法奇诺阳寿将尽。吉安·玛丽亚与德拉托雷、洛纳泰（Lonate）一同弹冠相庆，庆幸公爵的脖颈总算挣脱了那只冷酷鞋跟的踩踏（长久以来，他在那只脚下扭曲挣扎，活像圣米迦勒（Saint Michael）脚跟底下那条邪恶毒蛇）；得意忘形之下，他竟守不住口风。就在那个周五夜里，他在宫廷中口无遮拦地放话，说法奇诺非死即垂危；这消息从宫中漏进市井，及至周六清晨，已是满城皆知。这则噩耗带来的惊惶与绝望之深重，简直胜过吉安·玛丽亚戴上公爵冠冕以来降临米兰的一切灾厄。法奇诺当年执掌公国总管大权时，向来是百姓抵御公爵勒索、暴虐与荒唐暴行的屏障；哪怕后来远走失势，他依然是全城百姓心头的指望，众人只得强忍煎熬，翘首期盼着他终有卷土重来的一日。可法奇诺一死，便意味着公爵的兽行再无缰绳可勒，他的暴政从此畅行无阻，落在黎民头上的唯有一片毫无出路的绝境。或许百姓在心头将这场大祸放大了些，可对他们而言，那无异于末日降临。那个清晨，沉沉绝望笼罩了整座米兰城。若是有人把这光景报与公爵，他准会嗤笑出声——因为他压根没有那份心智去参透一个道理：人若被逼入真正的绝境，大祸便紧随其后。

于是立时之间，正当普罗大众被惊骇吓得浑身麻木、束手无策之际，城中却有一批人看清了眼下唯有挺身一搏。这其中有吉伯林派几大名门望族的子弟——巴焦家族（Bagio）、德尔·迈诺家族（del Maino）、特里武尔齐家族（Trivulzi）、阿利普兰迪家族等等；有那位曾被公爵用铁护手砸碎过脸庞的公爵卫队长贝尔蒂诺·曼泰加扎（Bertino Mantegazza）；而其中最凶悍、也最义无反顾的，正是家族曾蒙受公爵深仇大恨的韦内戈诺的乔瓦尼·普斯泰尔拉。

这群人里头，没有一个曾怀疑过法奇诺之死竟是公爵亲手所为。事情再简单不过：法奇诺一死，局势便逼到了唯有一举除掉公爵方能化解的地步——而这番局势，偏偏正是公爵自己机关算尽、费尽天大惨毒心思才一手酿成的。

===Original===
And so, briefly to recapitulate here a page of Visconti history, it came to pass that on the Monday morning, which was the first day of the Litany of May, as Gian Maria, gaily clad in his colours of red and white, was issuing from his bedroom to repair to Mass in the Church of San Gotthard, he found in the antechamber a score of gentlemen not latterly seen about his court. Mantegazza, who had command of the entrance, was responsible for their presence.

Before the Duke could comment upon this unusual attendance, perhaps before he had well observed it, three of them were upon him.

“This from the Pusterla!” cried Venegono, and with his dagger clove the Duke’s brow, slaying him instantly. Yet before he fell Andrea Bagio’s blade was buried in his right thigh, so that presently that white-stockinged leg was as red as its fellow.

As a consequence, Bellarion reaching Milan at dusk that evening found entrance denied him at the Ticinese Gate, which was held by Paolo del Bagio with a strong following of men-at-arms. Not until he had disclosed himself for Facino’s lieutenant was he admitted and informed of what had taken place.

===Chinese===
就这样，简略重述维斯孔蒂家族史上这一页：就在那个周一清晨——恰逢五月祷文日（Litany of May）的头一天——吉安·玛丽亚身穿他那身红白相间的华丽徽色服饰，从寝室迈步出来，正准备去圣哥达（San Gotthard）教堂做弥撒，却见前厅里站着二十来位近来在宫廷中久未露面的贵族绅士。把守门户的曼泰加扎，正是放他们进来的内应。

公爵还没来得及对这反常的阵仗开口发问，兴许压根都还没看清来人，其中三人已经扑到了他跟前。

“这是普斯泰尔拉家族给你的！”韦内戈诺一声暴喝，手中短剑顺势劈开公爵的额头，将他立毙当场。即便在他尚未倒地之际，安德烈亚·巴焦（Andrea Bagio）的利刃也已深深刺进了他的右大腿，眨眼间便将那条套着白袜的腿染得和另一条红袜一般鲜红。

正因如此，当贝拉里翁于那日黄昏时分赶到米兰城下时，发现提契诺门（Ticinese Gate）已被保罗·德尔·巴焦（Paolo del Bagio）率领大队披甲士卒把守，严禁外人入城。直到他亮明自己身为法奇诺副将的身份，守军才放他进门，并将城中发生的巨变告知于他。

===Original===
The irony of the event provoked in him a terrible mirth.

“Poor purblind fool,” was his comment. “He never guessed when he was torturing Mombelli that he was torturing him into signing his own death-warrant.” That, and the laugh with which he rode on into the city, left Bagio wondering whether his wits had turned.

He rode through streets in uproar, where almost every man he met was armed. Before the broken door of a half-shattered house hung some revolting bleeding rags, what once had been a man.
