These were all that remained of Squarcia Giramo, the infamous kennel-master who had been torn into pieces that day by the mob, and finally hung there before his dwelling which on the morrow was to be razed to the ground.

He came to the Old Broletto and the Church of Saint Gotthard, and paused there to survey the Duke’s body where it lay under an apronful of roses which had been cast upon it by a harlot. Thence he repaired to the stables of the palace, and by making himself known procured a fresh horse. On this he made his way through the ever-increasing tumult of the streets, back to the Ticinese Gate, and he was away through the darkness to cover for the second time that day the twenty miles that lie between Milan and Pavia.

It was past midnight when, so jaded that he kept his feet by a sheer effort of the will, he staggered into Filippo Maria’s bedchamber, ushered by the servant who had preceded him to rouse the Prince.

===Chinese===
世事如此阴差阳错的讽刺，激得他喉间涌起一阵森寒骇人的笑意。

“好个有眼无珠的可怜蠢货，”他冷然评道，“他拷打蒙贝利的时候，怕是做梦也没料到，自己竟是在逼着人家替他签下催命符呢！”说完这话，他大笑着策马进城而去，把巴焦留在原地，看得直怀疑这位大人是不是失心疯了。

他策马穿过沸反盈天、一片混乱的街巷，迎面撞见的几乎人人手执兵刃。一栋半毁宅邸的破门前，吊挂着几缕血肉模糊、令人作呕的碎布残片——那曾经是一个大活人。那就是臭名昭著的养犬官斯夸尔恰·吉拉莫所剩的全部遗骸；当日他被愤怒的暴民活活撕成碎片，最后被悬尸于自家门口示众，而这座宅子次日便要被夷为平地。

他来到旧布罗莱托宫与圣哥达教堂前，驻马俯瞰着横陈在地的公爵遗体——一名妓女刚往尸身上撒了一围裙鲜红的玫瑰。随后他转去宫中马厩，通报身份后换了匹健马，顶着愈演愈烈的街头喧嚣，再度折返提契诺门，趁着夜色奔腾而去，当天第二回策马跑起米兰至帕维亚之间那二十英里路程。

抵达时已是午夜过后。他疲惫到了极点，全凭一股意志硬撑着才不至于瘫倒在地，在一名先行入内唤醒亲王的仆役引领下，踉踉跄跄走进了菲利波·玛丽亚的寝室。

===Original===
Filippo Maria sat up in bed, blinking in the candlelight, at that tall, swaying figure that was almost entirely clothed in mud.

“Is that you, Lord Bellarion? You will have heard that Facino is dead﻿—God rest his soul!”

A harsh, croaking voice made him answer! “Aye, and avenged, Lord Duke.”

A quiver crossed the pale fat face under its sleek black cap of hair. The coarse lips parted. “Lord﻿ ﻿… Lord Duke﻿ ﻿… you said?” The high-pitched voice was awestricken.

“Your brother Gian Maria is dead, my lord, and you are Duke of Milan.”

“Duke of Milan? I am﻿ ﻿… ?” The grotesque young face showed bewilderment, confusion, fear. “And Gian Maria﻿ ﻿… Dead, do you say?”

===Chinese===
菲利波·玛丽亚从床上坐起身，在摇曳的烛光里眨巴着眼，望着眼前那个身形修长、摇摇晃晃、几乎浑身裹满泥浆的身影。

“是你吗，贝拉里翁大人？想来你已经听说了，法奇诺去世了——愿天主赐他灵魂安息！”

一声沙哑干涩的嗓音回答了他：“是的，而且大仇已报，公爵大人。”

那顶油亮乌黑的帽发底下，一张苍白肥肿的脸孔猛地抽搐了一下，粗厚的嘴唇微微张开。“公……公爵大人……你刚才叫我什么？”那尖细的嗓音里透着惊惧与敬畏。

“大人，您的兄长吉安·玛丽亚已经死了，如今您就是米兰公爵。”

“米兰公爵？我是……？”那张怪相的年轻面孔上写满了错愕、茫然与惊恐，“那吉安·玛丽亚……你是说他死了？”

===Original===
Bellarion did not mince matters. “He was despatched to hell this morning by some gentlemen in Milan.”

“Jesus-Mary!” croaked the Prince, and fell to trembling. “Murdered﻿ ﻿… And you﻿ ﻿… ?” He heaved himself higher in the bed with one arm, whilst he flung out the other in accusation. He did not love his brother. He profited greatly by his death. But a Visconti does not permit that others shall lay hands on a Visconti.

Bellarion laughed oddly. He had been forestalled. Perhaps it was as well. No need now to speak of his intentions.

“He was slain on his way to Mass this morning, at just about the hour that I arrived here from Bergamo.”

===Chinese===
贝拉里翁没有半点拐弯抹角：“今日一早，米兰的几位贵族绅士已经送他下地狱去了。”

“耶稣玛利亚！”亲王哑声尖叫起来，浑身簌簌发抖，“被谋害了……那你……？”他用一只手臂在床上撑高身子，另一只手直指着贝拉里翁厉声质问。他并不爱自己的兄长，兄长的死反倒叫他平白得了天大的便宜；然而无论如何，维斯孔蒂家的人绝不允许外人对维斯孔蒂动手动脚。

贝拉里翁古怪地笑了一声。有人抢在了他前头，兴许这样倒更好。眼下自然没必要再提起他原本打的什么主意了。

“他今天早晨去望弥撒的路上遇了刺，算算时辰，恰巧就在我从贝加莫赶到这里那会儿。”

===Original===
The accusing arm fell heavily to the Prince’s obese flank. The beady, lacklustre eyes still peered at the young condottiero.

“Almost I thought﻿ ﻿… And Giannino is dead﻿ ﻿… murdered! God rest him!” The phrase was mechanical. “Tell me about it.”

Bellarion recited what he knew, then staggered out, on the arm of the servant who was to conduct him to the room prepared for him.

“What a world! What a dunghill!” he muttered as he went. “And how well the old abbot knows it. *Pax multa in cella, foris autem plurima bella!*”

===Chinese===
那只指责的手臂沉沉垂落到亲王肥胖的腰侧，那双珠子般黯淡无光的小眼睛却依然紧盯着面前这位年轻的雇佣兵统帅。

“我差点还以为……这么说吉安尼诺（Giannino）真的死了……被人害死了！愿天主让他安息吧！”这句祷词念得干巴巴的毫无生气，“把经过细细讲给我听。”

贝拉里翁将所知详情原原本本道来，随后便由仆人搀扶着手臂，脚步虚浮地退了出去，任凭那仆人引自己去早已备好的房间歇息。

“好一个世道！好一个粪坑！”他一边走，一边低声咕哝道，“那位老院长真是看得再透彻不过了。*Pax multa in cella, foris autem plurima bella!*”（斗室之中多安宁，墙垣之外战祸频！）

## VI The Inheritance / 第六章 遗产

===Original===
Facino Cane, Count of Biandrate, Lord of Novara, Dertona, Varese, Rosate, Valsassina, and of all the lands on Lake Maggiore as far as Vogogna, was buried with great pomp in the Church of San Pietro in Ciel d’Oro.

His chief mourners were his captains summoned from Bergamo to do that last honour to their departed leader. At their head, as mourner in chief, walked Facino’s adoptive son Bellarion Cane, Count of Gavi. The others included Francesco Busone of Carmagnola, Giorgio Valperga, Nicolino Marsalia, Werner von Stoffel, and Vaugeois the Burgundian.

Koenigshofen and the Piedmontese Giasone Trotta were absent, having remained at Bergamo with the army.

Thereafter the captains assembled in the Hall of Mirrors to hear the will and last instructions of Facino. To read them came Facino’s secretary, accompanied by the Pavese notary who had drawn up the testament three days ago. Thither also came the Countess robed entirely in black and heavily veiled.

The rich and important fief of Valsassina was now disclosed to have been left by Facino to his adoptive son Bellarion, “in earnest of my love and to recompense his loyalty and worth.” Apart from that and a legacy in money for Carmagnola, the whole of his vast territorial possessions of cities, lands, and fortresses﻿—mostly acquired since he had been deposed in favour of Malatesta﻿—besides the enormous sum of four hundred thousand ducats, were all bequeathed to his widow. He expressed the wish that Bellarion should succeed him in the command of his condotta, and reminding his other captains that strength lies in unity he recommended them to remain united under Bellarion’s leadership, at least until the task of restoring order to the duchy should be fulfilled. To his captains also he recommended his widow, putting it upon them to see her firmly established in the dominions he bequeathed to her.

===Chinese===
法奇诺·卡内——比安德拉泰伯爵，兼领诺瓦拉（Novara）、德尔托纳（Dertona）、瓦雷泽（Varese）、罗萨泰（Rosate）、瓦尔萨西纳，以及远至沃戈尼亚（Vogogna）的马焦雷湖（Lake Maggiore）沿岸全境之主——以极隆重的仪仗安葬于圣彼得金天教堂。

执丧礼之首者，乃自贝加莫奉召赶来向亡故统帅致以最后敬意的麾下诸将。居于队列最前、充任首席丧主的，是法奇诺的养子、加维伯爵贝拉里翁·卡内。其余将领包括卡尔马尼奥拉的弗朗切斯科·布索内、乔治·瓦尔佩尔加（Giorgio Valperga）、尼科利诺·马尔萨利亚（Nicolino Marsalia）、维尔纳·冯·斯托费尔，以及勃艮第人沃茹瓦（Vaugeois）。

柯尼希斯霍芬与皮埃蒙特人贾索内·特罗塔因留守贝加莫统领大军而未克出席。

葬礼既毕，诸将齐聚镜厅，恭听法奇诺的遗嘱与临终训示。前来宣读遗命的，是法奇诺的秘书，随行的还有三天前亲手拟定遗嘱的那位帕维亚公证人。伯爵夫人亦步入厅中，通身一袭黑衣，面庞掩在厚重的黑纱之下。

遗嘱既启，众人方知法奇诺已将富庶要紧的瓦尔萨西纳采邑遗赠给养子贝拉里翁，“以证吾爱，亦酬其忠贞才德”。除此一处领地及拨予卡尔马尼奥拉的一笔遗赠钱款外，法奇诺名下所有广袤疆土——包括城池、田产与要塞，其中泰半皆是他遭罢黜以让位马拉泰斯塔之后陆续攻取所得——连同高达四十万杜卡特金币的巨额资财，尽数留给了他的遗孀。他还表明心愿，望由贝拉里翁接掌其雇佣兵团统帅之职，并切切叮嘱其余诸将：团结方有力量，务须在贝拉里翁统率之下精诚一体，至少应同心协力，直至重整公国秩序之大任告成。此外，他还将遗孀托付给众位将领，责成他们务必护持她稳稳执掌他所遗留的各处领地。

===Original===
When the reading was done, the captains rose in their places and turned to Madonna Beatrice where she sat like an ebony statue at the table’s head. Carmagnola, ever theatrical, ever a man of attitudes, drew his sword with a flourish and laid it on the board.

“Madonna, to you I surrender the authority I held under my Lord Facino, and I leave it in your hands until such time as it shall please you to reinvest me in it.”

The ceremonious gesture caught the fancy of the others. Valperga followed the example instantly, and presently five swords lay naked on the oak. To these, Bellarion, after a moment, a little scornful of this ritual, as he was of all unnecessary displays, added his own.

The Countess rose. She thanked them in a voice that shook with emotion, and one by one restored their weapons to them, naming each as she did so. Bellarion’s, however, she left upon the board, wherefore Bellarion, wondering a little, remained when she dismissed the others.

Slowly then she resumed her seat. Slowly she raised and threw back her veil, disclosing a face, which beyond a deeper pallor resulting, perhaps, from contrast with her sable raiment, showed little trace of grief. Her feline eyes considered him, a little frown between their fine black brows.

===Chinese===
遗嘱宣读完毕，诸将纷纷离座起身，转身面向端坐于长桌首座、宛如一尊黑檀雕像的贝阿特丽切夫人。向来爱做戏、事事讲究排场作态的卡尔马尼奥拉率先动作，花哨地掣出佩剑，稳稳置于长案之上。

“夫人，昔日法奇诺大人授我之兵权，今日谨奉还于您，暂交您掌管，静候您何时欢喜，再行赐予。”

这般郑重其事的做派立时合了其余众人的心意。瓦尔佩尔加当即效仿，片刻之间，橡木长案上已然寒光凛凛地躺了五柄长剑。贝拉里翁向来轻蔑此类繁文缛节，一如他向来鄙薄一切无谓的虚饰铺张，但略一迟疑之后，终究也将自己的佩剑放了上去。

伯爵夫人起身离座，以百感交集、微微颤抖的嗓音向众人致谢，随后逐一呼唤诸将姓名，将佩剑亲手交还。唯独贝拉里翁那一柄，她却留在了桌上未动；于是当她遣散众人退下时，贝拉里翁心下略生几分诧异，便留步未走。

待众人散尽，她缓缓落座。又缓缓抬手掀开面纱往后撩起，露出一张面庞——除了兴许因一身黑衣衬托而显得愈发苍白之外，那张脸上几乎不见半分悲戚之色。她那双猫儿般的眼眸端详着他，两道纤细的墨眉之间微蹙起一痕浅皱。

===Original===
“You were the last to offer me that homage, Bellarion.” Her voice was slow and softly attuned. “Why did you hesitate? Are you reluctant?”

“It was a gesture, madonna, that becomes the Carmagnolas of this world. Sincerity requires no symbols, and it was only at the symbol that I boggled. My service and my life are unreservedly at your command.”

There was a pause. Her eyes continued to ponder him. “Take up your sword,” she said at last.

He moved to do so, and then checked. “Yourself you restored theirs to the others.”

“The others are not as you. Upon you has fallen the mantle of Facino. How much of that mantle will you wear, Bellarion?”

“As much of it as my lord intended. You have heard his testament, madonna.”

===Chinese===
“贝拉里翁，数你最后一个向我献上这番效忠之礼。”她的声音不疾不徐，柔缓低沉，“你为何犹豫？莫非心怀勉强？”

“夫人，那般做派，正相宜于世上卡尔马尼奥拉之流的人物。赤诚忠心无须假借虚礼表记，我方才迟疑，不过是碍于这层虚饰罢了。我的微末之躯与毕生效力，皆毫无保留地听凭夫人差遣。”

室中静默了片刻。她的目光仍在打量揣摩着他。“拿回你的剑吧。”她终于开口。

他迈步欲取，旋即却停住了手。“旁人的剑，可都是您亲手交还的。”

“旁人岂能与你相提并论。如今法奇诺的衣钵已落到你肩上。贝拉里翁，这副衣钵，你打算披上几分？”

“主君意愿嘱托几分，我便承当几分。夫人方才已听闻他的遗嘱了。”

===Original===
“But not your own interpretation of it.”

“Have I not said that my life and services are at your command, as my lord, to whom I owe everything, enjoined upon me?”

“Your life and services,” she said slowly. Her breast heaved as if in repressed agitation. “That is much to offer, Bellarion. Do you ask nothing in return?”

“I offer these in return for all that I have received already. It is I who make payment, madonna.”

Again there was a baffled pause. She sighed heavily. “You make it hard for me, Bellarion.” There was a pathetic break in her voice.

“What do I make hard?”

===Chinese===
“却未听闻你自己的见解。”

“我方才岂非已经言明，谨遵主君遗命，我的性命与效力皆听凭您调遣？我平生所有，尽皆蒙他恩赐。”

“你的性命与效力，”她缓缓重复道，胸脯微微起伏，似在强抑着心潮翻涌，“贝拉里翁，你献出的筹码着实不轻。难道你就半点不求回报？”

“我所献上的，正是为了报答往日已受之恩。夫人，如今是我偿还恩情的时候。”

又是一阵令人无计可施的沉默。她重重叹了口气。“贝拉里翁，你叫我好生为难。”话音里透出一丝凄楚的哽咽。

“不知我叫夫人为难在何处？”

===Original===
She rose, and in evident timidity came to stand before him. She set a white hand on the black velvet sleeve of his tunic. Her lovely face, with which time had dealt so mercifully, was upturned to his, and there was now no arrogance in its lines or in her glance. She spoke quietly, wistfully.

“You may think, Bellarion, that with my lord scarce buried this is not the hour for﻿ ﻿… what I have to say. And yet, by the very fact of my lord’s death and by the very terms of his testament, this is the hour, because it must be the hour of decision. Here and now we must determine what is to follow.”

Tall and coldly stern he stood, looking down upon her who swayed a little there, so close to him that his nostrils were invaded by the subtle essences she used.

“I await your commands, madonna.”

“My commands? My commands? Dear God! What commands have I for you?” She looked away for an instant, then brought her eyes back to his face and her other hand to his other sleeve, so that she held him completely captive now. A faint colour stirred in the pale cheeks. “My lord has left me great possessions. They might serve as a footstool to help you mount to a great destiny.”

===Chinese===
她起身离座，显出几分羞怯之意，踱步站到他面前。她抬起一只白皙柔荑，轻轻按在他黑天鹅绒外袍的袖子上。那张备受岁月垂怜的娇艳面庞仰起来对着他，眉眼轮廓与顾盼之间，此刻已全无往日的骄矜傲慢。她轻声开口，语调幽幽带着几许怅惘。

“贝拉里翁，你兴许会觉得，主君入土方安，此时原不该讲……讲我接下来要说的话。然而，正因主君辞世，亦正因他遗嘱中的诸般条款，眼下反倒恰是时候——因为此刻正是必须决断的关头。日后局面该如何走，你我必须就在此地、就在当下定夺下来。”

他身姿修长，神情冷峻严毅，低头俯视着身前略略摇曳的她——她靠得那样近，身上熏染的幽微香露气息已直沁入他鼻端。

“谨候夫人训示。”

“我的训示？我的训示？天主啊！我能对你有什么训示？”她移开目光停了刹那，随即便将视线收回他脸上，另一只手也搭上了他的另一只衣袖，整个人宛若将他牢牢擒住一般。她苍白的脸颊上泛起一抹淡淡红晕。“主君留给了我广袤庞大的产业。这些基业，足可化作你脚下的踏脚石，扶助你登上何等辉煌的青云之路。”

===Original===
A little smile hovered about his lips as he looked down upon her who waited so breathlessly, her breast now touching his own.

“You are offering me﻿ ﻿…” he said, and stopped.

“Can you be in doubt of what I am offering? It is the hour of great decisions, Bellarion, for me and for you.” Closer she pressed, so that her weight was against him. She was deathly pale again, her eyes were veiled. “In unity is strength. That was Facino’s last reminder to us. And in what unity could there be greater strength than in ours? Facino’s army, the strongest that ever followed him, is solidly behind us so that we stand together. With that and my resources you need set no bounds to your ambition. You may be Duke of Milan if you will. You may even realise Galeazzo’s dream and make yourself King of Italy.”

His hovering smile settled and deepened. But the dark eyes grew sad.

“The world and you have never suspected,” he said gently, “that I am not really ambitious. You have witnessed my rise in four short years from a poor nameless, starveling scholar to knighthood, lordships, wealth, and fame; and, therefore, you imagine that I am one who has striven for the bounties of Fortune. It is not so, madonna. I have laboured for ends that are nowise bound up with the hope of any of these rewards, which I hold cheap. They are hollow vanities, empty bubbles, gewgaws to delight the children of the world. Possessions come to me, titles, honours, which deceive me no more than I desired them.”

She drew away from him a little, and looked at him almost in awe. “God! You talk like a monk!”

===Chinese===
看着眼前屏息凝神等待答复、此刻连胸口都已贴上他胸膛的女人，一抹浅笑悄然浮上他的唇角。

“夫人这是要赐予我……”他开口道，话到一半便收住了。

“我献上的是什么，你难道还会不明白吗？贝拉里翁，于我于你，这都是定夺干系重大的时刻。”她愈发贴近，将身子的重量都倚到了他身上。她脸色再度惨白如纸，双眸低垂掩住神光。“团结就是力量，这是法奇诺临终最后的叮咛。试问世间还有何种结合，能比你我携手更具力量？法奇诺麾下这支历来最为强盛的劲旅，正稳稳立于我们身后，只要你我并肩而立。凭此雄兵与我的财势，你的抱负便再无疆界可限。只要你愿意，便能坐上米兰公爵之位。你甚至能一圆加莱阿佐昔日的宏愿，自封为意大利国王！”

他唇畔那抹浅笑沉凝下来，愈发深邃；可那双深眸却渐渐染上几分凄清哀愁。

“世人与夫人恐怕从未料到，”他温和地说道，“我其实并无什么野心。您亲眼见证我不过短短四年光景，便从一个默默无闻、挨饿受冻的寒门学子，一步步获封骑士、坐拥采邑、兼得富贵与盛名；因此您便以为，我乃是为了追逐命运女神的垂青赏赐而苦心经营之人。并非如此，夫人。我奔波劳碌所图之事，原与这些虚名厚禄的指望毫不相干，在我眼里，这些原不值一提。它们不过是空洞的浮华、虚幻的泡影，是专供尘世顽童嬉戏欢喜的玩意儿罢了。田产、爵位、荣宠纵然落到我头上，我既不曾刻意祈求，也绝不会被它们迷了心窍。”

她往后略略退开半步，近乎敬畏地端详着他。“天主啊！你这番话简直像个修士！”

===Original===
“It is possible that I think like one, and very natural remembering how I was nurtured. There is one task, one purpose which has detained me in this world of men. When that is accomplished, I think I shall go back to the cell where there is peace.”

“You!” Her hands had fallen from his arms. She gasped now in her amazement. “With the world at your feet if you choose! To renounce all? To go back to the chill loneliness and joylessness of monkhood? Bellarion, you are mad.”

“Or else sane, madonna. Who shall judge?”

“And love, Bellarion? Is there no love in the world? Does that not lend reality to all these things that you deem shams?”

“Does it heal the vanity of the world?” he cried. “It is a great power, as I perceive. For love men will go mad, they will become beasts: they will murder and betray.”

“Heretic!”

===Chinese===
“我所思所想兴许确与修士无异，念及我自幼受教养的出处，这原也再自然不过。这尘世间唯有一件事、一个夙愿羁绊着我。待此事了结，我想我终归还是要回到那方清静安宁的修院斗室中去。”

“你！”她的双手早已从他臂膀滑落，此刻惊愕得倒抽一口凉气，“只要你肯点头，整座天下便踩在你脚下！你竟要尽数抛却？竟要重回那孤寂清冷、毫无欢愉可言的苦修生涯？贝拉里翁，你简直疯了。”

“抑或是独醒也未可知，夫人。此事又有谁能评断？”

“那情爱呢，贝拉里翁？世上难道就没有爱了吗？难道它不能为你眼中这些虚幻假象赋予真切实在的滋味吗？”

“它难道就能医治尘世的虚妄么？”他高声反问道，“依我看来，爱确是一股巨大的力量。为了爱，人会发狂，会沦为禽兽：他们会行凶杀人，也会背信弃义。”

“异端！”

===Original===
That startled him a little. Once before he had been dubbed heretic for beliefs to which he clung with assurance; and experience had come to lay bare his heresy to his own eyes.

“Upon occasion, madonna, we have talked of love, you and I. Had I given heed, had your beauty beglamoured me, what a treacherous thing should I not have been in Facino’s eyes! Do you wonder that I mistrust love as I mistrust all else the world can offer me?”

“While Facino lived, that﻿ ﻿…” She broke off. Her eyes were on the ground, her hands now folded in her lap. She had drawn away from him a little and leaned against the table’s edge. “Now﻿ ﻿…” She parted her hands and held them out, leaving him to guess her mind.

“Now his behests are upon me, and they shall be obeyed as if he still lived.”

“What is there in his behests against﻿ ﻿… against what I was offering? Am I not commended to you by his testament? Am I not a part of his legacy to you?”

“The service of you is; and your loyal servant, madonna, you shall ever find me.” She turned aside with a little gesture of irritation, and remained silent, thoughtful.

===Chinese===
这个字眼教他心头微微一震。早年间，他也曾因固守自己笃信不疑的信条而被人斥为异端；而日后的亲身历练，终究让他自己看清了那份偏执谬见。

“夫人，往昔您我也曾数度谈及情爱。倘若当日我动了凡心，倘若我被您的绝色容颜迷了心智，那在法奇诺眼中，我岂不成了个忘恩负义的奸贼？如此一来，我对情爱心存戒惧，一如我对尘世所能赐予的其余一切都心怀戒备，难道还值得奇怪么？”

“法奇诺在世之时，那自当……”她话语顿住，低垂视线盯着地面，双手交叠垂在腹前。她又往后退了些许，斜倚在长案边沿。“可如今……”她摊开双手伸向身前，余意尽在不言之中，留待他自己去领会。

“如今他的遗命在肩，我自当奉行不渝，宛如他尚在人世一般。”

“他的遗命之中，究竟哪一条有违……有违我方才相许之情？他立下的遗嘱，岂非将我托付给了你？我岂非也是他留给你的那份遗产中的一桩？”

“效忠护持夫人确在遗命之中；而我永远都会是夫人忠心耿耿的臣仆。”她懊恼地微一摆手转过身去，默然立在原地，沉吟不语。

===Original===
A sleek secretary broke in upon them. The Count of Pavia commanded the Lord Bellarion’s presence in the library. A courier had just arrived from Milan with grave news.

“Say to his highness that I come.”

The secretary withdrew.

“You give me leave, madonna?”

She stood leaning sideways against the heavy table, her face averted. “Aye, you may go.” Her voice rasped.

===Chinese===
一名举止油滑的秘书恰在此时闯入，打断了两人。原来是帕维亚伯爵传唤贝拉里翁大人即刻前往藏书室，刚有信使自米兰飞马抵此，带来了紧要军情。

“去禀告殿下，我即刻便到。”

秘书躬身退下。

“夫人容我告退么？”

她侧身倚着沉重的长案，偏过脸去不看他。“去吧，你走便是。”她的嗓音干涩暗哑。

===Original===
But he waited yet a moment. “The sword, madonna? Will you not arm me with your own hands for your service?”

She turned her head to look at him again, and there was now a curl of disdain on her pale lips.

“I thought you looked askance on symbols. Was not that your profession?” She paused, but, without waiting for his answer, added: “Take up your sword, yourself, you that are so fully master of your own destinies.”

And on that she turned and went, trailing her funereal draperies over the gay mosaics of that patterned floor.

He remained where she left him until she had passed out of that great hall and the door had closed. Then, at last, he fetched a sigh and went to restore his blade to its scabbard.

===Chinese===
然而他却又站定了片刻。“这柄剑呢，夫人？您不愿亲手替我佩上剑，好教我为您效力么？”

她回过头来再次看向他，苍白的唇边此刻已挑起一抹轻蔑的冷笑。

“我倒以为你最瞧不上什么虚礼表记呢。方才你不是亲口这般宣称的么？”她略顿了顿，却不等他回答，便接着冷冷道，“你自己把剑拿起来吧——像你这样把自家命运攥得丝毫不差的人，原也用不着旁人代劳。”

说罢她转身拂袖而去，宽大的丧服拖曳过那片花纹斑斓、色泽明丽的马赛克地砖，发出沙沙轻响。

他立在原地一动不动，直待她走出那座宏阔大厅、房门轰然阖上，这才长叹一声，上前拾起长剑归入鞘中。

===Original===
His thoughts were on Facino hardly cold in the grave, on this widow who had so shamelessly wooed him, yet in terms which demanded as a condition the satisfaction of her inordinate ambition; and lastly on that obese young Prince who waited for him. And in the mirror of his mind he saw a reflection of a scene now some months old. He saw again the glance of those beady, lecherous eyes lambent about Facino’s Countess.

Inspiration came to him of how best he might gratify her vast ambition, her greed of greatness. Her suggestion to him had been that he should make her Duchess of Milan, and Duchess of Milan he would make her yet.

On that half-ironic thought he came to the library where the Prince waited. Filippo Maria was seated at a table near one of the windows. Spread before him were some parchments, writing-materials, and a horn of unicorn that was almost a yard long, of solid ivory, one of the library’s most treasured possessions.

The Prince was more than usually pallid, his glance unsteady, his manner nervous and agitated. Perfunctorily he made the inquiries concerning the obsequies of Facino which courtesy demanded. He reiterated excuses already made for his own absence from the ceremony, an absence really based on resentment of the yoke which Facino had imposed upon him. That done, he picked up a parchment from the table.

===Chinese===
他心头萦绕着尸骨未寒的法奇诺，想着这位寡妇方才竟如此毫无廉耻地向他示爱求欢，开出的价码却又偏是要满足她那贪得无厌的野心；最后，他想到了此刻正候着自己的那位肥胖少年王爷。在他脑海的明镜之中，骤然浮现出几个月前的一幕旧景：他又一次瞧见那双绿豆般细小的色欲之眼，正垂涎闪烁地逡巡在法奇诺伯爵夫人的身段之上。

灵光陡然一闪，他立时想出了一条妙计，正可十全十美地遂了她那膨胀的野心与攀附权贵的贪欲。她方才曾明示他，要他扶她当上米兰公爵夫人——好极了，他偏要如她所愿，把她推上米兰公爵夫人的宝座。

怀着这半带讥诮的念头，他步入了王爷久候的藏书室。菲利波·玛丽亚正坐在靠窗的一张桌案后。案上摊着几卷羊皮纸、一套书写文具，还有一支将近一码长的实心象牙独角兽角——那是整座藏书室最为珍贵的宝物之一。

这位少年王爷的脸色比往常更加苍白，眼神飘忽不定，举止间透着焦躁与惶恐。他按礼数敷衍着问了几句法奇诺葬仪的情形，又将自己缺席丧礼的托辞反复申说了一遍——实则他之不去，不过是心怀宿怨，恼恨法奇诺生前套在他头上的重重枷锁罢了。寒暄敷衍既毕，他从桌上拿起一卷羊皮纸。

===Original===
“Here’s news,” he said, and his voice trembled. “Estorre Visconti has been created Duke of Milan.” He paused, and the little dark eyes blinked up at the tall Bellarion standing composed at his side. “You knew already?”

“Not so, highness.”

“And you show no surprise?”

“It is a bold step, and it may cost Messer Estorre his head. But it was to be expected from what had gone before.”

The beady eyes returned to the parchment, which shook in the podgy fingers.

“Fra Berto Caccia, the Bishop of Piacenza, preached a sermon to the people lauding the murder of my brother, and promising in Estorre’s name a Golden Age for Milan, with immunity from taxation. Thereupon they laid at his bastard feet the keys of the city, the standard of the republic, and the ducal sceptre.” He dropped the parchment, and sat back folding plump, white hands across his paunch. “This calls for action, speedily.”

===Chinese===
“出大事了，”他开口道，嗓音直发颤，“埃斯托雷·维斯孔蒂已经被立为米兰公爵了。”他略一停顿，一双细小的黑眼珠眨巴着仰望身旁神色沉静、身形颀长的贝拉里翁。“你早就知道了？”

“并未听闻，殿下。”

“你倒毫不吃惊？”

“此举着实胆大妄为，弄不好会叫埃斯托雷先生掉了脑袋。不过顺着先前那些事由推演下来，这也原在意料之中。”

那双绿豆眼重新落回羊皮纸上，纸卷在他肥胖短粗的手指间微微抖动。

“皮亚琴察主教贝尔托·卡恰修士（Fra Berto Caccia）向百姓布道，竟大肆赞颂杀害我兄长之举，又以埃斯托雷的名义许诺为米兰带来免除赋税的黄金时代。百姓受此蛊惑，当即将城门钥匙、共和国旗帜以及公爵权杖一并捧到了那个私生子脚下。”他丢开羊皮纸，往椅背上一靠，将白胖的双手交叠在隆起的肚腩上。“此事刻不容缓，须得火速发兵！”

===Original===
“We can provide action enough to surfeit Messer Estorre.”

“Ha!” The great flabby face grew almost kindly, the little eyes beamed upon the condottiero. “Serve me well in this, Bellarion, and you shall know gratitude.”

Bellarion’s gesture seemed to wave the notion of reward aside. He came straight to facts. “We can withdraw eight thousand men from Bergamo. The place is at the point of surrender, and four thousand will well suffice to tighten the last grip upon the Malatesta vitals. Perhaps the Lord Estorre has not included that in his calculations. With eight thousand men we can sweep him out of Milan at our pleasure.”

“And you’ll give orders? You’ll give orders at once? The army, they tell me, is now in your control. Facino’s authority has descended to you, and has been accepted by your brother captains.”

And now this arch-dissembler went to work.

===Chinese===
“我们大可给他送去一场战事，管叫埃斯托雷先生吃个饱。”

“呵！”他那张肥大松垮的脸庞顿时舒展开几分和颜悦色，一双小眼睛笑眯眯地望着这位雇佣兵统帅，“贝拉里翁，此事若能替我办妥，本王自当厚报你的功劳。”

贝拉里翁微微抬手，似是将封赏的念头挥诸脑后，径直切入正题。“眼下我们可从贝加莫抽调八千兵马。那座城已到垂死乞降的边缘，仅留四千人便足可扼紧马拉泰斯塔的咽喉，待其毙命。埃斯托雷大人打的算盘里，兴许尚未把这支兵力算进去。手握八千精兵，我们随时皆可将他扫出米兰。”

“那你这就下令？这就即刻传令调兵？众人皆言，大军如今已在你掌控之中。法奇诺的权柄已传予你手，诸位同袍将领也都服你号令。”

此刻，这位工于心计、深藏不露的伪装大师开始施展手段了。

===Original===
“Hardly so much, highness. Facino’s captains have sworn fealty, not to me, but to the Lady Beatrice.”

“But﻿ ﻿… But you, then?” The news dismayed him a little. “What place is yours?”

“At your highness’s side, if your highness commands me.”

“Yes, yes. But whom do you command? Where, exactly, do you stand now?”

“At the head of the army in any enterprise into which the Countess sends her captains.”

“The Countess?” The Prince shifted his bulk uneasily in his chair, slewing round so as to face the soldier more fully. “What then if﻿ ﻿… What if the Countess should not﻿ ﻿…” He waved his fat hands helplessly.

===Chinese===
“恐怕远非如此，殿下。法奇诺麾下诸将宣誓效忠的对象并非是我，而是贝阿特丽切夫人。”

“可……可那你呢？”这消息令他微感惊惶，“那你又处于何等地位？”

“只要殿下一声令下，臣自当常侍殿下左右。”

“是，是。可你究竟能调动谁？眼下你在军中究竟算作什么位置？”

“但凡伯爵夫人遣派麾下诸将出征，我便率领大军冲锋陷阵。”

“伯爵夫人？”王爷在椅上不安地挪动着肥胖的身躯，斜转过身来，好正对着这位武将，“那倘若……倘若伯爵夫人不肯……”他无助地挥了挥两只肥厚的手掌。

===Original===
“It is not likely that the Countess should oppose your own wishes, highness.”

“Not likely? But﻿—Lord of Heaven!﻿—it’s possible.” He heaved himself up, nervous, agitated. “I must know. I must﻿ ﻿… I’ll send for her.” He reached for a hand-bell on the table.

But Bellarion’s hand closed over his own before he could ring.

“A moment, Lord Prince. Before you send for the Lady Beatrice, had you not best consider precisely what you will say to her?”

“What is to say beyond discovering her disposition towards me.”

“Can you entertain a doubt upon that, Lord Prince?” Bellarion was smiling. Their hands came away together from the bell, and fell apart. “Her disposition towards your potency is, to my knowledge, of the very kindliest. Such, indeed, that﻿—I’ll be frank with you﻿—I found it necessary once to remind her of her duty to her lord.”

===Chinese===
“伯爵夫人应当不至于违逆殿下的心意。”

“不至于？可——老天爷在上！——万一她真不肯呢？”他心神不宁、焦灼万分地挣扎着起身，“我必须探个明白。我得……我这就传她进来。”说着便伸手去拿桌上的手摇铃。

可铃尚未摇响，贝拉里翁的手已稳稳按住了他的手背。

“且慢，王爷。在传召贝阿特丽切夫人之前，殿下岂不该先仔细斟酌一下，究竟要同她说些什么么？”

“除了探一探她对本王究竟怀着什么心思，还有什么好说的。”

“王爷对此难道还存有半分疑虑么？”贝拉里翁唇边含笑，两人手掌一齐从摇铃上撤回，各自垂下，“她对殿下您的情意，据我所知，着实热络温存得很。实不相瞒——她当年那般情意，甚至逼得我一度不得不出言提醒她莫忘了身为贵妇人的本分。”

===Original===
“Ah!” The fat pale face quivered into something akin to malevolence. The Prince remembered a sudden coolness in the Countess and her removal to Melegnano, and perceived in this meddler’s confession the explanation of it. “By Saint Ambrose, that was bold of you!”

“I am accounted bold,” Bellarion reminded him, deeming it necessary.

“Aye, aye!” The shifty eyes fell away uncomfortably under his glance. “But if she is kindly disposed, then﻿ ﻿…”

“I know that she was, highness, and may be rendered so again. Though perhaps less easily now than heretofore.”

“Less easily? Why so?”

“As Facino’s widow, she is in wealth and power the equal of many a prince in Italy. She has considerable dominions﻿ ﻿…”

===Chinese===
“哦！”那张肥硕苍白的脸庞微微一颤，浮出一丝近乎怨毒的阴狠神色。王爷登时想起伯爵夫人当年陡然转冷、随即移居梅莱尼亚诺的旧事，从眼前这个多事之徒的坦白里，他总算明白了前因后果。“凭圣安布罗斯起誓，你这胆子可真不小！”

“世人原也向来夸我胆大，”贝拉里翁觉得有必要提醒他一句。

“那是，那是！”那双游移不定的小眼珠在他的注视下局促地避了开去，“不过，既然她对本王情意深厚，那……”

“臣知道她往日确是如此，殿下，日后也未尝不能重拾旧情。只是如今再想让她回心转意，恐怕不如从前那般容易了。”

“不如从前容易？此话怎讲？”

“身为法奇诺的遗孀，她如今论财势权柄，足以与意大利诸多邦君王侯比肩。她手握广袤领地……”

===Original===
“Torn by Facino from the great heritage left by the Duke my father.” In that rare burst of indignation his whole bulk quivered like a great jelly.

“They might be restored to the ducal crown by peaceful arts.”

“Peaceful arts? What arts? Will you be plain?”

But the time for direct answers was not yet. “And not only has the Countess lands, but the control of a vast fortune. Some four hundred thousand ducats. You will need money, highness, for the pay of this great army now under Bergamo, and your own treasury will hardly supply it. There is taxation. But your highness knows the ills that wait on that for a prince newly come into his own. And not only the lands and money of which your highness stands in need, but the men also does the Countess bring.”

“You but repeat yourself.”

===Chinese===
“全都是法奇诺从先父公爵留下的偌大家业里强抢去的！”这罕见的一阵激愤，令他那副肥硕身躯宛如一大团肉冻般剧烈颤抖起来。

“这些失地，大可借平和的怀柔手段重归公爵冕下。”

“平和的怀柔手段？什么手段？你把话说痛快些！”

然而挑明话头的时机尚未成熟。“不仅如此，伯爵夫人坐拥的何止广袤封土，更执掌着一笔泼天巨财，足有四十万杜卡特金币之数。殿下眼下急需银钱来发放贝加莫城下那支大军的军饷，而您的府库恐怕捉襟见肘，难以支应。诚然可以加征赋税，但殿下自知，一位新近继统的君主若贸然横征暴敛，必将招致何等祸患。伯爵夫人所能献上的，不仅是殿下亟需的城池与金钱，更有那支如虎添翼的雄兵。”

“你不过是把刚才的话又重复了一遍。”

===Original===
Bellarion looked at him, and smiled. “Never, do I believe, did a Prince find a bride more richly dowered.”

“A bride?” The youth was startled, terrified almost. “A bride?”

“Would less content your highness? Would you be satisfied to receive the assistance of the Countess’s possessions, when you may make them your own and wield them at your pleasure?”

He stared, his jaw fallen. Then slowly he brought his lips together again, and licked them thoughtfully, screwing up his mean eyes.

“You are proposing that I should take to wife Facino’s widow, who is twice my age?” He asked the question very slowly, as if pondering each word of it.

===Chinese===
贝拉里翁望着他，嘴角含笑。“普天之下，恐怕从未有过哪位王侯，能觅得陪嫁如此丰厚的新娘。”

“新娘？”这青年大吃一惊，简直骇得魂不附体，“新娘？！”

“难道退而求其次便能叫殿下称心么？明明可以将伯爵夫人的全部家业尽收己有、随心所欲地调度驱使，您难道倒甘心只求她借出一臂之力？”

他目瞪口呆地盯着贝拉里翁，下巴险些掉下来。接着，他缓缓合拢双唇，一边若有所思地舔了舔嘴角，一边将那双狡诈寒酸的小眼睛眯成了一道缝。

“你的意思是，要我迎娶法奇诺那个年岁足抵我两倍的遗孀为妻？”他问得极为缓慢，仿佛字字句句都在反复咀嚼掂量。

===Original===
Bellarion laughed. “Not proposing it, highness. It is not for me to make such proposals. I do not even know what the lady will say. But if she is willing to become Duchess of Milan, she can provide the means to make you Duke.”

Filippo Maria sat down suddenly. The sweat broke from his pale brow. He mopped it with his hand, disturbing the black fringe that disfigured it. Then, lost in thought, he stroked the loose folds of his enormous chin, and gradually his eyes kindled.

At long length he put forth his hand again to the bell. This time Bellarion did not interfere. He perceived in the act the young Prince’s surrender to the forces of greed and lust which Bellarion himself had loosed against him.

He took his leave, and went out with the sad knowledge that greed and wantonness would make of the woman, too, a ready prey.

His work was done. She should have the thing she coveted, and find in it her punishment﻿ ﻿…

===Chinese===
贝拉里翁轻笑一声。“并非臣下提议，殿下。这等终身大事，臣下岂敢僭越建言。甚至连夫人本人意下如何，臣下也一概不知。但倘若她有心坐上米兰公爵夫人之位，她手中握着的资财兵甲，却正足以助您登上米兰公爵的宝座。”

菲利波·玛丽亚颓然跌坐回椅中，苍白的额角渗出豆大的冷汗。他抬手胡乱揩去汗水，揉乱了额前那片有碍观瞻的黑刘海。继而他陷入深思，手指摩挲着硕大下颌垂坠的层层赘肉，那双眼睛渐渐燃起了幽光。

良久，他再度伸手去拿那个手摇铃。这一次，贝拉里翁没有拦阻。他从这个举动里清清楚楚地看出，这位少年王爷已然彻底臣服于由他亲手纵放出来的贪婪与淫欲。

他躬身告辞，缓步退了出去，心下怀着一抹凄清的了然：贪欲与淫佚，同样会将那个女人变成任人摆布的猎物。

他的差事已毕。她终将如愿以偿地得到她梦寐以求的一切——并在其中，领受属于她的惩罚……

## VII Prince of Valsassina / 第七章 瓦尔萨西纳亲王

===Original===
As Bellarion had calculated and disposed, so things fell out, and Filippo Maria Visconti in the twenty-second year of his age led to the altar the widowed Countess of Biandrate who was thirty-nine. As a young girl, she had married, at the bidding of ambition, a man who was twenty years her senior; as a middle-aged woman now, and for the same reason, she married one who was almost as much her junior. She had not the foresight to perceive that the grievance on the score of disparity of years which she had nursed against Facino would be nursed against herself to her ultimate destruction by this sly, furtive, and cruel Prince to whom now she gave herself and her vast possessions. That, however, is no part of the story I have set myself to tell.

Estorre Visconti defended in vain his usurped dominion against Gian Maria’s legitimate successor. Filippo Maria, with Carmagnola in command of some seven thousand men, laid siege to Milan, whilst Bellarion went north to make an end of the Bergamo resistance. Because in haste to have done, he granted Malatesta easy terms of surrender, permitting him to ride out of the city with the honours of war, lance on thigh. Thereafter, having restored order in Bergamo and left there a strong garrison under an officer of trust, he marched with the main army to join Filippo Maria who was conducting operations from the mills on Monte Lupario, three miles from Milan. Some four weeks already had he spent there, with little progress made. Estorre had enrolled and constrained to the defence of the city almost every man of an age to bear arms. It was necessary to make an end, and Bellarion himself with a few followers entered the Castle of Porta Giovia which was being held against Estorre by Vimercati, the castellan. From its walls, having attracted the people by trumpet-blast, he published Filippo Maria’s proclamation, wherein the Prince solemnly undertook that if the city were at once surrendered to him it should have nothing to fear; that there should be no pillage, executions, or other measures punitive of this resistance to the State’s legitimate lord.

The news flew in every direction, with the result that before nightfall all those whom Estorre had constrained to follow him had fallen away, and he was left with only his mercenaries. With these, next morning, he hacked a way out through the Comasina Gate as the people were throwing open to the new Duke the gates of the city on the other side.

Filippo Maria entered with a comparatively small following and in the wake of a train of bread-carts sent ahead to relieve the famine which already was beginning to press upon the inhabitants. The acclamations of “Live the Duke!” quieted his natural timidity as he rode through the streets to shut himself up in the Castle of Porta Giovia, which remained ever afterwards his residence. Not for Filippo Maria the Palace of the Old Broletto or the gaiety of courts. His dark, scheming, yet pusillanimous nature craved the security of a stronghold.

===Chinese===
果如贝拉里翁所筹划与安排的那般，事情一一应验：二十二岁的菲利波·玛丽亚·维斯孔蒂挽着三十九岁的比安德拉泰伯爵寡居夫人步入了教堂圣坛。少女时代，她顺从野心的驱使，嫁给了一位比她年长二十岁的男子；如今步入中年，她又出于同样的缘由，嫁给了一位几乎同样比她年轻那么多岁的男子。她却没有远见去洞察，当年她自己因年龄悬殊而对法奇诺积郁于心的怨怼，日后也会被眼前这位阴鸷、诡谲而残忍的亲王积郁在心，反过来把连人带庞大家产一起交托给他的她推向毁灭的深渊。不过，这并非我要讲述的故事。

埃斯托雷·维斯孔蒂妄图抵御吉安·玛丽亚的合法继承人，死守自己窃据的领地，终究只是徒劳。菲利波·玛丽亚由卡尔马尼奥拉率领约七千兵马围攻米兰，与此同时，贝拉里翁北上平定贝加莫的抵抗。因急于了结战事，他给了马拉泰斯塔宽厚的投降条件，准许他依循战阵荣典、持枪抵胯骑马出城。此后，他在贝加莫重整秩序，留下一名亲信将领统率重兵驻守，随即率主力大军南下，与菲利波·玛丽亚会师——后者当时正驻扎在距米兰三英里外的卢帕里奥山（Monte Lupario）水磨坊一带指挥战事。他在那里已耗了约莫四周，却寸功未立。埃斯托雷把城里几乎所有适龄男丁尽数征召入伍，逼迫他们守城死战。必须速作决断了；于是贝拉里翁亲率数名随从，潜入正由城堡总管维梅尔卡蒂（Vimercati）据守以抗衡埃斯托雷的波尔塔焦维亚城堡。他登上城墙，命人吹响号角引来城中百姓，当众宣读菲利波·玛丽亚的谕令：亲王在谕令中郑重承诺，只要全城立刻归降，百姓便绝无任何可惧之处；绝不纵兵劫掠，绝不滥行处决，亦绝不因民众先前抗拒邦国合法君主而采取任何报复惩戒之举。

消息顿时传遍四方。结果未至黄昏，所有被埃斯托雷强征入伍的市民便纷纷散去，他身边只剩下区区雇佣兵。次日清晨，当城中百姓在另一侧大开城门迎候新公爵之际，埃斯托雷率领这批残部从科马西纳门（Comasina Gate）硬生生杀出一条血路逃之夭夭。

菲利波·玛丽亚带着一支规模不大的随从队进城，走在先行派去赈济城中已然初现饥荒的漫长面包车队后头。百姓山呼“公爵万岁！”的欢呼声，抚平了他天性中的怯懦；他一路策马穿过街巷，径直走进波尔塔焦维亚城堡闭门不出，此后终身便以此为居所。旧布罗莱托宫的浮华与宫廷的欢宴，向来不合菲利波·玛丽亚的胃口。他那阴沉、多谋却又怯懦多疑的本性，渴求的唯有坚固要塞所赐予的安稳。

===Original===
For assisting him to the ducal throne, and no doubt to ensure their continued support, he rewarded his captains generously, and none more generously than Bellarion to whom he considered that he owed everything. Bellarion was not only confirmed in the lordship of Valsassina in feud, for himself and his heirs forever, but the Duke raised the fief into a principality.

Bellarion remained the Duke’s marshal in chief and military adviser, and it was by the dispositions which he made during that summer and autumn of 1412 that the lands of the duchy were finally cleared of the insurgent brigands who had renewed their depredations.

Peace being restored at home, and industry being liberated at last from the trammels that had lain upon it since the death of Gian Galeazzo, prosperity flowed swiftly back to the State of Milan, and the people heaped blessings upon the shy, furtive ruler of whom they saw so little.

It is possible that Filippo Maria would have been content to rest for the present upon what was done, to leave the frontiers of the duchy as he found them, and to dismiss the greater part of the costly condottas in his employ. But Bellarion at his elbow goaded him to further enterprise, and met his sluggish reluctance with a culminating argument that shamed him into action.

“Will you leave, in tranquil possession, the brigands who have encroached upon the glorious patrimony built up by your illustrious father? Will you dishonour his memory and be false to your name, Lord Duke?”

Thus, and similarly, Bellarion, with a heat that was purely histrionic. He cared no more for the integrity of Gian Galeazzo’s patrimony than he cared for that of the Kingdom of England. What he cared for was that the order to dispossess those tyrants would sound the knell of Theodore of Montferrat. Thus, at last, should he be enabled to complete the service, to which five years ago he had dedicated himself, and to which unfalteringly, if obscurely and tortuously, he had held. Very patiently had he waited for this hour, when, yielding at last to his bold importunities, the Duke summoned a council of the officers of State and the chief condottieri to determine the order in which action should be taken.

===Chinese===
为酬谢麾下诸将扶立公爵大位之功——自然也是为了确保他们日后继续效忠——菲利波·玛丽亚大加赏赐，而受赏最厚者莫过于他自认将一切功业尽归其身的贝拉里翁。公爵不仅以世袭采邑之名，将瓦尔萨西纳领主之位正式确认授予贝拉里翁及其子孙永世承袭，更将这块采邑升格为亲王国。

贝拉里翁继续出任公爵的三军总元帅兼军事枢密。正是凭借他在 1412 年夏秋两季的周密调度，公国境内那些死灰复燃、肆行劫掠的叛乱匪帮才得以彻底肃清。

国内既已重归安宁，工商业也终于摆脱了自吉安·加莱阿佐逝世以来一直压在头上的种种桎梏，繁盛气象迅速重返米兰邦国；百姓们纷纷为这位深居简出、行迹隐秘而少见真容的君主祈福颂德。

若依菲利波·玛丽亚自己的心思，或许眼下便满足于现状了：将公国疆界维持在接手时的模样，再把靡费甚巨的雇佣兵团遣散大半。然而近在身侧的贝拉里翁却步步催逼，激他再展宏图，并以一记直击要害的诘问，迫得那拖沓怯战的公爵无地自容，只得下定决心：

“难道您竟要听任那些强盗安稳霸占您英明先父毕生缔造的辉煌基业吗？公爵大人，您难道甘心辱没先父英名、有负维斯孔蒂的姓氏吗？”

贝拉里翁就这样言辞激切地反复劝谏，那满腔热忱却纯然是演出来的戏码。他对吉安·加莱阿佐遗产是否完整，并不比对英格兰王国的疆土更上心。他在乎的，唯有那道驱逐僭主群盗的军令一旦颁下，便将敲响蒙费拉托的西奥多的丧钟。如此一来，五年前他立誓效命的那桩夙愿——那桩他虽行迹晦暗、曲折迂回却始终矢志不渝追寻的事业——终于能画上圆满的句号。他极其耐心地守候着这一刻的降临；如今公爵终于屈从于他大胆而不懈的恳请，召集国务重臣与诸位主要雇佣兵统帅共商军机，议定各路出兵的先后次序。

===Original===
At once Bellarion urged that a beginning should be made by recovering Vercelli, than which few strongholds were of more importance to the safety of the duchy.

It provoked a protest from Beccarla, who was the Duke’s Minister of State.

“An odd proposal this from you, Lord Bellarion, remembering that it was by your own action in concert with the Count of Biandrate that the Marquis Theodore was placed in possession of Vercelli.”

Bellarion crushed him with his logic. “Not odd, sir, natural. Then I was on the other side. And if, being on the other side, I conceived it important that Theodore should hold Vercelli, now that I am opposed to him I conceive it equally important that he should be driven from it.”

===Chinese===
贝拉里翁当即力陈，首战应当直取韦尔切利——论及公国安危，世上鲜有要塞比它更为紧要。

这话立时引来了公爵的国务大臣贝卡拉（Beccarla）的抗议。

“贝拉里翁大人，这话从您口中说出来可真是蹊跷。别忘了，当年正是您亲自与比安德拉泰伯爵联手合谋，才把韦尔切利拱手送到西奥多侯爵手中的。”

贝拉里翁以无懈可击的逻辑瞬间将他驳倒。“并不蹊跷，阁下，实乃顺理成章。当年我站在另一边。既然我站在另一边时，深知西奥多据有韦尔切利何等紧要；那么如今我站在他的对立面，自然也同样深知将他逐出该城何等紧要。”

===Original===
There was a pause. Filippo Maria, somnolent in his great chair, looked round the group. “What is the military view?” he asked. He had noticed that not one of the captains had voiced an opinion. He was answered now by the burly Koenigshofen.

“I have no views that are not Bellarion’s. I have followed him long enough to know that he’s a safe man to follow.”

Giasone Trotta, uninvited, expressed the same sentiment. Filippo Maria turned to Carmagnola, who sat silent and thoughtful.

“And you, sir?” he asked.

Carmagnola reared his blond head, and Bellarion braced himself for battle. But to his amazement, for once﻿—for the first time in their long association﻿—Carmagnola was on his side.

“I am of Bellarion’s mind, magnificent. We who were with my Lord Facino when he made alliance with Theodore of Montferrat know Theodore for a crafty, daring man of boundless ambition. His occupation of Vercelli is a menace to the peace of the duchy.”

===Chinese===
席间一时静了下来。昏昏欲睡地靠在高背大椅里的菲利波·玛丽亚环视众人。“军中诸将意下如何？”他问道。他早就留意到，在座的雇佣兵队长竟无一人开口表态。此刻率先作答的，是身材敦实的柯尼希斯霍芬。

“贝拉里翁怎么看，我就怎么看，别无他议。我追随他已经够久了，深知跟着他走绝不会出错。”

贾索内·特罗塔（Giasone Trotta）不等点名，便随声附和。菲利波·玛丽亚于是转向一直默然沉思的卡尔马尼奥拉。

“那么阁下呢？”他问道。

卡尔马尼奥拉抬起那一头金发，贝拉里翁暗自绷紧心弦准备迎战。然而令他大感惊愕的是，这一次——也是二人漫长共事生涯中的头一遭——卡尔马尼奥拉竟然站到了他这一边。

“臣与贝拉里翁所见略同，殿下。当年法奇诺大人与蒙费拉托的西奥多结盟之时，我等皆在阵中，深知西奥多此人狡诈大胆、野心无边。他盘踞韦尔切利，实乃公国安宁的心腹大患。”

===Original===
After that the other captains, Valperga and Marsilio, who had been wavering, threw in their votes, so that the military opinion was solidly unanimous.

Filippo Maria balanced the matter for a moment.

“You are not forgetting, sirs, that for Theodore’s good behaviour I have in my hands a precious hostage, in the person of his nephew, the Marquis Gian Giacomo, in whose name Theodore rules. You laugh, Bellarion!”

“That hostage was procured to ensure, not the good faith of Theodore, but the safety of the real Prince of Montferrat. Carmagnola has told your magnificence that Theodore is crafty, daring, and ambitious. It is a part of his ambition to make himself absolute sovereign where at present he is no more than Regent. Let your magnificence judge if the thought of harm to the hostage you hold would be a deterrent to him.”

A while still they debated. Then Filippo Maria announced that he would take thought and make known his decision when it was reached. On that he dismissed them.

===Chinese===
此言既出，原本摇摆不定的另外两位将领瓦尔佩尔加（Valperga）与马尔西利奥（Marsilio）也纷纷附议赞同，军中诸将的意见遂铁板一块、毫无异议。

菲利波·玛丽亚权衡了片刻。

“诸位莫非忘了，为防西奥多蠢动，本爵手里还握着一件贵重人质——便是他的侄儿吉安·贾科莫侯爵，西奥多如今正是打着他的旗号摄政当国。贝拉里翁，你笑什么！”

“当初扣下那位人质，原不是为了担保西奥多守信，而是为了保全蒙费拉托真正君主的性命。卡尔马尼奥拉方才也禀明殿下，西奥多狡诈、胆大而又野心勃勃。他野心所图，正是要把自己如今不过暂代的摄政之位，变成大权独揽的真君之位。请殿下圣裁：您手中那名人质的安危，又怎能令他有所顾忌？”

众人又议论了一阵。随后菲利波·玛丽亚宣布自己尚需斟酌，待决断已定自会昭告众人，说罢便散了朝会。

===Original===
As they went from the council chamber the captains witnessed the phenomenon of a yet closer unity between Bellarion and Carmagnola. The new Prince of Valsassina linked arms with Francesco Busone, and drew him away.

“You will do a service in this matter, Ser Francesco, if you send word to Lady Valeria and her brother urging them to come at once to Milan and petition the Duke to place Gian Giacomo upon his throne. He is of full age, and only his absence from Montferrat enables Theodore to continue in the Regency.”

Carmagnola looked at him suspiciously. “Why do you not send that message, yourself?”

Bellarion shrugged and spread his hands a little. “I have not the confidence of the Princess. A message from me might be mistrusted.”

Carmagnola’s fine blue eyes pondered him still with that suspicious glance. “What game do you play?” he asked.

“I see that you mistrust me, too.”

===Chinese===
诸将走出议事厅时，亲眼见着了一桩奇景：贝拉里翁与卡尔马尼奥拉竟愈发亲密无间。这位新封的瓦尔萨西纳亲王亲热地挽起弗朗切斯科·布索内（Francesco Busone）的手臂，将他拉到一旁。

“弗朗切斯科先生，此事若由你递信给瓦莱里娅小姐与她弟弟，催促他们火速赶来米兰，呈请公爵扶立吉安·贾科莫重登君位，那可真是立了一桩大功。他已然成年，全因身在蒙费拉托之外，才让西奥多得以继续把持摄政大权。”

卡尔马尼奥拉狐疑地打量着他。“你自己何不派人送信去？”

贝拉里翁耸了耸肩，微微摊开双手。“我素来不得公主殿下信任。若是我送去的口信，她多半会起疑心。”

卡尔马尼奥拉那双漂亮的蓝眼睛依旧带着审视的疑色端详着他。“你究竟在玩什么把戏？”他问道。

“看来连你也不信任我。”

===Original===
“I ever have done.”

“It’s a compliment,” said Bellarion.

“If it is, I don’t perceive it.”

“If you did, you wouldn’t pay it. You are direct, Carmagnola; and for that I honour you. I am not direct, and yet you may come to honour me for that too when you understand it, if you ever do. You ask what game I play. A game which began long ago, in which this is the last move. The alliance I brought about between Facino and Theodore was a move in this game; the securing of the person of Gian Giacomo of Montferrat as a hostage was another; to make it possible for Theodore to occupy Vercelli and make himself Lord of Genoa, yet another. My only aim was to unbridle his greed so that he should become a menace to the duchy, against such a day as this, when on the Duke’s side it is my duty to advise his definite destruction.”

Carmagnola’s eyes were wide, amazement overspread his florid handsome face.

“By the bones of Saint Ambrose, you play mighty deep!”

===Chinese===
“我向来如此。”

“这倒算是句夸奖了，”贝拉里翁说。

“若是夸奖，我可没觉出来。”

“你要是觉出来了，反倒不会这么夸了。你生性坦直，卡尔马尼奥拉；为此我敬重你。我却并不坦直，然而有朝一日你若能看透其中关窍——假使你真能看透的话——兴许也会因此而敬重我。你问我在玩什么把戏？这是一盘很久以前便已开局的棋，而眼前正是最后一步。当年我促成法奇诺与西奥多结盟，是这盘棋里的一着；把蒙费拉托的吉安·贾科莫扣作人质，又是一着；放手让西奥多占据韦尔切利并自立为热那亚领主，更是其中一着。我唯一的盘算，便是彻底放纵他的贪欲，使他膨胀成公国的腹心大患——好待今日这般时机到来，让我名正言顺地站在公爵一边，献策将他彻底覆灭。”

卡尔马尼奥拉双眼圆睁，那张红润英俊的脸上瞬间布满惊骇之色。

“凭圣安布罗斯（Saint Ambrose）的圣骨作证，你这盘棋下得可真够深啊！”

===Original===
Bellarion smiled. “I am frank with you. I explain myself. It is tedious but necessary so as to conquer your mistrust and procure your cooperation.”

“To make me a pawn in this game of yours?”

“That is to describe yourself unflatteringly. Francesco Busone of Carmagnola is no man’s pawn.”

“No, by God! I am glad you perceive that.”

“Should I have explained myself if I did not?” said Bellarion to assure him of a fact of which clearly he was far from sure.

===Chinese===
贝拉里翁微微一笑。“我已对你披肝沥胆，把前因后果都挑明了。这话虽嫌冗长，却非说不可，好打消你的疑忌，赢取你的鼎力相助。”

“好拿我当你这盘棋里的一枚卒子？”

“你这么说可太贬低自己了。卡尔马尼奥拉的弗朗切斯科·布索内，岂是任人摆布的棋子。”

“天主作证，绝不是！很高兴你倒还看得明白。”

“我若不明白，又岂会对你和盘托出？”贝拉里翁答道——借此笃定地安抚着对方那颗分明远未笃定的心。

===Original===
“Tell me why you so schemed and plotted?”

Bellarion sighed. “To amuse myself, perhaps. It interests me. Facino said of me that I was a natural strategist. This broader strategy upon the great field of life gives scope to my inclinations.” He was thoughtful, chin in hand. “I do not think there is more in it than that.” And abruptly he asked: “You’ll send that message?”

Carmagnola too considered. There was a dream that he had dreamed, a game that he could play, making in his turn a pawn of this crafty brother captain who sought to make a pawn of him.

“I’ll go to Melegnano in person,” he announced.

He went, and there dispelled the fretful suspense in which the Princess Valeria waited for a justice of which she almost despaired.

===Chinese===
“告诉我，你费尽心机布局设谋，到底图什么？”

贝拉里翁轻叹一声。“兴许只是为了自娱解闷吧。这事合我兴味。法奇诺曾说我天生是个运筹帷幄的奇才。在人世这片大沙场上纵横捭阖，正合我的性情。”他托着下巴沉吟道，“我想，此外也并无他图了。”随即话锋陡转，问道：“那信你送还是不送？”

卡尔马尼奥拉也思量起来。他心中早藏着一个美梦，一盘他自己也能下出来的棋——反过来把这位企图利用他的狡猾同袍将领变成自己手中的一枚卒子。

“我亲自去一趟梅莱尼亚诺（Melegnano）。”他当即宣告。

他果然动身前往，一扫瓦莱里娅公主日夜煎熬的焦虑悬心——她苦苦盼着公道伸张，几乎已要彻底绝望了。

===Original===
He dealt in that directness which was the only thing Bellarion found to honour in him. But the directness now was in his manner only.

“Lady, I come to bid you take a hand in your own and your brother’s reinstatement. Your petition to the Duke is all that is needed now to persuade him to the step which I have urged; to march against the usurper Theodore and cast him out.”

It took her breath away. “You have urged this! You, my lord? Let me send for my brother that he may thank you, that he may know that he has at least one stout brave friend in the world.”

“His friend and your servant, madonna.” He bore her white hand to his lips, and there were tears in her eyes as she looked upon his bowed handsome head. “My hopes, my plans, my schemes for you are to bear fruit at last.”

“Your schemes for me?”

Her brows were knit over her moist dark eyes. He laughed. A jovial, debonair, and laughter-loving gentleman, this Francesco Busone of Carmagnola.

===Chinese===
他拿出了那股在贝拉里翁眼里唯一可敬的坦率劲儿来应付她。只是如今这份坦率，不过流于表面做派罢了。

“小姐，我此来正是请您与令弟一道亲自出面，重夺本属于你们的一切。眼下只差您向公爵递上一纸陈情，便足以说服他听从我力陈的方略——挥师讨伐篡位者西奥多，将他逐出蒙费拉托。”

她激动得一时屏住了呼吸。“竟是您力陈此事！是您吗，大人？快容我差人去请我弟弟来向您致谢，好让他知道，在这世上他至少还有一位忠勇可靠的挚友。”

“是他的挚友，也是您的忠仆，小姐。”他捧起她雪白的手背轻吻，而她低头望着他垂首行礼的俊美面庞，眼眶不禁湿润了。“我为您倾注的心愿、谋划与布局，总算要开花结果了。”

“您为我设的布局？”

她那双盈着泪光的深邃黑眸上方，秀眉微微蹙起。他却朗声大笑起来。这位卡尔马尼奥拉的弗朗切斯科·布索内，果然是个风流倜傥、爽朗爱笑的佳公子。

===Original===
“So as to provide a cause disposing the Duke of Milan to proceed against the Regent Theodore. The hour has come, madonna. It needs but your petition to Filippo Maria, and the army marches. So that I command it, I will see justice done to your brother.”

“So that you command it? Who else should?” Carmagnola’s bright face was overcast. “There is Bellarion Cane.”

“That knave!” She recoiled, her countenance troubled. “He is the Regent’s man. It was he who helped the Regent to Vercelli and to the lordship of Genoa.”

“Which he never could have done,” Carmagnola assured her, “but that I abetted him. I saw that thus I should provide a reason for action against the Regent when later I should come to be on the Duke’s side.”

“Ah! That was shrewd! To feed his ambition until he overreached himself.”

===Chinese===
“正是如此，为的便是替米兰公爵造出一条兴兵讨伐摄政王西奥多的师出之名。时机已经成熟，小姐。如今只需您向菲利波·玛丽亚呈上奏请，大军即刻开拔。只要这支大军由我统帅，我定教令弟沉冤得雪、公道重申。”

“由您统帅？除了您还能有谁？”卡尔马尼奥拉晴朗的面容忽然阴沉下来。“还有个贝拉里翁·卡内。”

“那个无耻奸贼！”她不由得往后退了一步，满面惊疑忧愤，“他是摄政王的党羽！当年正是他帮着摄政王夺取了韦尔切利，又助他窃据热那亚领主之位！”

“若非我暗中纵容助力，”卡尔马尼奥拉信誓旦旦地向她保证，“他休想成事。我早就看准了，日后待我站到公爵这一边时，这恰恰能为我们讨伐摄政王提供绝佳的借口。”

“啊！真是高明至极！故意助长他的野心，好让他贪心不足、自取灭亡。”

===Original===
Carmagnola strutted a little. “It was a deep game. But we are at the last move in it. If you mistrust this Bellarion﻿ ﻿…”

“Mistrust him!” She laughed a bitter little laugh, and she poured forth the tale of how once he had been a spy sent by Theodore to embroil her, and how thereafter he had murdered her one true and devoted friend Count Spigno.

Feeding her mistrust and bringing Gian Giacomo fully to share it, Carmagnola conducted them to Milan and procured audience for them with the Duke.

Filippo Maria received her in a small room in the very heart of the fortress, a room to which he had brought something of the atmosphere of his library at Pavia. Here were the choicely bound manuscripts, and the writing-table with its sheaves of parchment, and its horn of unicorn, which as all the world knows is a prophylactic against all manner of ills of the flesh and the spirit. Its double window looked out upon the court of San Donato where the October sunshine warmed the red brick to the colour of the rose.

He gave her a kindly welcome, then settled into the inscrutable inertia of an obese Eastern idol whilst she made her prayer to him.

===Chinese===
卡尔马尼奥拉得意地挺了挺胸膛。“这盘棋确实下得极深。不过眼下已走到了收官之着。倘若您信不过那个贝拉里翁……”

“信不过他！”她凄然冷笑一声，竹筒倒豆子般将往事尽数道出——当年此人如何受西奥多指派充当细作前来挑拨陷害她，后来又如何残忍杀害了她唯一忠心赤诚的挚友斯皮尼奥伯爵。

卡尔马尼奥拉一路煽风点火，将她的猜忌喂得愈发深重，又劝得吉安·贾科莫也对此深信不疑，随即护送姐弟二人赶赴米兰，替他们求得公爵召见。

菲利波·玛丽亚在要塞最深处的一间小室里接见了她，屋中陈设隐隐透出他帕维亚书斋的几分气象。只见架上列满装帧精美的抄本典籍，书案上摊着一叠叠羊皮纸，案头还摆着一支独角兽角——世人皆知此物乃百病不侵、驱邪避秽的灵药。一扇双格窗朝外望向圣多纳托庭院（San Donato），十月的融融秋阳正将那片红砖墙晒得泛起玫瑰般的暖色。

他温言迎候了她，随后便沉坐下去，如同一尊肥硕而高深莫测的东方偶像般纹丝不动，静静听她向自己陈情乞援。

===Original===
When it was done he nodded slowly, and despatched his secretary in quest of the Prince of Valsassina. The name conveyed nothing to her, for she had not heard of Bellarion’s latest dignity.

“You shall have my decision later, madonna. It is almost made already, and in the direction you desire. When I have conferred with the Prince of Valsassina upon the means at our command, I will send for you again. Meanwhile the Lord of Carmagnola will conduct you and your brother to my Duchess, whom it will delight to care for you.” He cleared his throat. “You have leave to go,” he added in his shrill voice.

They bowed, and were departing, when the returning secretary, opening the door, and holding up the arras that masked it, announced: “The Prince of Valsassina.”

He came in erect and proud of bearing, for all that he still limped a little. His tunic was of black velvet edged with dark brown fur, a heavy gold chain hung upon his breast, a girdle of beaten gold gripped his loins and carried his stout dagger. His hose were in white and blue stripes.

From the threshold he bowed low to the Prince and then to Madonna Valeria, who was staring at him in sudden panic.

===Chinese===
待她诉毕，他缓缓颔首，随即遣书记官去传召瓦尔萨西纳亲王。这个封号于她而言全然陌生，因为她尚未听闻贝拉里翁新近荣膺的爵位。

“过些时日自会给您答复，小姐。主意其实已近乎定下，也正合您所愿。待本爵与瓦尔萨西纳亲王商议妥当手头可调遣的兵力，便再召您前来。眼下且由卡尔马尼奥拉大人引您与令弟去见本爵的公爵夫人，她定然欢喜照拂二位。”他清了清嗓子，又用那尖细的嗓音补了一句：“退下吧。”

众人躬身行礼，正待告退，恰逢去而复返的书记官推开房门，掀开遮门的挂毯高声通传：“瓦尔萨西纳亲王到。”

来人昂首阔步走入室内，气宇轩昂，尽管左腿仍微有些跛。他身着一件深棕毛皮滚边的黑丝绒短袍，胸前垂着一根沉甸甸的金链，腰间束一条锻金腰带，佩着一柄厚实的短剑，下身穿着蓝白条纹的紧身长袜。

他在门槛边先向公爵深深施礼，接着又向正惊惶失措、呆呆盯着他的瓦莱里娅小姐躬身致意。

===Original===
She curtsied to him almost despite herself, and then made haste to depart with Carmagnola and her brother. But there was a weight of lead in her breast. If action against Theodore depended upon this man’s counsel, what hope remained? She put that question to Carmagnola. He quieted her fears.

“After all, he is not omnipotent. Our fealty is not to him, but to the Duchess Beatrice. Win her to your side, and things will shape the course you desire, especially if I command the enterprise.”

And meanwhile this man whom she mistrusted was closeted with the Duke, and the Duke was informing him of this new factor in their plans against Montferrat.

“She desires us to break a lance in her brother’s behalf. But Montferrat is loyal to Theodore. They have no opinion there of Gian Giacomo, and to impose by force of arms a prince upon a people is perhaps to render that people hostile to ourselves.”

“If that were so, and I confess that I do not share your potency’s apprehensions, it would still be the course I should presume to advise. In Theodore you have a neighbour whom ambition makes dangerous. In Gian Giacomo you have a mild and gentle youth, whose thoughts, since his conversion from debauchery, turn rather to religion than to deeds of arms. Place him upon the throne of his fathers, and you have in such a man not only a friendly neighbour but a grateful servant.”

===Chinese===
她几乎身不由己地向他屈膝回礼，随后便匆匆随卡尔马尼奥拉和弟弟退了出去。然而她胸口却仿佛压了一块沉铅。倘若讨伐西奥多之举竟要仰仗此人的筹谋，那还剩几分指望？她将这番忧虑问向卡尔马尼奥拉，后者出言宽慰了她的惊惧。

“说到底，他也并非一手遮天。我们效忠的并非是他，而是贝阿特丽切公爵夫人。只要赢得夫人站在您这边，事情自会依您所望的方向水到渠成——尤其是倘若此番出征由我挂帅。”

而此时此刻，那位备受她猜忌的男子正与公爵密室长谈，公爵将他们对蒙费拉托全盘大计中骤然生出的这桩新变故相告于他。

“她恳请我们为了她弟弟挺枪出战。可蒙费拉托上下忠于西奥多。那里的臣民向来瞧不上吉安·贾科莫，若以兵戈强行将一位君主加诸一国百姓头上，只怕反倒会招致彼邦民众仇视我等。”

“即便果真如此——虽说恕臣直言，臣并不认同殿下的忧虑——臣仍冒昧建言采行此策。西奥多此人野心勃勃，做邻居实在危险之至。而吉安·贾科莫乃是个性情温良谦和的年轻人；自打他痛改前非、戒绝放荡之后，心思便更倾向于虔敬宗教，而非舞刀弄枪。将他扶上先祖宝座，您得到的不仅是一位友善的邻邦君主，更是一位感恩戴德的忠实藩臣。”

===Original===
“Ha! You believe in gratitude, Bellarion?”

“I must, since I practise it.”

There followed that night a council of the captains, and since they were still nominally regarded as in the service of Facino’s widow, the Duchess herself attended it, and since the fortunes of the legitimate ruler of Montferrat was one of the issues, the Marquis Gian Giacomo and his sister were also invited to be present.

The Duke, at the head of the long table, with the Duchess on his right and Bellarion on his left, made known the intention to declare war immediately upon the Regent of Montferrat upon two grounds: his occupation of the Milanese stronghold and lands of Vercelli, and his usurpation of the regency beyond the Marquis Gian Giacomo’s attainment of full age. Of his captains now he desired an account of the means at their disposal, and afterwards a decision of those to be employed in the undertaking.

Carmagnola came prepared with a computation of the probable forces which Theodore could levy; and they were considerable; not less than five thousand men. The necessary force to deal with him was next debated, having regard also to certain other enterprises to which Milan was elsewhere committed. At length this was fixed by Bellarion. It was to consist of the Germans under Koenigshofen, Stoffel’s Swiss, Giasone Trotta’s Italian mercenaries, and Marsilio’s condotta, amounting in all to some seven thousand men. That would leave free for other eventualities the condottas of Valperga and of Carmagnola with whom were Ercole Belluno and Ugolino da Tenda.

===Chinese===
“哈！贝拉里翁，你竟相信世上有所谓感恩之情？”

“臣不能不信，只因臣自己便笃行不悖。”

当夜随即召开了众将军事会议。由于诸将名义上仍算效力于法奇诺的遗孀，公爵夫人便亲自列席；又因蒙费拉托合法君主的命运正是此番议事的要端之一，吉安·贾科莫侯爵及其姐也一同受邀与会。

公爵端坐长桌主位，公爵夫人居其右首，贝拉里翁居其左首，当众宣布即刻向蒙费拉托摄政王宣战，兴师之由凡二：其一，侵占米兰领属之韦尔切利要塞及疆土；其二，吉安·贾科莫侯爵既已成年，仍恋栈摄政之位、僭越不交政权。公爵如今命诸将禀明麾下可用兵马之数，再议定此役当遣何部出征。

卡尔马尼奥拉早有备而来，报出了西奥多可能征募的兵力估数：为数颇为可观，不下五千之众。众人随即斟酌破敌所需兵力，并兼顾米兰别处业已担负的若干战事。最终由贝拉里翁拍板定案：出征大军由柯尼希斯霍芬麾下的德意志兵、斯托费尔的瑞士雇佣兵、贾索内·特罗塔的意大利雇佣兵以及马尔西利奥的雇佣兵团合编而成，总计约七千人。如此一来，瓦尔佩尔加与卡尔马尼奥拉——以及随他同行的埃尔科莱·贝卢诺和乌戈利诺·达·滕达——所部雇佣兵团便可留作机动，以备他变。

===Original===
Against this, and on the plea that the Duke might require the services of the Prince of Valsassina at home, Carmagnola begged that the enterprise against Montferrat should be confided to his leadership, his own condotta taking the place of Bellarion’s, but all else remaining as Bellarion disposed.

The Duke, showing in his pale face no sign of his surprise at this request, looked from Carmagnola to Bellarion, appearing to ponder, what time the Princess Valeria held her breath.

At length the Duke spoke. “Have you anything to say to that, Valsassina?”

“Nothing if your highness is content. You will remember that Theodore of Montferrat is one of the most skilful captains of the day, and if this business is not to drag on unduly, indeed if it is to be brought to a successful issue, you would do well to send against him of your best.”

A sly smile broke upon that sinisterly placid countenance.

“By which you mean yourself.”

===Chinese===
针对这一部署，卡尔马尼奥拉以公爵坐镇后方或许正须倚重瓦尔萨西纳亲王运筹为由，恳请将讨伐蒙费拉托一役交由自己挂帅，以他本部的雇佣兵团替代贝拉里翁所部出征，其余一切皆照贝拉里翁原议不变。

公爵苍白的脸上丝毫不露闻此请求的惊讶之色，目光在卡尔马尼奥拉与贝拉里翁之间来回逡巡，作沉吟状；其间瓦莱里娅公主紧张得屏息凝神。

良久，公爵终于开口。“瓦尔萨西纳，对此你有何话说？”

“只要殿下圣心满意，臣别无他言。只是殿下当铭记，蒙费拉托的西奥多乃当今世上屈指可数的用兵奇才；此战若不愿久拖生变，实则若想克奏全功，殿下最好还是遣最精锐的统帅去与他周旋。”

一抹狡黠的笑意悄然绽开在那张阴沉却波澜不惊的胖脸上。

“言下之意，便是指你自己喽。”

===Original===
“For my part,” said Koenigshofen, “I do not willingly march under another.”

“And for mine,” said Stoffel, “whilst Bellarion lives I do not march under another at all.”

The Duke looked at Carmagnola. “You hear, sir?”

Carmagnola flushed uncomfortably. “I had set my heart upon the enterprise, Lord Duke.”

The Princess Valeria interposed. “By your leave, highness; does my vote count for anything in this matter?”

“Assuredly, madonna. Your own and your brother’s.”

===Chinese===
“就我而言，”柯尼希斯霍芬开口道，“我可不情愿在旁人麾下听调。”

“就我而言，”斯托费尔接着道，“只要贝拉里翁还在世一天，我就绝不在旁人麾下出征。”

公爵望向卡尔马尼奥拉。“你听见了吗，阁下？”

卡尔马尼奥拉脸上局促地一阵发红。“公爵大人，此役我实是志在必得。”

瓦莱里娅公主此时插言道：“请殿下恩准：不知此事臣女可有一言之权？”

“那是自然，小姐。您与令弟皆有发言之权。”

===Original===
“Then, Lord Duke, my vote, indeed my prayer, is that my Lord of Carmagnola be given the command.”

The Duchess raised her long eyes to look at her in wonder.

Bellarion sat inscrutable.

The request wounded without surprising him. He knew her unconquerable mistrust of him. He had hoped in the end which was now approaching to prove to her its cruel injustice. But if occasion for that were denied him, it would be no great matter. What signified was that her own aims should be accomplished, and, after all, they were not beyond the strength and skill of Carmagnola, who had his talents as a leader when all was said.

The Duke’s lacklustre eyes were steadily upon Valeria. He spoke after a pause.

===Chinese===
“那么，公爵大人，臣女的主张——乃至臣女的恳求——便是请将主帅之职授予卡尔马尼奥拉大人。”

公爵夫人抬起那双细长的眼眸，惊诧地望向她。

贝拉里翁端坐不动，神色莫测。

这番请求虽刺痛了他，却并未令他感到意外。他早知她对自己那份根深蒂固的猜忌牢不可破。他原指望趁着如今大功将成之际，亲手向她证明这份疑忌何等冷酷不公。然而即便连这证明的机会也遭剥夺，倒也无妨。真正紧要的，是她自己的夙愿得以实现；而平心而论，此事亦未超出卡尔马尼奥拉的才力所能及——说到底，这人身为统帅确有过人之才。

公爵那双黯淡无光的眼睛一动不动地注视着瓦莱里娅。顿了片刻，他才开口。

===Original===
“Almost you imply a doubt of the Prince of Valsassina’s capacity.”

“Not of his capacity. Oh, not of that!”

“Of what, then?”

The question troubled her. She looked at her brother, and her brother answered for her.

“My sister remembers that the Prince of Valsassina was once the Marquis Theodore’s friend.”

“Was he so? When was that?” The Duke looked at Bellarion, but it was Gian Giacomo who answered the question.

===Chinese===
“您这话几乎是在怀疑瓦尔萨西纳亲王的才干了。”

“并非怀疑他的才干。哦，绝非如此！”

“那又怀疑什么呢？”

这句反问令她心头一乱。她望向弟弟，弟弟替她作了答：

“家姐牢记着，瓦尔萨西纳亲王昔日曾是西奥多侯爵的朋友。”

“竟有此事？那是何时？”公爵转眼看向贝拉里翁，抢先接过话头的却是吉安·贾科莫。

===Original===
“When, in alliance with him, he placed him in possession of Vercelli and Genoa.”

“The alliance was the Lord Facino’s, not Valsassina’s. Bellarion served under him. But so also did Carmagnola. Where is the difference between them?”

“My Lord of Carmagnola acted then with a view to my brother’s ultimate service,” the Princess answered. “If he was a party to the Marquis Theodore’s occupation of Vercelli, it was only so that in that act the Marquis might provide a cause for the action that is now proposed against him by the Duke of Milan.”

Bellarion laughed softly at the light he suddenly perceived.

“Do you mock that statement, sir?” Carmagnola challenged him. “Do you dare to say what was in my mind at the time?”

“I have honoured you for directness, Carmagnola. But it seems you can be subtle too.”

===Chinese===
“便是当年与他结盟、助他占据韦尔切利与热那亚之时。”

“结盟之人乃是法奇诺大人，并非瓦尔萨西纳。贝拉里翁当时不过受其驱策。可卡尔马尼奥拉不也同样在法奇诺麾下效力么？二人之间又有何分别？”

“卡尔马尼奥拉大人当年所行，乃是为了我弟弟日后得以翻身复国，”公主答道，“即便他曾插手助西奥多侯爵占据韦尔切利，也不过是要借侯爵那一着棋，为如今米兰公爵出兵讨伐他制造师出之名罢了。”

贝拉里翁恍然悟透了其中奥妙，忍不住低声轻笑起来。

“阁下莫非是在讥嘲这番话不成？”卡尔马尼奥拉厉声质问他，“难道你敢妄断我当时心中所想？”

“我向来敬重你坦直，卡尔马尼奥拉。看来你倒也懂得深谋曲折呢。”

===Original===
“Subtle!” Carmagnola flushed indignantly. “In what have I been subtle?”

“In the spirit in which you favoured Theodore’s occupation of Vercelli,” said Bellarion, and so left him gaping foolishly. “What else did you think I had in mind?” He smiled almost ingenuously into the other’s face.

The Duke rapped the table. “Sirs, sirs! We wander. And there is this matter to resolve.”

===Chinese===
“深谋曲折！”卡尔马尼奥拉愤然涨红了脸，“我哪里深谋曲折了？”

“就在你当初力主让西奥多占据韦尔切利那番苦心上啊，”贝拉里翁答道，说得对方张口结舌、傻愣在当场。“不然你以为我指的还能是什么？”他望着对方的脸，竟露出近乎天真无邪的笑意。

公爵抬手叩了叩桌面。“诸位，诸位！扯远了。眼前正事尚待决断。”

===Original===
Bellarion answered him.

“Here, then, is a solution your highness may be disposed to adopt. Instead of Valperga and his troops, I take with me Carmagnola and his own condotta which is of a similar strength, and, like Valperga’s, mainly horse. Thus we march together, and share the enterprise.”

“But unless Bellarion commands it, Lord Duke, your highness will graciously consider sending another condotta in the place of mine,” said Koenigshofen, and Stoffel was about to add his own voice to that, when the Duke losing patience broke in.

“Peace! Peace! I am Duke of Milan, and I give orders here. You are summoned to advise, not to browbeat me and say what you will and will not do. Let it be done as Valsassina says, since Carmagnola has set his heart upon being in the campaign. But Valsassina leads the enterprise. The matter is closed on that. You have leave to go.”

===Chinese===
贝拉里翁起身回禀：

“那么，殿下或许不妨采纳这样一个两全之策：改调卡尔马尼奥拉及其所部雇佣兵团随臣出征，替下瓦尔佩尔加一军；两部兵力相当，且与瓦尔佩尔加所部一样皆以骑兵为主。如此我等便可并肩进军，共成此役。”

“可公爵大人，此役若不由贝拉里翁统帅，还望殿下开恩，另派他部雇佣兵团替下末将所部吧，”柯尼希斯霍芬说道。斯托费尔正待开口附和，公爵终于按捺不住怒火，厉声打断：

“住口！住口！本爵才是米兰公爵，这里由本爵发号施令！召你们前来是议事献策，岂容你们威胁胁迫本爵，由着你们挑拣什么肯做、什么不肯做！就依瓦尔萨西纳所言办理——既然卡尔马尼奥拉一门心思想参预此战，便准他同去。但全军主帅仍由瓦尔萨西纳担任。此事就此定案，毋庸再议。退下吧。”

## VIII Carmagnola’s Bridges / 第八章 卡尔马尼奥拉的桥梁

===Original===
Dissensions at the very outset between Carmagnola and Bellarion protracted by some days the preparations for the departure of the army. This enabled Theodore of Montferrat fully to make his dispositions for resistance, to pack the granaries of Vercelli and otherwise victual it for a siege, and to increase the strong body of troops already under his hand, with which he threw himself into the menaced city. Further, by working furiously during those October days, he was enabled to strengthen his bastions and throw up fresh earthworks, from which to shatter the onslaught when it should come.

Upon these very circumstances of which Bellarion and his captains were duly informed followed fresh dissensions. Carmagnola advocated that operations should be begun by the reduction of Mortara, which was being held for Theodore, and which, if not seized before they marched upon Vercelli, would constitute, he argued, a menace upon their rear. Bellarion’s view was that the menace was not sufficiently serious to merit attention; that whilst they were reducing it, Theodore would further be strengthening himself at Vercelli; and that, in short, they should march straight upon Vercelli, depending that, when they forced it to a capitulation, Mortara would thereby be scared into immediate surrender.

Of the captains some held one view, some the other. Koenigshofen, Stoffel, and Trotta took sides with Bellarion. Ercole Belluno, who commanded the foot in Carmagnola’s condotta, took sides with his leader as did also Ugolino da Tenda who captained a thousand horse. Yet Bellarion would have overruled them but for the Princess Valeria who with her brother entered now into all their councils. These were on the side of Carmagnola. Hence a compromise was effected. A detachment under Koenigshofen including Trotta’s troops was to go against Mortara, to cover the rear of the main army proceeding to Vercelli.

===Chinese===
大战伊始，卡尔马尼奥拉与贝拉里翁之间的分歧便使大军开拔的筹备耽搁了数日。这让蒙费拉托的西奥多（Theodore of Montferrat）得以从容部署防御：他将韦尔切利（Vercelli）的粮仓装得满满当当，储备了充足的围城军需，又扩充了麾下本就精锐的兵力，亲自率军进驻这座危城。更有甚者，在十月那几天里，他督促军民昼夜赶工，加固棱堡，并构筑起新的土垒，只待敌军猛攻一至，便将其击溃。

贝拉里翁与众将领如实获悉这些敌情后，军中又生出新的争执。卡尔马尼奥拉主张先攻占莫尔塔拉（Mortara）——该地正由西奥多的守军据守，他认为若不在进军韦尔切利前拔除这颗钉子，大军后背便会时刻面临威胁。贝拉里翁却认为这点威胁不足为虑；倘若他们把时间耗在攻打莫尔塔拉上，西奥多只会借机在韦尔切利把防线筑得更加固若金汤。简而言之，他力主直捣韦尔切利，笃信只要迫使韦尔切利投降，莫尔塔拉便会闻风丧胆、不战而降。

众将领对此各执一词。柯尼希斯霍芬（Koenigshofen）、斯托费尔（Stoffel）与特罗塔（Trotta）站在贝拉里翁一边；而统领卡尔马尼奥拉雇佣兵团（condotta）步兵的埃尔科莱·贝卢诺（Ercole Belluno），以及率领一千骑兵的乌戈利诺·达·滕达（Ugolino da Tenda），则支持自己的主帅。若非瓦莱里娅公主（Princess Valeria）如今携胞弟一同出席每次军事会议，贝拉里翁原本可以力排众议。然而姐弟二人皆偏袒卡尔马尼奥拉，最终双方只得折中妥协：由柯尼希斯霍芬率领一支包含特罗塔所部在内的分队前去攻打莫尔塔拉，以掩护主力大军向韦尔切利推进时的后方。

===Original===
To Vercelli that army, now not more than some four thousand strong, yet strong enough in Bellarion’s view for the task in hand, made at last a speedy advance. But at Borgo Vercelli they were brought to a halt by the fact that Theodore had blown up the bridge over the Sesia, leaving that broad, deep, swift-flowing river between the enemy and the city which was their goal.

At Carpignano, twenty miles higher up, there was a bridge which Bellarion ascertained had been left standing. He announced that they must avail themselves of that.

“Twenty miles there, and twenty miles back!” snorted Carmagnola. “It is too much. A weariness and a labour.”

“I’ll not dispute it. But the alternative is to go by way of Casale, which is even farther.”

“The alternative,” Carmagnola answered, “is to bridge the Sesia and the Cerva above their junction where the Sesia is narrower. Our lines of communication with the army at Mortara should be as short as possible.”

===Chinese===
这支如今兵力不过四千人上下、但在贝拉里翁看来已足以胜任此役的大军，终于迅速向韦尔切利进发。然而行至博尔戈韦尔切利（Borgo Vercelli）时，他们却被迫停下脚步——西奥多早已炸毁了横跨塞西亚河（Sesia）的桥梁，将这条宽阔、幽深而湍急的大河横亘在敌军与他们志在必得的城池之间。

上游二十英里处的卡尔皮尼亚诺（Carpignano）另有一座桥，贝拉里翁探明那座桥尚且完好无损。他下令大军必须绕道那座桥过河。

“去二十英里，回来又是二十英里！”卡尔马尼奥拉嗤之以鼻，“太远了，徒劳无功，疲师劳众。”

“这我不否认。可另一条路是绕道卡萨莱（Casale），那比这儿还要远。”

“还有一条路，”卡尔马尼奥拉答道，“是在塞西亚河与切尔瓦河（Cerva）汇流处上方架桥——那一段的塞西亚河河面更窄。我们与莫尔塔拉分队之间的联络线应当越短越好。”

===Original===
“You begin to perceive one of the disadvantages of having left that army at Mortara.”

“It is no disadvantage if we make proper provision.”

“And you think that your bridges will afford that provision.” Bellarion’s manner was almost supercilious.

Carmagnola resented it. “Can you deny it?”

“I can do more. I can foresee what will happen. Sometimes, Francesco, you leave me wondering where you learnt the art of war, or how ever you came to engage in it.”

===Chinese===
“你总算开始意识到把那支军队留在莫尔塔拉的弊端之一了。”

“只要措施得当，这就称不上弊端。”

“这么说，你觉得你搭的桥就能算措施得当了。”贝拉里翁的神态几乎有些傲慢。

卡尔马尼奥拉大为光火：“难道你能否认吗？”

“我岂止能否认，我还能预见到将会发生什么。弗朗切斯科（Francesco），有时候你真让我怀疑，你究竟是从哪儿学来的兵法，当初又是怎么吃上行伍这碗饭的。”

===Original===
They held their discussion in the kitchen of a peasant’s house which for the Princess Valeria’s sake they had invaded. And the Princess and her brother were its only witnesses. When Carmagnola now moved wrathfully in great strides about the dingy chamber, stamping upon the earthen floor and waving his arms as he began to storm, one of those witnesses became an actor to calm him. The Princess Valeria laid a hand upon one of those waving arms in its gorgeous sleeve of gold-embroidered scarlet.

“Do not heed his taunts, Messer Carmagnola. You have my utter trust and confidence. It is my wish that you should build your bridges.”

Bellarion tilted his chin to look at her between anger and amusement.

“If you are to take command, highness, I’ll say no more.” He bowed, and went out.

“One of these days I shall give that upstart dog a lesson in good manners,” said Carmagnola between his teeth.

===Chinese===
他们商议军情的地点，是这户农舍的厨房——只因照顾瓦莱里娅公主，众人才临时征用了这处宅院。屋里仅有的两位旁观者，便是公主与她的弟弟。眼下卡尔马尼奥拉怒不可遏地在昏暗狭窄的屋里大步踱来踱去，重重踩着泥土地面，挥舞着双臂正要大发雷霆，那两位旁观者中的一人便亲自上场安抚他。瓦莱里娅公主将一只手轻轻搭在他那正乱挥的手臂上——那臂上套着金线刺绣的猩红锦袖，华贵非凡。

“别理会他的冷嘲热讽，卡尔马尼奥拉阁下。我完全信任您、仰仗您。我意已决，就请您着手架桥吧。”

贝拉里翁微微扬起下巴看着她，神情既含怒意又带几分玩味。

“既然由殿下您来发号施令，那我便无话可说了。”他行了一礼，转身步出屋去。

“总有一天，我要好好教训教训那条不知天高地厚的暴发户恶犬，叫他懂得什么是礼数。”卡尔马尼奥拉咬牙切齿地说道。

===Original===
The Princess shook her head.

“It is not his manners, sir, that trouble me; but his possible aims. If I could trust him﻿ ﻿…”

“If you could trust his loyalty, you should still mistrust his skill.”

“Yet he has won great repute as a soldier,” put in Gian Giacomo, who instinctively mistrusted the thrasonical airs of the swaggering Carmagnola, and mistrusted still more his fawning manner towards Valeria.

“He has been fortunate,” Carmagnola answered, “and his good fortune has gone to his head.”

===Chinese===
公主摇了摇头。

“阁下，真正令我忧心的倒不是他的礼数，而是他居心何在。要是我能信得过他……”

“就算您信得过他的忠心，也依然该怀疑他的本事。”

“可他作为一名统帅，毕竟早已名扬四海。”吉安·贾科莫（Gian Giacomo）插嘴道。他本能地厌恶卡尔马尼奥拉那副虚张声势、不可一世的派头，更不信任他对瓦莱里娅大献殷勤的谄媚嘴脸。

“他不过是走运罢了，”卡尔马尼奥拉答道，“而这点好运气早就冲昏了他的头脑。”

===Original===
Meanwhile Bellarion went straight from that interview to despatch Werner von Stoffel with five hundred arbalesters and six hundred horse to Carpignano.

There was a fresh breeze with Carmagnola when the latter discovered this. He demanded to know why it should have been done without previous consultation with himself and the Princess, and Valeria was beside him when he asked the question.

Bellarion’s answer was a very full one.

“You will be a week building your bridges. In that time it may occur to Theodore to do what he should have done already, to destroy the bridge at Carpignano.”

“And what do I care about the bridge at Carpignano when I shall have bridges of my own here?”

===Chinese===
与此同时，贝拉里翁一离开那场谈话，便径直下令派遣维尔纳·冯·斯托费尔（Werner von Stoffel）率领五百名弩手与六百名骑兵开赴卡尔皮尼亚诺。

卡尔马尼奥拉得知此事后，又起了一阵风波。他质问贝拉里翁为何事先不与自己及公主商议便擅自调兵，而他发问时，瓦莱里娅正立在他身旁。

贝拉里翁的回答滴水不漏。

“你造那些桥少说得花上一周。在这期间，西奥多说不定就会想起去办那件他早该办的事——毁掉卡尔皮尼亚诺的桥梁。”

“等我在这儿架好了自己的桥，我还管卡尔皮尼亚诺的桥作甚？”

===Original===
“When you have bridges of your own here, you need not care. But I have a notion that it will be longer than you think before you have these bridges, and that we may have to go by way of Carpignano in the end.”

“I shall have my bridges in a week,” said Carmagnola.

Bellarion smiled. “When you have them, and when you have put two thousand men across to hold them, I’ll bid Stoffel return from Carpignano.”

“But in the meantime﻿ ﻿…”

Bellarion interrupted him, and suddenly he was very stern.

===Chinese===
“等你真在这儿架好了自己的桥，自然用不着管。不过我倒预感，你的桥绝不会像你想的那样快就能完工，到头来我们恐怕还是得从卡尔皮尼亚诺过河。”

“一周之内，我的桥必成。”卡尔马尼奥拉硬邦邦地说道。

贝拉里翁淡淡一笑：“等你建成了桥，并且派两千人马过河守住桥头，我自会下令让斯托费尔从卡尔皮尼亚诺撤回来。”

“可在这期间……”

贝拉里翁打断了他，脸色骤然一沉，凛然生威。

===Original===
“In the meantime you will remember that I command. Though I may choose to humour you and her highness, as the shortest way to convince you of error, yet I do not undertake to obey you against my better judgment.”

“By God, Bellarion!” Carmagnola swore at him, “I’ll not have you gay with me. You’ll measure your words, or else you’ll eat them.”

Very coldly Bellarion looked at him, and observed Valeria’s white restraining hand which again was upon Carmagnola’s sleeve.

“At the moment I have a task in hand to which I belong entirely. While it is doing if you forget that I command, I shall remove you from the army.”

He left the swaggerer fuming.

===Chinese===
“在这期间，你给我记牢了，这支军队由我统帅。尽管我可以顺着你和殿下的意思，好让你们尽快认清自己的错误，但我绝不会违背我更周全的判断去听命于你。”

“看在上帝的份上，贝拉里翁！”卡尔马尼奥拉冲他破口大骂，“我可容不得你跟我这般放肆戏弄！说话给我掂量着点，否则我叫你把话原封不动咽回去！”

贝拉里翁冷冷地打量着他，目光落到瓦莱里娅那只再次轻轻按在卡尔马尼奥拉衣袖上以示劝阻的白皙玉手。

“眼下我手头有重任在身，须得全力以赴。在此期间，你若敢忘了谁才是主帅，我便将你逐出军营。”

他丢下那个暴跳如雷的狂徒，拂袖而去。

===Original===
“Only my regard for you, madonna, restrains me,” he assured the Princess. “He takes that tone when he should remember that, if it came to blows between us, the majority of the men here would be upon my side, now that he has sent nearly all his own away.” He clenched his hands in anger. “Yet for your sake, lady, I must suffer it. There can be no quarrel between his men and mine until we have placed you and your brother in possession of Montferrat.”

These and other such professions of staunch selfless loyalty touched her deeply; and in the days that followed, whilst the troopers, toiling like woodmen, were felling trees and building the bridges above the junction of the rivers, Carmagnola and Valeria were constantly together.

She was driven now to the discomfort of living under canvas, sharing the camp life of these rude men of war, and Carmagnola did all in his power to mitigate for her the hardships it entailed, hardships which she bore with a high gay courage. She would go with him daily to watch the half-naked labourers in the river, bundling together whole trees as if they were mere twigs, to serve as pontoons. And daily he gave her cause to admire his skill, his ingenuity, and his military capacity. That Bellarion should have sneered at this was but another proof of Bellarion’s worthlessness. Either he could not understand it, or else of treacherous intent he desired to deprive her of its fruits.

Meanwhile Carmagnola beglamoured her with talk of actions past, in all of which he played ever the heroic part. The eyes of her mind were dazzled by the pictures his words drew for her. Now she beheld him leading a knightly charge that shattered an enemy host into shards; now she saw him at the head of an escalade, indomitably climbing enemy walls under a hail of stones and scalding pitch; now she saw him in council, wisely planning the means by which victory might be snatched from overwhelming opposition.

===Chinese===
“夫人，全凭我对您的敬重，我才勉强忍耐下来。”他向公主表白道，“他竟敢用这种腔调跟我说话，却忘了倘若我们真动起手来，眼下他把自己的亲信几乎全派了出去，留在这儿的大半人马都会站在我这一边。”他气得双拳紧握，“可为了您，贵人，我不得不咽下这口气。在把您和您的弟弟送回蒙费拉托掌权之前，他的部下和我的人马绝不能起内讧。”

这一番番忠肝义胆、忘我效忠的剖白深深打动了瓦莱里娅。随后的日子里，士兵们宛如伐木工般挥汗劳作，在两河交汇处的上游砍伐林木、搭建桥梁，而卡尔马尼奥拉与瓦莱里娅也几乎形影不离。

她如今只得栖身于简陋的帐篷中，与这群粗豪的武夫同甘共苦，忍受军旅生活的种种不便；而卡尔马尼奥拉则竭尽所能为她排忧解难，减轻苦楚——公主自己也以高昂乐观的勇气坦然面对这一切。她每天都与他同行，去河畔观看那些赤裸着上身的劳工在水中作业，将整棵整棵的大树当作细枝般捆扎成浮桥的舟筏。每一天，他都让她有机会赞叹他的巧思、才干与将略。至于贝拉里翁竟敢对此嗤之以鼻，这恰恰进一步证明了贝拉里翁的无能与卑劣——他要么是根本看不懂，要么就是居心叵测，妄图剥夺公主本该收获的胜果。

与此同时，卡尔马尼奥拉又用往昔的战功把她哄得心醉神迷——在他口中，每一场战役的主角都是英勇无敌的他自己。他言辞间勾勒出的画面，令公主的心神目眩神驰：一会儿，她仿佛看见他率领骑士纵马冲锋，将敌军阵势撞得粉身碎骨；一会儿，又看见他一马当先攀登云梯，冒着如雨落下的石块与滚烫的沥青，百折不挠地攻上敌军城墙；一会儿，又看见他端坐军帐之中，运筹帷幄，巧谋破敌之策，从压倒性的强敌手中夺取胜利。

===Original===
One day when he spoke of these things, as they sat alone watching the men who swarmed like ants about the building of his bridge, he touched a closer note.

“Yet of all the enterprises to which I have set these rude, soldier hands, none has so warmed me as this, for none has been worthier a man’s endeavour. It will be a glorious day for me when we set you in your palace at Casale. A glorious day, and yet a bitter.”

“A bitter?” Her great dark eyes turned on him in question.

His countenance clouded, his own glance fell away. “Will it not be bitter for me to know this service is at an end; to know that I must go my ways; resume a mercenary’s life, and do for hire that which I now do out of﻿ ﻿… enthusiasm and love?”

She shifted her own glance, embarrassed a little.

===Chinese===
有一天，他们独自并肩坐着，望着工匠们如蚁群般忙碌于架桥工程，他又谈起了这些往事，话锋一转，语调变得愈发贴心缠绵。

“然而，在我这双粗糙的武夫之手所投身过的所有伟业之中，没有哪一件能像这一次这样令我满腔热血，因为再没有比这更值得大丈夫倾力相赴的事业了。当我们迎您重返卡萨莱宫殿的那一天，于我而言必将是无比荣耀的一天——荣耀，却也苦涩。”

“苦涩？”她那双硕大深邃的黑眸转向他，带着几分疑惑。

他神色一黯，垂下眼帘。“当我知道效劳之期已尽，知道我必须就此离去，重新过回雇佣兵的生涯，拿钱财卖命，去干那些如今我全凭……满腔热忱与爱慕去做的事——这难道不令我感到苦涩吗？”

她微微避开视线，略显局促不安。

===Original===
“Surely you do yourself less than justice. There is great honour and fame in store for you, my lord.”

“Honour and fame!” He laughed. “I would gladly leave those to tricksters like Bellarion, who rise to them so easily because no scruples ever deter them. Honour and fame! Let who will have those, so that I may serve where my heart bids me.”

Boldly now his hand sought hers. She let it lie in his. Above those pensive, mysterious eyes her line brows were knit.

“Aye,” she breathed, “that is the great service of life! That is the only worthy service﻿—as the heart bids.”

His second hand came to recruit the first. Lying almost at her feet, he swung round on his side upon the green earth, looking up at her in a sort of ecstasy. “You think that, too! You help me to self-contempt, madonna.”

===Chinese===
“大人未免太过自轻了。往后自有无尽的荣耀与盛名在等着您。”

“荣耀与盛名！”他笑了一声，“那种东西，我情愿留给贝拉里翁那样的奸诈之徒——他们毫无底线可言，爬上去自然轻而易举。荣耀与盛名！谁爱要谁拿去吧，只要我能随心之所向去效劳便足矣。”

他胆子大了起来，伸手去寻她的手。她任由自己的手静静躺在他的掌心。在那双沉思而神秘的眼眸上方，她细长的双眉微微蹙起。

“是啊，”她轻叹道，“那才是人生最崇高的效劳！唯有听从本心而去效力，方才弥足珍贵。”

他的另一只手也合了上来，紧紧拢住她的手。他几乎是卧在她脚边，在青草地上侧转过身，仰望着她，神情近乎迷醉：“连您也这样认为！夫人，您这话真叫我愈发鄙薄自己了。”

===Original===
“To self-contempt? It is the only contempt that you will ever know. But why should you know that?”

“Because all my life, until this moment, I have served for hire. Because, if this adventure had not come to me by God’s grace, in such worthless endeavours would my life continue. Now﻿—now that I know the opinion in which you must hold such service﻿—it is over and done for me. When I shall have served you to your goal, I shall have performed my last.”

There fell a long pause between them. At last: “When my brother is crowned in Casale, he will need a servant such as you, Messer Carmagnola.”

“Aye, but shall you, madonna? Shall you?”

She looked at him wistfully, smiling a little. He was very handsome, very splendid and very brave, a knight to win a lady’s trust, and she was a very lonely, friendless lady in sore need of a stout arm and a gallant heart to help her through the trials of this life.

===Chinese===
“鄙薄自己？那是您这辈子唯一会遭到的鄙薄了。可您为什么会这么想呢？”

“因为长久以来，直到此刻之前，我一直都是在为赏钱卖命。倘若不是蒙上帝垂怜让我遇上这场奇遇，我的一生便会在那样毫无价值的奔忙中虚度下去。如今——如今我知道了您对那种雇佣行当的看法——我与它便一刀两断了。等我助您达成夙愿之后，我就此金盆洗手，不再为他人效力。”

两人之间陷入了长久的沉默。终于，她开口道：“等我弟弟在卡萨莱加冕之时，他会需要像您这样一位忠臣的，卡尔马尼奥拉阁下。”

“是啊，可夫人您呢？您会需要吗？”

她含情脉脉地望着他，嘴角噙着一抹浅笑。他生得如此英俊，风采照人而又勇武过人，正是那种最能赢得淑女信赖的骑士；而她自己，却是一位孤苦伶仃、举目无亲的女子，正迫切需要一条强健的臂膀与一颗豪侠之心，助她度过这人世间的重重磨难。

===Original===
The tapering fingers of her disengaged hand descended gently upon his golden head.

“Shall I not?” she asked with a little tremulous laugh. “Shall I not?”

“Why, then, madonna, if you will accept my service, it shall be yours for as long as I endure. It shall never be another’s. Valeria! My Valeria!”

That hand upon his head, overheating its very indifferent contents, drove him now to an excessive precipitancy.

He carried the hand he held almost fiercely to his lips.

It was withdrawn, gently but firmly as was its fellow. His kiss and the bold use of her name scared her a little.

===Chinese===
她空着的那只手伸出纤细修长的指尖，轻轻落在他金发垂覆的头顶。

“我岂能不需要呢？”她略带颤音地轻笑道，“我岂能不需要呢？”

“那么，夫人，您若肯接纳我的效忠，此生只要我一息尚存，便只为您一人效力，绝不事二主。瓦莱里娅！我的瓦莱里娅！”

头顶那只玉手的轻抚，把他本就平庸的头脑烘得热昏了头，驱使他做出了极其唐突鲁莽的举动。

他几乎是狂热地将手中握着的那只手凑到唇边一吻。

那只手随即抽了回去，动作轻柔却坚定，头顶上的另一只手也一同收了回去。他这一吻以及如此大胆直呼她的闺名，着实令她有几分惊惶。

===Original===
“Carmagnola, my friend﻿ ﻿…”

“Your friend, and more than your friend, madonna.”

“Why, how much more can there be than that?”

“All that a man may be to a woman, my Valeria. I am your knight. I ever have been since that day in the lists at Milan, when you bestowed the palm on me. I joy in this battle that is to be fought for you. I would joy in death for you if it were needed to prove my worship.”

“How glibly you say these things! There will have been queens in other lists in which you have borne off the palm. Have you talked so to them?”

===Chinese===
“卡尔马尼奥拉，我的朋友……”

“是您的朋友，而且不止是朋友，夫人。”

“哦？比朋友更进一层，还能是什么呢？”

“是一个男人能成为一个女子的一切，我的瓦莱里娅。我是您的骑士。打从米兰（Milan）比武场那一天起，当您亲手将象征胜利的棕榈枝颁给我时，我便已是您的骑士了。能为您而战，我甘之如饴；倘若需要以死来明证我对您的崇敬，我也赴汤蹈火、在所不辞。”

“这番甜言蜜语，您说得可真顺溜！您在别的比武场上摘得桂冠时，想必也有过别的女主人吧。您对她们，是不是也说过同样的话？”

===Original===
“O cruelty!” he cried out like a man in pain. “That you should say this to me! I am swooning at your feet, Valeria, you wonder of the world!”

“My nose, sir, is too long for that!” She mocked him, but with an underlying tenderness; and tenderness there was too in her moist eyes. “You are a whirlwind in your wooing as in the lists. You are reckless, sir.”

“Is it a fault? A soldier’s fault, then. But I’ll be patient if you bid me. I’ll be whatsoever you bid me, Valeria. But when we come to Casale﻿ ﻿…”

He paused for words, and she took advantage of that pause to check him.

“It is unlucky to plan upon something not yet achieved, sir. Wait﻿ ﻿… wait until that time arrives.”

===Chinese===
“啊，您太残忍了！”他如同痛彻心扉般喊道，“您竟忍心对我说这种话！瓦莱里娅，我早已拜倒在您的石榴裙下神魂颠倒，您真是世间独一无二的奇观！”

“阁下，我的鼻子可太长了，当不起这‘奇观’二字！”她打趣着他，话音里却藏着一缕柔情；她那双湿润的眼眸中，也流露着同样的温存。“您求起爱来，简直像您在比武场上一样势如疾风。您太孟浪了，阁下。”

“这算过错吗？若算，那也是个武夫的毛病。但只要您吩咐，我便学着忍耐。您要我怎样，我便怎样，瓦莱里娅。可等我们打进卡萨莱之后……”

他一时语塞，稍作停顿，她正好趁机打断了他。

“阁下，尚未做成之事便提前盘算，是不吉利的。等等吧……等那一刻真正到来再说。”

===Original===
“And then?” he asked her breathlessly. “And then?”

“Have I not said that to plan is unlucky?”

Boldly he read the converse of that statement. “I’ll not tempt fortune, then. I dare not. I will be patient, Valeria.”

But he let it appear that his confidence was firm, and she added nothing now to shake it.

And so in ardent wooing whilst he waited for his bridge, Carmagnola spent most of the time that he was not engaged in directing the construction of it. Bellarion in those days sulked like Achilles in his tent, with a copy of Vegetius which he had brought from Milan in his baggage.

===Chinese===
“到那时又怎样呢？”他屏息追问，“到那时又怎样呢？”

“我不是刚说过，提前盘算是不吉利的吗？”

他胆大包天地从她这话的反面读出了弦外之音：“那我便不去试探命运了。我不敢冒那个险。我会耐心等待的，瓦莱里娅。”

不过他神态间流露出十足的笃定与自信，而她此刻也没有再多说什么去动摇他的这份念头。

于是，在等待桥梁落成的日子里，卡尔马尼奥拉一有闲暇不督工，便把大半光阴都花在了热烈求爱上。而贝拉里翁那段日子则像阿喀琉斯（Achilles）一样闷在营帐里生闷气，手里捧着一卷从米兰行李中带来的韦格蒂乌斯（Vegetius）兵书。

===Original===
The bridges took, not a week, but eleven days to build.
