===Original===
Valeria calmed them. “Don’t you see, Messer Carmagnola, that he but uses you as a whipping-boy instead of me. It is I who am the fool, the numskull in his eyes; for these deeds are more mine than any other’s. But my old friend Barbaresco is too courteous to say so.”

“Courteous?” snorted Carmagnola. “That is the last term I should apply to his boorishness. By what right does he come hectoring here?”

“By the right of his old affection for me and my brother. That is what makes him hot. For my sake, then, bear with him, sir.”

The great man bowed, his hand upon his heart, signifying that for her sake there was no indignity he would not suffer.

Thereafter he defended himself with great dignity. If the letter had been all, he might have taken Barbaresco’s views. But it was, he repeated, the traitor Bellarion’s avowed intention to raise the siege. That, in itself, was a proof of his double-dealing.

===Chinese===
瓦莱里娅好言安抚住他们。“您难道看不出来吗，卡尔马尼奥拉先生，他不过是拿您当替罪羊，代我挨骂罢了。在他眼里，真正的蠢货、榆木脑袋是我——因为这些事大半出自我手，而非别人。只是我的老朋友巴巴雷斯科顾念礼数，不好意思当面这么说我罢了。”

“顾念礼数？”卡尔马尼奥拉冷哼一声，“他这般粗鄙无礼，我最不会拿‘礼数’二字来形容他。他凭什么权利跑到这里来盛气凌人？”

“凭他对我和弟弟多年不变的深情厚谊。正是这份情谊才让他如此激愤。那么，看在我的份上，请阁下容忍他这一回吧。”

这位大人物鞠了一躬，手按胸口，表示只要为了她，受再大的委屈他也在所不辞。

随后，他极有尊严地为自己辩解起来。倘若只有这封信，他或许也会采信巴巴雷斯科的看法。但他反复强调，叛徒贝拉里翁公开宣称要撤围解兵一事摆在那里。单凭这一点，就足以证明他两面三刀。

===Original===
“How did this letter come to you?” Barbaresco asked.

Gian Giacomo answered whilst Valeria added in bitter self-reproach, “And this messenger was never examined, although Bellarion demanded that he should be brought before us.”

“Let us waste it now,” said Barbaresco.

“To what purpose, sir?”

“Why, to beguile our leisure. No other entertainment offers.”

===Chinese===

“小姐，您这是在拿这事责怪我吗？”卡尔马尼奥拉叫道，“他不过是个可怜的乡巴佬，什么也说不出来。不审他，是因为审了也是白费工夫。”

“那咱们现在就白费一回工夫吧，”巴巴雷斯科说道。

“为了什么呢，阁下？”

===Original===
Carmagnola contained himself under that sardonic leer.

“Sir, you are resolved, it seems, to try my patience. It requires all my regard and devotion for her highness to teach me to endure it. The messenger shall be brought.”

At Valeria’s request not only the messenger, but the captains who had voted Bellarion’s death were also summoned. Carmagnola demurred at first, but bowed in the end to her stern insistence.

They came, and when they were all assembled, they were told by the Princess why they had been summoned as well as what she had that morning learnt from Barbaresco. Then the messenger was brought in between the guards, and it was the Princess herself who questioned him.

“You have nothing to fear, boy,” she assured him gently, as he cowered in terror before her. “You are required to answer truthfully. When you have done so, and unless I discover that you are lying, you shall be restored to liberty.”

===Chinese===
面对那副满怀讽意的狞笑，卡尔马尼奥拉强压下怒火。

“阁下，看来您是铁了心要考验我的耐心了。若非我对殿下怀有万分敬重与赤诚，断难忍受这般挑衅。把信使带上来吧。”

应瓦莱里娅的要求，不仅信使被带了进来，先前投票赞成处死贝拉里翁的几位队长也一并被传唤到场。卡尔马尼奥拉起初颇有推诿之意，但最终还是屈服于她斩钉截铁的坚持。

===Original===
Carmagnola, who had come to take his stand at her side, bent over her.

“Prudent or not, it is promised.” There was in her tone an asperity that dismayed him. She addressed herself to the clown.

“When you were given this letter you would be given precise instructions for its delivery, were you not?”

“Yes, magnificent madonna.”

“What were those instructions?”

===Chinese===
早已走过来站在她身旁的卡尔马尼奥拉俯下身去，低声说道：

===Original===

===Chinese===

===Original===
The Princess leaned forward, and she was not the only one to move.

“Were you told or did you know what soldiers occupied the section of the lines to which you were bidden?”

“I just knew that they were soldiers of the besieging army, or the Lord Bellarion’s army. I am telling you the truth, madonna. I was told to be careful to go straight, and not to wander into any other part of the line but that.”

Ugolino da Tenda made a sharp forward movement. “What are you saying?”

“The truth! The truth!” cried the lad in terror. “May God strike me dumb forever if I have uttered a lie.”

“Quiet! Quiet!” the Princess admonished him. “Be sure we know when you speak the truth. Keep to it and fear nothing. Did you hear mention of any name in connection with that section of the line?”

===Chinese===
公主身子微微前倾，动容的也不止她一人。

“他们有没有告诉你，或者你自己知不知道，派你去的这一段阵线是由哪支兵马驻守的？”

“我只知道那是围城大军的兵，或者说是贝拉里翁大人的兵。小姐，我说的都是真话。他们再三叮嘱我要直直往前走，千万别拐到防线的别处去。”

乌戈利诺·达·滕达（Ugolino da Tenda）猛地往前跨了一步。“你说什么？”

“真话！全都是真话！”那小伙子吓得喊了起来，“我要是敢撒半句谎，就叫老天爷劈死我，让我一辈子变成哑巴。”

“安静！安静！”公主厉声劝住他，“放心，你是不是在说真话，我们自有分辨。只要照实说，什么也不用怕。他们提起这一段防线的时候，你有没有听见他们提到什么名字？”

===Original===
“Did I?” He searched his mind, and his eyes brightened. “Aye, aye, I did. They spoke amongst them. They named one Calmaldola, or﻿ ﻿… Carmandola﻿ ﻿…”

“Or Carmagnola,” da Tenda cut in, and laughed splutteringly in sheer contempt. “It’s clear, I think, that Theodore’s letter was intended for just the purpose that it’s served.”

“Clear? How is it clear?” Carmagnola’s contempt was in the question.

“In everything, now that we have heard this clown. Why was he sent to the southern section? Do you suppose Theodore did not know that Valsassina himself and those directly under him, of whom I was one, were quartered in Quinto, on the western side?” Then his voice swelled up in anger. “Why was this messenger not examined sooner, or﻿ ﻿…” he checked and his eyes narrowed as they fixed themselves on Carmagnola’s flushed and angry face “… or, was he?”

“Was he?” roared Carmagnola. “Now what the devil do you mean?”

===Chinese===
“提没提到？”他绞尽脑汁回想着，眼睛忽然一亮，“有，有，提到了。他们几个在自个儿说话，嘴里念叨着一个叫卡尔马尔多拉（Calmaldola），还是……卡尔曼多拉（Carmandola）的人……”

“还是卡尔马尼奥拉，”达·滕达（da Tenda）冷笑着打断了他的话，满脸尽是鄙夷，“我看这事再明白不过了：泰奥多罗那封信，正是为了达到如今这个效果才写出来的。”

“明白？怎么就明白了？”卡尔马尼奥拉反问道，语气里同样带着轻蔑。

“听完这乡巴佬的话，一切都清清楚楚了。为什么要派他往南段防线去？难道你以为泰奥多罗不知道瓦尔萨西纳（Valsassina）本人和他的直属部众——其中也包括我——都驻扎在西边的昆托吗？”说到这里，他的声音因愤怒而陡然拔高，“为什么不早些审问这个信使，或者说……”他顿住话头，双目微眯，死死盯住卡尔马尼奥拉那张涨红发怒的脸，“……难道其实早就审过了？”

“早就审过了？”卡尔马尼奥拉怒吼道，“你这混账到底是什么意思？”

===Original===
“You know what I mean, Carmagnola. You led us all within an ace of doing murder. Did you lead us so because you’re a fool, or a villain? Which?”

Carmagnola sprang for him, roaring like a bull. The other captains got between, and the Princess on her feet, commanding, imperious, added her voice sharply to theirs to restore order. They obeyed that slim, frail woman, scarcely more than a girl, as she stood there straight and tense in her wine-coloured mantle, her red-gold head so proudly held, her dark eyes burning in her white face.

“Captain Ugolino, that was ill said of you,” she reproved him. “You forget that if this messenger was not examined before, the blame for that is upon all of us. We took too much for granted and too readily against the Prince of Valsassina.”

“It is now that you take too much for granted,” answered Carmagnola. “Why did Valsassina intend to raise this siege if he is honest? Answer me that!”

===Chinese===
“你心里清楚我是什么意思，卡尔马尼奥拉。你差一点就把我们所有人都领上了谋害忠良的绝路。你这么领着我们走，究竟是因为你是个蠢货，还是个奸贼？到底是哪一种？”

卡尔马尼奥拉如公牛般咆哮着向他猛扑过去。其余几位队长连忙上前隔开两人，公主也霍然站起，神态凛然威严，清亮锐利的声音压过众人，喝止了这场混乱。她站在那儿，一袭紫红斗篷裹着纤弱瘦削的身躯，年纪虽不过是个少女，可那满头红金色秀发高傲地昂起，苍白的面庞上一双黑眸灼灼生辉，教在场众将无不俯首听命。

“乌戈利诺队长，这话你说得太失分寸了，”她责备道，“你别忘了，如果这个信使此前未曾受审，这份过错也在我们大家身上。是我们对瓦尔萨西纳亲王先入为主、太过轻信流言了。”

“现在才是你们太过轻信呢，”卡尔马尼奥拉反唇相讥，“要是瓦尔萨西纳问心无愧，他为什么打算撤围？谁来回答我这个问题！”

===Original===
His challenge was to all. Ugolino da Tenda answered it.

“For some such reason as he had when he sent his men to hold the bridge at Carpignano while you were building bridges here. Bellarion’s intentions are not clear to dull eyes like yours and mine, Carmagnola.”

Carmagnola considered him malevolently. “You and I will discuss this matter further elsewhere,” he promised him. “You have used expressions I am not the man to forget.”

“It may be good for you to remember them,” said the young captain, no whit intimidated. “Meanwhile, madonna, I take my leave. I march my condotta out of this camp within an hour.”

She looked at him in sudden distress. He answered the look.

“I am grieved, madonna. But my duty is to the Prince of Valsassina. I was seduced from it by too hasty judgment. I return to it at once.” He bowed low, gathered up his cloak, and went clanking out.

===Chinese===
他这一问，是向在场所有人发难。接下这记挑战的是乌戈利诺·达·滕达。

“大概就像他当初派兵去死守卡尔皮尼亚诺（Carpignano）的桥梁、而你却只顾着在这里造桥时所怀的苦心吧。贝拉里翁的谋略，岂是你我这等凡眼俗胎所能看透的，卡尔马尼奥拉。”

卡尔马尼奥拉阴狠地上下打量着他。“你我日后自会找个地方把这笔账算清，”他咬牙切齿地撂下话，“你方才用的字眼，我可不是轻易能忘的人。”

“记在心里兴许对你有好处，”年轻的队长丝毫不为所动，说道，“眼下，小姐，我要向您告辞了。一个时辰之内，我便率领我的雇佣兵团（condotta）拔营离开。”

她闻言一惊，流露出满面忧色。他读懂了她的眼神。

“小姐，我也深感遗憾。但我的效忠对象是瓦尔萨西纳亲王。此前我一时轻率盲从，偏离了本分；如今我自当立刻重归正途。”他深深一鞠躬，拢起斗篷，盔甲铿锵作响地大步走了出去。

===Original===
“Hold there!” Carmagnola thundered after him. “Before you go I’ve an account to settle with you.”

Ugolino turned on the threshold, drawn up to his full height.

“I’ll afford you the opportunity,” said he, “but only after I have the answer to my question, whether you are a villain or a fool, and only if I find that you’re a fool.”

The captains made a barrier which Carmagnola could not pass. Livid with anger and humiliation, his grand manner dissipated, he turned to the Princess.

“Will your highness suffer me to go after him? He must not be permitted to depart.”

But she shook her red-gold head. “Nay, sir. I detain no man here against his inclinations. And Captain Ugolino seems justified of his.”

===Chinese===
“站住！”卡尔马尼奥拉在他身后雷霆般大喝，“你走之前，我还有笔账要跟你算！”

乌戈利诺在门槛上转过身，挺直了颀长的身躯。

“这个机会我自会给你，”他说，“但前提是得先弄明白我方才问的那个问题——你究竟是个奸贼，还是个蠢货——而且，只有当我发现你不过是个蠢货的时候，我才会奉陪。”

几位队长筑起一道人墙，拦住了卡尔马尼奥拉的去路。他气得面色铁青、奇耻大辱，平日的赫赫威仪荡然无存，只得转向公主。

“殿下肯准许我去追他吗？绝不能放任他这样一走了之。”

然而她摇了摇那头红金色的秀发。“不，阁下。我从不违背任何人的意愿强留他人。何况依我看，乌戈利诺队长此举倒像是理直气壮。”

===Original===
“Justified! Dear God! Justified!” He apostrophised the groined ceiling, then swung to the other four captains standing there. “And you?” he demanded. “Do you also deem yourselves justified to mutiny?”

Belluno was prompt to answer. But then Belluno was his own lieutenant. “My lord, if there has been an error we are all in it, and have the honesty to admit it.”

“I am glad there is still some honesty among you. And you?” His angry eyes swept over the others. One by one they answered as Belluno had done. But they were men of little account, and the defection of the four of them would not have reduced the army as did Ugolino’s, whose condotta amounted to close upon a thousand men.

===Chinese===
“理直气壮！天哪！理直气壮！”他仰望着交叉肋拱天花板高声呼喊，接着猛然转身面向站在那里的另外四位队长。“你们呢？”他厉声质问，“难道你们也觉得自己有理哗变吗？”

贝卢诺（Belluno）抢先作答——不过话说回来，贝卢诺本就是他自己的副官。“大人，若真是出了差错，我们大家都有份，也都有诚心认错的勇气。”

“我很欣慰你们当中还有几分诚实。你们呢？”他怒火中烧的目光扫过其余几人。他们一个个都像贝卢诺那样表了态。然而这些人本就无足轻重，即便他们四个一齐倒戈，也不会像乌戈利诺那样重创全军——毕竟乌戈利诺麾下的雇佣兵团足有近千人之众。

===Original===
“We are forgetting this poor clown,” said the Princess.

Carmagnola looked at him as if he would with joy have wrung his neck.

“You may go, boy,” she told him. “You are free. See that he leaves unhindered.”

He went with his guards. The captains, dismissed, went out next.

Carmagnola, his spirit badly bruised and battered, looked at the Princess, who had sunk back into her chair.

===Chinese===
“咱们把这可怜的乡巴佬给忘了，”公主说道。

卡尔马尼奥拉瞪着那小子，看那神情恨不得亲手拧断他的脖子才痛快。

“你可以走了，孩子，”她对他说，“你自由了。去看着，让他顺顺利利地离开，别阻拦。”

他跟着卫兵出去了。几位队长得了遣散，随后也退了出去。

心神受创、灰头土脸的卡尔马尼奥拉望向公主，只见她已无力地跌坐回椅子里。

===Original===
“However it has been achieved,” she said, “Theodore’s ends could not better have been served. What is left us now?”

“If I might venture to advise﻿ ﻿…” quoth Barbaresco, smooth as oil, “I should say that you could not do better than follow Ugolino da Tenda’s example.”

“What?”

“Return to your fealty to Bellarion.”

“Return?” Carmagnola leaned towards him from his fine height, and his mouth gaped. “Return?” he repeated. “And leave Vercelli?”

“Why not? That would no more than fulfil Bellarion’s intention to raise the siege. He will have an alternative.”

===Chinese===
“不管这局面是怎么闹成的，”她说，“泰奥多罗的算盘再没有比现在更如意的了。如今我们还剩什么？”

“倘若容我进一言……”巴巴雷斯科油滑得像抹了油一般说道，“依我看，您眼下最明智的做法，莫过于效仿乌戈利诺·达·滕达的榜样。”

“什么？”

“重归您对贝拉里翁的效忠。”

“重归？”卡尔马尼奥拉凭着高大的身躯朝他倾过身来，惊得目瞪口呆，“重归？”他重复了一遍，“然后放弃韦尔切利（Vercelli）？”

“有何不可？这不过是顺应贝拉里翁撤围的原意罢了。他心里定然另有妙计。”

===Original===
“I care nothing for his alternatives, and let us be clear upon this: I owe him no fealty. My fealty was sworn not to him, but to the Duchess Beatrice. And my orders from Duke Filippo Maria are to assist in the reduction of Vercelli. I know where my duly lies.”

“It is possible,” said the Princess slowly, “that Bellarion had some other plan for bringing Theodore to his knees.”

He stared at her. There was pain in his handsome eyes. His face was momentarily almost convulsed. And there was little more than pain in his voice when he spoke.

“Oh, madonna! Into what irreparable error is your generous heart misleading you? How can you have come in a breath to place all your trust in this man whom for years you have known, as many know him, for a scheming villain?”

“Could I do less having discovered the cruelty of my error?”

===Chinese===
“他的妙计我毫不在乎，而且把话说清楚：我并不欠他什么忠义。我宣誓效忠的不是他，而是贝阿特丽切（Beatrice）公爵夫人。而菲利波·玛丽亚公爵给我的军令，是协助攻克韦尔切利。我深知自己的职责所在。”

“说不定，”公主缓缓说道，“贝拉里翁另有一套让泰奥多罗俯首称臣的方略。”

他定定地凝视着她。那双俊美的眼睛里流露出痛苦，整张脸庞一时间几乎有些扭曲，开口时嗓音里也几乎只剩下了痛楚。

“哦，小姐！您那颗宽厚仁慈的心，究竟要把您引向怎样无可挽回的歧途啊？这个男人，您多年来早已像许多人一样看透了他是个工于心计的奸雄，怎么转瞬之间就把全部的信任都托付给他了呢？”

“我既然发觉自己犯下了那样残酷的过错，难道还能少做一点弥补吗？”

===Original===
“Are you sure﻿—can you be sure upon such slight grounds﻿—that you were in error? That you are not in error now? You heard what Belluno said of him on the night my bridges were destroyed﻿—that Bellarion never looks where he aims.”

“That, sir, is what has misled me, to my present shame.”

“Is it not rather what is misleading you now?”

“You heard what Messer Barbaresco had to tell me.”

“I do not need to hear Messer Barbaresco or any other. I know what I can see for myself, what my wits tell me.”

===Chinese===
“您确定吗——凭着这么点儿微不足道的凭据，您真能确定自己先前错了吗？能确定您现在没有再错吗？当初我的浮桥被毁那一夜，贝卢诺的话您也听见了——贝拉里翁瞄准哪儿，眼睛从不往哪儿看。”

“阁下，当初正是这句话误导了我，才害我落到如今这步田地，追悔莫及。”

“莫非现在误导您的，不正是另一番话吗？”

“巴巴雷斯科先生方才告诉我的一切，您也亲耳听见了。”

“我不需要听信巴巴雷斯科先生或任何别人的话。我只相信自己亲眼所见，只相信我自己的判断力。”

===Original===
She looked at him almost slyly, for one normally so wide-eyed, and her answer all considered was a little cruel.

“Are you still unshaken in your confidence in your wits? Do you still think that you can trust them?”

That was the deathblow to his passion for her, as it was the deathblow of the high hopes he is suspected of having centred in her, seeing himself, perhaps, as the husband of the Princess Valeria of Montferrat, supreme in Montferrine court and camp. It was a sword-thrust full into his vanity, which was the vital part of him.

He stepped back, white to the very lips, his countenance disordered. Then, commanding himself, he bowed, and steadied his voice to answer.

===Chinese===
她几乎带了点狡黠地望向他——对于向来目光坦率清澈的她而言实属罕见；而且平心而论，她的回答着实有些残忍。

“经历过这一切，您对自己的判断力竟然还如此深信不疑？您还真觉得自己的脑子靠得住吗？”

这一击彻底断送了他对她的痴情，也粉碎了人人都猜到他曾寄托在她身上的宏图美梦——或许他曾幻想自己能迎娶蒙费拉托的瓦莱里娅公主，从此在蒙费拉托的朝堂与军营中独揽大权、睥睨群雄。这一剑正刺中了他的虚荣心，而那恰恰是他身上最致命的要害。

他踉跄着退后一步，嘴唇瞬间褪尽血色，神情一片仓皇。随即，他强自收敛心神，深深一躬，稳住声线答道：

===Original===
“Madonna, I see that you have made your choice. My prayer will be that you may not have occasion to repent it. No doubt the troops accompanying these gentlemen of Montferrat will be your sufficient escort to Mortara, or you may join forces with Ugolino da Tenda’s condotta. Although I shall be left with not more than half the men the enterprise demands, with these I must make shift to reduce Vercelli, as my duty is. Thus, madonna, you may yet owe your deliverance to me. May God be with you!” He bowed again.

Perhaps he hoped still for some word to arrest him, some retraction of the injustice with which she used him. But it did not come.

“I thank you for your good intentions, my lord,” she said civilly. “God be with you, too.”

He bit his lip, then turned, and threw high that handsome golden head which he was destined to leave, some few years later, between the pillars of the Piazzetta in Venice. Thus he stalked out. All considered, it was an orderly retreat; and that was the last she ever saw of him.

As the door banged, Barbaresco smacked his great thigh with his open palm and exploded into laughter.

===Chinese===
“小姐，我看出您心意已决。我唯愿祈祷上苍保佑，但愿您日后切莫有追悔莫及之日。有这几位蒙费拉托诸君麾下的兵马相随，想必已足以为您护驾前往莫尔塔拉（Mortara）；您也可以去与乌戈利诺·达·滕达的雇佣兵团汇合。虽说我手下留下的兵力不过是这场战事所需的一半罢了，但凭着这点人马，我也必当勉力攻克韦尔切利，以尽我的本分。如此一来，小姐，您日后或许仍要仰仗我才得脱困。愿上帝与您同在！”他又深深行了一礼。

或许他还期盼着能听到一句挽留的话，或是她收回对他不公的苛责。然而，这句话始终没有出口。

“多谢您的美意，大人，”她客客气气地说道，“也愿上帝与您同在。”

他咬了咬嘴唇，转过身，高高扬起那颗英俊的金色头颅——几年之后，这颗头颅注定要被斩落于威尼斯（Venice）小广场（Piazzetta）的那两根石柱之间。就这样，他昂首阔步地走了出去。平心而论，这场退场还算体面有度；而这，也是她最后一次见到他。

房门刚“砰”地一声关上，巴巴雷斯科便摊开蒲扇般的大掌狠狠拍在大腿上，爆发出了一阵哄堂大笑。

## XIII The Occupation of Casale / 十三 占领卡萨莱
===Original===

When Bellarion proclaimed his intention of raising the siege of Vercelli, he had it in mind, in view of the hopelessness of being able to reduce the place reasonably soon, to draw Theodore into the open by means of that strategic movement which Thucydides had taught him, and to which he had so often already and so successfully had recourse.
His Swiss, being without baggage, travelled lightly and swiftly. They left their camp before Vercelli on the night of Wednesday, and on the evening of the following Friday, Bellarion brought them into the village of Pavone, where Koenigshofen had established himself in Facino’s old quarters of three years ago. There they lay for the night. But whilst his weary followers rested, himself he spent the greater part of the night in the necessary dispositions for striking camp at dawn. And very early on that misty November morning he was off again with Giasone Trotta, Koenigshofen, and all the horse, leaving Stoffel to follow more at leisure with the foot, the baggage, and the artillery.
Before nightfall he was at San Salvatore, where his army rested, and on the following Sunday morning at just about the time that Barbaresco was reaching Vercelli, Bellarion, Prince of Valsassina, was approaching the Lombard Gate into Casale, by the road along which he had fled thence years before, a nameless outcast waif whose only ambition was the study of Greek at Pavia.
He had travelled by many roads since then, and after long delays he had reached Pavia, no longer as a poor nameless scholar, but as a condottiero of renown, not to solicit at the University the alms of a little learning, but to command whatever he might crave of the place, holding even its Prince in subjection. Greek he had not learnt; but he had learnt much else instead, though nothing that made him love his fellow man or hold the world in high regard. Therefore, he was glad to think that here he touched the end of that long journey begun five years ago along this Lombard Road; the mission upon which he had set out blindly that day was, after many odd turns of Fortune, all but accomplished. When it was done, he would strip off this soldier’s harness, abdicate his princely honours, and return on foot﻿—humbler than when he had set out, and cured of his erstwhile heresy﻿—to the benign and peaceful shelter of the convent at Cigliano.

===Chinese===

贝拉里翁（Bellarion）宣告解围韦尔切利（Vercelli）之意时，心里想的是：既然短期内攻下此城全然无望，便用修昔底德（Thucydides）教他的那一手战略调动，把西奥多（Theodore）诱到开阔地来——这一手他已用过多次，回回得手。

他的瑞士部下没有辎重，行军轻疾。星期三夜里他们撤出韦尔切利城外的营寨；星期五傍晚，贝拉里翁把他们带进帕沃内（Pavone）村——柯尼希斯霍芬（Koenigshofen）已在那里安顿下来，驻的正是三年前法奇诺（Facino）的旧营。他们在村里歇了一夜。可当疲惫的部下休息时，他本人却把大半夜花在拂晓拔营的必要部署上。十一月那个雾蒙蒙的清晨，天刚破晓他又上路了，带着贾索内·特罗塔（Giasone Trotta）、柯尼希斯霍芬和全部骑兵，留施托费尔（Stoffel）押着步兵、辎重和炮队随后从容跟进。

天黑前他到了圣萨尔瓦托雷，大军在那里歇息；下一个礼拜天早晨，恰在巴巴雷斯科（Barbaresco）抵达韦尔切利的同时，瓦尔萨西纳亲王贝拉里翁正走近卡萨莱（Casale）的伦巴第门——走的正是几年前他从那里逃走的路：那时他是个无名的、被逐出门的流浪儿，唯一的抱负是去帕维亚（Pavia）读希腊文。

此后他走了不知多少条路；几经耽搁，他终于到了帕维亚——不再是那个无名的穷书生，而是一位声名显赫的雇佣兵统帅（condottiero）；不是来向大学乞讨一星半点的学问，而是来对这座城予取予求，连它的亲王也在他掌中。希腊文他没有学成；可他学到了许多别的东西——只是没有一样叫他爱人，或叫他把这世界看高。所以此刻他很欣慰地想：五年前沿着这条伦巴第大道开始的长途，在这里到了尽头；当年盲目踏上的一趟使命，几经命运的种种奇转，如今即将完成。事成之后，他要卸下这身军装，辞去亲王的尊荣，步行回去——比出发时更谦卑，也医好了早年的乖谬——回到奇利亚诺（Cigliano）修道院那仁厚安宁的荫庇里去。

===Original===

There was no attempt to bar his entrance into the Montferrine capital. The officer commanding the place knew himself without the necessary means to oppose this force which so unexpectedly came to demand admittance. And so, the people of Casale, issuing from Mass on that Sunday morning, found the great square before Liutprand’s Cathedral and the main streets leading from it blocked by outlandish men-at-arms﻿—Italians, Gascons, Burgundians, Swabians, Saxons, and Swiss﻿—whose leader proclaimed himself Captain-General of the army of the Marquis Gian Giacomo of Montferrat.
It was a proclamation that not at all reassured them of their dread at the presence of a rapacious and violent soldiery.
The Council of Ancients, summoned by Bellarion’s heralds, assembled in the Communal Palace, to hear the terms of this brigand captain﻿—as they conceived him﻿—who had swooped upon their defenceless city.
He came attended by a group of officers. He was tall and soldierly of bearing, in full armour, save for his helm, which was borne after him by a page, and his escort, from the brawny, bearded Koenigshofen to the fierce-eyed, ferrety Giasone, was calculated to inspire dread in peaceful citizens. But his manner was gentle, and his words were fair.
“Sirs, your city of Casale has nothing to fear from this occupation, for it is not upon its citizens that we make war, and so that they give no provocation, they will find my followers orderly. We invite your alliance with ourselves in the cause of right and justice. But if you withhold this alliance we shall not visit it against you, provided that you do not go the length of actively opposing us.
“The High and Mighty Lord Filippo Maria Visconti, Duke of Milan, weary of the encroachments upon his dominions resulting from the turbulent ambition of your Prince-Regent, the Marquis Theodore, has resolved to make an end of a regency which in itself has already become an usurpation, and to place in the authority to which his majority entitles him your rightful Prince, the Marquis Gian Giacomo Paleologo. I invite you, sirs, to perform your duty as representatives of the people by swearing upon my hands fealty to that same Marquis Gian Giacomo in the cathedral at the hour of vespers this evening.”
That invitation was a command, and it was punctually obeyed by men who had not the strength to resist.

===Chinese===

没有谁试图拦他进蒙费拉托（Montferrat）的都城。守城的军官自知没有力量抵挡这支突然前来叫门的大军。就这样，那个礼拜天的早晨，卡萨莱的民众做完弥撒出来，发现柳特普兰德大教堂前的大广场和通它的各条大街，都被一伙异样的甲兵堵满了——意大利人、加斯科涅人（Gascons）、勃艮第人、士瓦本人、萨克森人、瑞士人——为首的宣告自己是蒙费拉托侯爵吉安·贾科莫（Gian Giacomo）殿下军队的统帅。

这样一纸宣告，丝毫不曾缓和他们看见一支贪暴的兵马临城的恐惧。

贝拉里翁的传令官召来的元老议事会，齐集公议宫，来听这位——在他们想来——扑向他们不设防的城的强盗头子开条件。

他由一群军官陪同而来。他身材高大，一派军人的气概，全身披挂，只差头盔——由一名侍童捧在身后；他的随员，从虬髯戟张、膀大腰圆的柯尼希斯霍芬到目光凶悍、尖嘴猴腮的贾索内，桩桩件件都是算计好了要叫安分的市民胆寒的。可他的态度温和，言辞也漂亮。

「诸位先生，你们的卡萨莱城于这次进驻无所畏惧；我们打的不是它的市民，只要他们不挑衅，自会发现我的部下守规矩。我们邀你们结盟，共襄正义之师。你们若不肯结盟，我们也不加罪——只要你们不至于走到公然同我们作对的地步。

「尊贵威严的米兰（Milan）公爵菲利波·玛丽亚（Filippo Maria）·维斯孔蒂殿下，倦于贵摄政侯爵西奥多枭雄之志对公爵领地的步步侵凌，已决意终结这场本身已成僭据的摄政，把权柄交还给它合法的主人——已届亲政之年的贵侯爵吉安·贾科莫·帕莱奥洛戈（Gian Giacomo Paleologo）。我邀诸位先生，以人民代表的身份，今晚晚祷时分在大教堂向同一位吉安·贾科莫侯爵宣誓效忠，执我之手为证。」

这邀请便是命令；无力于抗拒的人，准时照办了。

===Original===

Meanwhile a measure of reassurance had been afforded the city by Bellarion’s proclamation enjoining order upon his troops. The proclamation was in no equivocal terms. It reminded the men that they were in occupation of a friendly city which they were sent to guard and defend, and that any act of pillage or violence would be punished by death. They were housed, some in the citadel, and the remainder in the fortress-palace of the Montferrine princes, where Bellarion himself took up his quarters.
In Theodore’s own closet, occupying the very chair in which Theodore had sat and so contemptuously received the unknown Bellarion on that day when the young student had first entered those august walls, Bellarion that night penned a letter to the Princess Valeria, wherein he gave her news of the day’s events. That letter, of a calligraphy so perfect that it might be mistaken for a page from some monkish manuscript of those days, is one of the few fragments that have survived from the hand of this remarkable man who was adventurer, statesman, soldier, and humanist.
“Most honoured and most dear lady,” he addresses her﻿—“*Riveritissima et Carissima Madonna.*” The exordium is all that need concern us now.

===Chinese===

与此同时，贝拉里翁约束军纪的告示也算给了这城一分定心。告示的措辞毫无含糊。它告诫部众：他们驻在一座友好的城里，是派来守卫和保卫它的；任何劫掠或强暴之行，一律处死。他们分驻各处：一部分在要塞，其余的在蒙费拉托亲王们的堡垒宫里——贝拉里翁自己也驻在那里。

当夜，在西奥多自己的私室里，坐在当年年轻的求学者初进那座威严宫墙、西奥多冷冷接待无名的贝拉里翁时所坐的同一把椅子上，贝拉里翁给瓦莱里娅公主（Valeria）修书一封，告诉她这一天的事。那封信，一手好字好得可以混作哪部僧侣抄本里的一页，是这位奇人——冒险家、政治家、军人兼人文学者——留世不多的手泽之一。

「最受尊敬、最亲爱的夫人，」他这样称呼她——「Riveritissima et Carissima Madonna（最受尊敬、最亲爱的夫人）」。开场白我们此刻只须提这一句。

===Original===

> Ever since at your own invitation I entered your service that evening in your garden here at Casale, where today I have again wandered reviving memories that are of the fairest in my life, that service has been my constant study. I have pursued it, by tortuous ways and by many actions appearing to have no bearing upon it, unsuspected by you when not actually mistrusted by you. That your mistrust has wounded me oftentimes and deeply, would have weighed lightly with me had I not perceived that by mistrusting you were deprived of that consolation and hope which you would have found in trusting. The facts afforded ever a justification of your mistrust. This I recognized; and that facts are stubborn things, not easily destroyed by words. Therefore I did not vainly wear myself in any endeavour to destroy them, but toiled on, so that, in the ultimate achievement of your selfless aims for your brother, the Marquis, I might prove to you without the need of words the true impulse of my every action in these past five years. The fame that came to me as a condottiero, the honours I won, and the increase of power they brought me I have never regarded as anything but weapons to be employed in this your service, as means to the achievement of your ends. But for that service accepted in this garden, my life would have been vastly different from all that it has been. No burden heavier than a scholar’s would have been mine, and today I might well be back with the brethren at Cigliano, an obscure member of their great brotherhood. To serve you, I have employed trickery and double-dealing until men have dubbed me a rogue, and some besides yourself have come to mistrust me, and once I went the length of doing murder. But I take no shame in any of these things, nor, most dear lady, need you take shame in that your service should have entailed them. The murder I did was the execution of a rogue; the conspiracy I scattered was one that would have made a net in which to take you; the deceits I have put upon the Marquis Theodore, chiefly when I made him serve my dear Lord Facino’s turn and seduced him into occupying Vercelli, so as subsequently to afford the Duke of Milan a sound reason for moving against him, were deceits employed against a deceiver, whom it would be idle to combat in honest fashion.

===Chinese===

> 自从那天傍晚，承您亲自相邀，我在卡萨莱您这座花园里进入您的麾下——今天我又在那里徘徊，重温一生中最美的记忆——为您效力便始终是我的功课。我循着曲折的路，做着许多看似与它无干的举动，追随着它；您不曾疑心时未察觉，疑心时更无从知。您的疑心一次次深深地伤了我；可我若不曾看出，您因疑心而失掉了信任本可给您的安慰和指望，这点伤原也算不得什么。事实永远替您的疑心作保。这一点我认；事实是硬东西，言语轻易毁不掉。所以我并不徒然费力于销毁事实，只是埋头苦干，好教您为令弟侯爵定下的无私目标最终达成之时，我不须言语，便向您证明这五年里我的每一举动的真实动机。我身为雇佣兵统帅得来的名声、赢得的荣衔和随之增长的权势，我从不当作别的，只当是为您这份差遣所用的兵器，当是达成您的目标的手段。若没有在这座园子里接下的这份差遣，我的一生会同实际的样样都不同。我挑的担子不会重过一个学者的，今天我多半已回到奇利亚诺的弟兄们中间，做他们那个伟大团体里一个无名的成员。为了效劳您，我用了权术和两面手法，直到人家叫我奸雄；除您之外也有人不再信我；有一回我甚至走到杀人的地步。可这些事我一概不以为耻；最亲爱的夫人，效劳您须付出这些，您也不必为之羞愧。我行的那桩谋杀，是处决一个恶棍；我搅散的那场阴谋，本是要织一张网拿您；我施在西奥多侯爵身上的那些骗局——尤其是我叫我亲爱的法奇诺大人借重于他、诱他占了韦尔切利、好叫米兰公爵随后有一个名正言顺的理由对他动手——都是对骗子用的骗术；同骗子堂堂正正地斗，是白费劲。

===Original===

In his eyes more than any other’s﻿—for he is not the only victim of the duplicity I have used to place you ultimately where you should be﻿—I am a double-dealing Judas. And it is said of me, too, that in the field as in the council, I prevail by subterfuge and never by straightforward blows. But my conscience remains tranquil. It is not what a man does or says that counts; but what a man intends. I have embraced as a part of my guiding philosophy that teaching of Plato’s which discriminates between the lie on the lips and the lie in the heart. On my lips and in my actions lies have been employed. I confess it frankly. But in my heart no lie has ever been. If I have employed at times dishonest means, at least the purpose for which they have been employed has been unfalteringly, unswervingly honest, and one in the final achievement of which there can be only pride and a sense of duty done.
> To this if you believe it﻿—and the facts will presently constrain you to do so, unless my fortune in the field should presently desert me﻿—I need add no details of the many steps in your service. By the light of faith in me from what is written and what is presently to do, you will now read aright those details for yourself.
> We touch now the goal whither all these efforts have been addressed.

===Chinese===

> 在他的眼里，我尤其是个两面三刀的犹大——因为为了把您最终送上您该在的位置，我两面手法收拾的受骗者不止他一个。人家还说，我在战场上、在议事厅里，靠的全是诡计，从不靠光明正大的打击。可我的良心安然。要紧的不是一个人做什么、说什么；是一个人存什么心。我把柏拉图那条教诲奉为我立身哲学的一部分：分清嘴上的谎和心里的谎。我嘴上、我的行动里用过谎。我坦白承认。可我心里从没有过谎。我若有时用了不诚实的手段，至少用它们的那份目的，从始至终是诚实的、不摇动的；这目的最终达成之日，有的只能是骄傲和尽了一份本分的自觉。
> 这一层您若信——事实马上就要逼您信了，除非我在战场上的运气此刻抛下我——我便无须再细数为您效力的一步步。凭着我写下的和即将做成的事所点燃的那点信，那些细节您如今自会读得分明。
> 如今我们触到了这一切努力所指的终点。

===Original===

Upon this follows his concise account of the events from the moment of his escape from Quinto, and upon that an injunction to her to come at once with her brother to Casale, depending upon the protection of his arm and the loyalty of a people which only awaits the sight of its rightful Prince to be increased to enthusiasm and active support.
That letter was despatched next day to Quinto, but it did not reach her until almost a week later between Alessandria and Casale.
Meanwhile early on the morrow the city was thrown into alarm by the approach of a strong body of horse. This was Ugolino da Tenda’s condotta, and Ugolino himself rode in with a trumpeter to make renewed submission to the Lord Bellarion, and to give him news of what had happened in Quinto upon the coming of Barbaresco.
Bellarion racked him with questions, as to what was said, particularly as to what the Princess said and how she looked, and what passed between her and Carmagnola. And when all was done, far from the stern reproaches Ugolino had been expecting he found himself embraced by a Bellarion more joyous than he had ever yet known that sardonic soldier.
That gaiety of Bellarion’s was observed by all in the days that followed. He was a man transformed. He displayed the lightheartedness of a boy, and moved about the many tasks claiming his attention with a song on his lips, a ready laugh upon the slightest occasion, and a sparkle in his great eyes that all had hitherto known so sombre.
And this notwithstanding that these were busy and even anxious days of preparation for the final trial of strength. He rode abroad during the day with two or three of his officers, one of whom was always Stoffel, surveying the ground of the peninsula that lies between Sesia and Po to the north of Casale, and at night he would labour over maps which he was preparing from his daily notes. Meanwhile he kept himself day by day informed, by means of a line of scouts which he had thrown out, of what was happening at Vercelli.
With that clear prescience, which in all ages has been the gift of all great soldiers, he was able not merely to opine but quite definitely to state the course of action that Theodore would pursue.

===Chinese===

随后是他从昆托（Quinto）脱身那一刻起诸事的简述；再往后是一句叮嘱，要她即刻携弟来卡萨莱，托庇于他的臂膀和一乡百姓的忠爱——那百姓只待一睹合法亲王的面容，便会燃起热忱和实干的拥戴。

那封信次日发往昆托，可直到差不多一礼拜后，才在亚历山德里亚（Alessandria）与卡萨莱之间送到她手里。

其间，次日一早，一支大队骑兵的逼近叫全城警慌。那是乌戈利诺·达·滕达（Ugolino da Tenda）的雇佣兵团（condotta）；乌戈利诺本人带着一名号手骑马进城，向贝拉里翁大人重新归顺，并禀报巴巴雷斯科抵达昆托后那里的种种。

贝拉里翁拿问题拷问他：说了什么话，尤其是公主说了什么、脸色如何、她同卡尔马尼奥拉（Carmagnola）之间过了什么话。等一切问完，乌戈利诺非但没有等来预想的雷霆申斥，反而被贝拉里翁一把抱住——这位冷嘲的军人，从未像此刻这样欢畅过。

随后几天，人人都看出了贝拉里翁这份高兴。他像换了一个人。他显出小孩子的没心没肺，在千头万绪的差事中间转来转去，嘴里哼着歌，芝麻大的事也笑，一双素来阴沉的大眼睛里闪闪发光。

尽管这些天正是为最后的实力较量的紧张备战之日。白天他带着两三名军官骑马出巡——其中总有施托费尔——踏勘卡萨莱北面塞西亚河（Sesia）与波河（the Po）之间那片半岛形的地；夜里他便伏在地图上，绘制拿每天的札记起草的图。与此同时，他撒出一线哨探，逐日掌握韦尔切利的动静。

凭着历朝历代一切伟大军人共有的那份清明预见，他不但能推测、简直能够断言西奥多将要采取的方略。

===Original===

Because of this, on the Wednesday of that week, he moved Ugolino da Tenda and his condotta out of Casale, and transferred them bag and baggage﻿—by night so that the movement might not be detected and reported to the enemy﻿—to the woods about Trino, where they were ordered to encamp and to lie close until required.
On the morning of Friday arrived at last in Casale the Marquis Gian Giacomo and his sister, escorted by the band of Montferrine exiles under Barbaresco and Casella, and the people turned out to welcome not only the Princes, but in many cases their own relatives and friends. Bellarion, with his captains and a guard of honour of fifty lances, received the Princes at the Lombard Gate, and escorted them to the palace where their apartments had been prepared.
The acclamations of the people lining the streets brought tears to the eyes of the Princess and a flush to the cheeks of her brother, and there were tears in her eyes when she sought Bellarion in his room to abase herself in the admission of her grievous misjudgment and to sue pardon for it.
“Your letter, sir,” she told him, “touched me more deeply than anything I can remember in all my life. Think me a fool if you must for what is past, but not an ingrate. My brother shall prove our gratitude so soon as ever it lies within his power.”
“Madonna, I ask no proofs of it, nor need them. To serve you has not been a means, but an end, as you shall see.”
“That vision at least does not lie in the future. I see now, and very clearly.”
He smiled, a little wistfully, as he bowed to kiss her hand.
“You shall see more clearly still,” he promised her.
That colloquy went no further. Stoffel broke in upon them to announce that his scouts had come galloping in from Vercelli with the news that the Lord Theodore had made a sally in force, shattering a way through Carmagnola’s besiegers, and that he was advancing on Casale with a well-equipped army computed to be between four and five thousand strong.
The news had already spread about the city, and was causing amongst the people the gravest apprehension and unrest. The prospect of a siege and of the subsequent vengeance of the Lord Theodore upon the city for having harboured his enemies filled them with dread.

===Chinese===

因此，那个礼拜三，他把乌戈利诺·达·滕达连同他的兵团调出卡萨莱，连人带装——趁夜转移，免得行动被敌人察觉报了上去——移到特里诺（Trino）一带的树林里，命他们扎营潜伏，候命待用。

礼拜五早晨，吉安·贾科莫侯爵同他的妹妹终于到了卡萨莱，由巴巴雷斯科和卡塞拉（Casella）率领的一队蒙费拉托流亡者护卫；百姓倾城相迎——迎的不仅是两位亲王，许多人迎的还是自家的亲眷朋友。贝拉里翁偕众队长和五十枪骑的仪仗，在伦巴第门迎候亲王兄妹，护送他们到宫里——殿宇已经备好。

夹道百姓的欢呼叫公主眼里涌出泪，叫她弟弟颊上飞起红；她到贝拉里翁房里找他，为自家的深重错判屈身认错、乞求宽宥时，眼里还噙着泪。

「您的信，先生，」她对他说，「打动我之深，是我一生记不起来的。过去的事，您要当我傻就当我傻；可别当我忘恩负义。我弟弟一有能力证明我们的感激，立刻就会证明。」

「夫人，我不求证明，也不需要。效劳您于我不是手段，是目的——您会见到的。」

「这番光景至少不在将来。我如今看清了，清清楚楚。」

他微微一笑，带着一点怅惘，躬身吻了她的手。

「您还会看得更清楚。」他许诺她。

这场会谈没有再深入。施托费尔闯进来禀报：哨探从韦尔切利飞马赶回，带来消息说西奥多大人大举出城突击，从卡尔马尼奥拉的围军里杀开一条血路，正以一支装备齐整、估计四五千人的大军进逼卡萨莱。

消息已在城里传开，在百姓中间引起极度的忧惶不安。一场围城、以及围城之后西奥多大人对这座窝藏了他仇敌的城池的报复——这前景叫他们胆战。

===Original===

“Send out trumpeters,” Bellarion ordered, “and let it be proclaimed in every quarter that there will be no siege, and that the army is marching out at once to meet the Marquis Theodore beyond the Po.”

===Chinese===

「派号手出去，」贝拉里翁下令，「传告四面八方：不会有围城；大军即刻出城，到波河对岸迎击西奥多侯爵。」

## XIV The Vanquished / 十四 败者
===Original===

Theodore’s sally from Vercelli had been made at daybreak on that Friday morning. It had been shrewdly planned, for Theodore was no bungler, and, before he had brought more than half his men into action, Carmagnola, startled by the suddenness of the blow that fell upon him, was routed and in flight.
After that, this being no more than the preliminary of the task before him, Theodore marched out every man of his following to go against Bellarion at Casale. Thus, by that ancient plan of attacking a vital point that had been left undefended, had Bellarion succeeded in drawing his enemy from a point of less importance in which he was almost impregnably entrenched. Theodore had perceived, as Bellarion had calculated that he would, that it could serve little purpose for him to hold an outpost like Vercelli if in the meantime the whole of his dominions were to be wrenched from his grasp.
No sooner was he gone, however, than Carmagnola, informed of his departure, rallied his broken troops, and with drums beating, trumpets blaring, and flags flying, marched like a conqueror into the now undefended city of Vercelli. For the resistance it had made, he subjected it to a cruel sack, giving his men unbounded licence, and that same evening he wrote to Duke Filippo Maria in the following terms:

> **Most Potent Duke and my Good Lord**﻿—It is my joyous task to give your highness tidings that, informed of the reduction in our numbers resulting from the defection of the Prince of Valsassina and several other captains acting in concert with him, the Lord Theodore of Montferrat, greatly presumptuous, did today issue from Vercelli for wager of battle against us. A vigorous action was fought in the neighbourhood of Quinto, in which despite our inferior numbers we put the Marquis to flight. Lacking numbers sufficient to engage in pursuit, particularly as this would have led us into Montferrine territory, and since the reoccupation of Vercelli and its restoration to your duchy was the task with which your highness entrusted us, I marched into the city at once, and I now hold it in the name of your exalted potency. By this complete and speedy victory I hope to merit the approbation of your highness.

===Chinese===

西奥多从韦尔切利突围，是那个礼拜五清晨天一亮发的。计划得精明——西奥多不是笨手；他还没把一半人马投入，猝不及防捱了这一击的卡尔马尼奥拉已经溃了、逃了。

此后，这只是他面前任务的开场；西奥多率全部人马开拔，去卡萨莱对付贝拉里翁。于是，凭那攻敌要害不设防之地的古老方略，贝拉里翁把敌人从一处他几乎据为铁桶的次要据点里引了出来——正如他算准的那样。西奥多看出了——贝拉里翁也算准他会看出：整个领地眼看要被人从掌中撜走，守住韦尔切利这样一座前哨，于他没什么用处。

可他前脚一走，得了讯的卡尔马尼奥拉后脚就收拢溃卒，鼓号齐鸣、旌旗招展，像个凯旋者开进了那座不设防的韦尔切利城。为着它作过的抵抗，他叫全城遭了一场酷烈的洗劫，纵兵无度；当晚他就给菲利波·玛丽亚公爵修书如下：

> **至威至严的公爵、我的好主上**——欣然寎告殿下：得悉瓦尔萨西纳亲王偕协同作乱的数名队长叛去、我军兵力因此折损，蒙费拉托的西奥多大人骄狂无状，今日果出韦尔切利，向我邀战。战于昆托左近，我军虽众寡不敌，仍将侯爵击溃。因兵力不足以穷追——况追则深入蒙费拉托境——且收复韦尔切利、归还殿下公国，正是殿下交付我等的任务，我当即进军入城，今已以至尊殿下之名据守之。凭此全胜之速，惟愿不负殿下的嘉许。

===Original===

Meanwhile Theodore’s march on Casale had anything but the aspect of a flight. The great siege train he dragged along with him over the sodden and too-yielding ground of that moist plain delayed his progress to such an extent that it was not until late on that November afternoon when he reached Villanova, here to receive news from his scouts that a considerable army, said to be commanded by the Prince of Valsassina, was circling northward from Terranova.
The news was unexpected and brought with it some alarm. He had gone confidently and rather carelessly forward fully expecting to find the enemy shut up in Casale. Hence all the ponderous siege train which had so hampered his progress. That Bellarion, forsaking the advantage of Casale’s stout walls, should come out to meet him and engage him in the open was something beyond his dreams, and but for the unexpectedness of it, he would have rejoiced in such a decision on the part of his redoubtable opponent.
It was in that unexpectedness, as usual, that lay Bellarion’s advantage. Theodore, compelled now to act in haste, not knowing at what moment the enemy might be upon him, made dispositions to which it was impossible to give that thought which the importance of the issues demanded. The first of these was to order the men, who were preparing to encamp for the night, to be up again and to push on and out of this village before they found themselves hemmed into it. That circling movement reported suggested this danger to Theodore.
They came out in rather straggling order to be marshalled even as they marched. Theodore’s aim, and it was shrewd enough, was to reach the broad causeway of solid land between Corno and Popolo, where marshlands on either side would secure his flanks and compel the enemy to engage him on a narrow front. What was to follow he had not yet had time to consider. But if he could reach that objective, he would be secure for the present, and he could rest his men in the two hamlets on the marshes.
But a mile beyond Villanova, Bellarion was upon his left flank and rear. He had little warning of it before the enemy was charging him. But it was warning enough. He threw out his line in a crescent formation, using his infantry in a manner which merited Bellarion’s entire approval, and obviously intent upon fighting a rearguard battle whilst bringing his army to the coveted position.

===Chinese===

与此同时，西奥多进军卡萨莱，全无败逃的模样。那列庞大的攻城辎重，在潮湿平原那片泡软了、太肯陷的地上一路拖磨，把行程耽搁到那样的地步：直到那个十一月的下午很晚了，他才到维拉诺瓦，在这里从哨探口中得到消息：一支可观的大军——据说由瓦尔萨西纳亲王统领——正从泰拉诺瓦向北包抄。

这消息出人意料，也带来几分惊惶。他一路走得自信而大意，满以为敌人会龟缩在卡萨莱城里。所以才拖了这满身笨重的攻重。贝拉里翁竟舍弃卡萨莱坚壁之利，出城同他野战——这超出了他的梦想；若非来得这样意外，这位可畏的对手作此决断，他倒要欢庆。

照例，贝拉里翁的优势正在这意外里。西奥多如今被迫仓促行事，不知敌人几时压到，作的部署来不及倾注事体所要求的那份思考。头一道部署是：正要扎营过夜的队伍重新起身，赶在被兜进村子之前推出村去。那报来的包抄之势，向西奥多点破了这一重危险。

他们零零落落开出村去，边行军边列队。西奥多的目标——也够精明——是抢到科尔诺与波波洛之间那道坚实的宽堤道上；两侧的沼泽保他的两翼，逼敌人在窄正面同他接战。接下去怎么办，他还来不及想。可只要抢到那个目标，眼下就稳了，还能让队伍在沼地里那两个小村歇息。

可出了维拉诺瓦才一英里，贝拉里翁就压上了他的左翼和后队。敌人冲来之前他几乎没有预警。可那预警尽够了。他把战线甩成一个新月阵，用兵之道深得贝拉里翁的赞赏；意图也分明：打一场后卫战，同时把大军带向那块宝地。

===Original===

But the infantry were not equal to their commander, and they were insufficiently trained in these tactics. Some horses were piked, but almost every horse piked meant an opening in the human wall that opposed the charge, and through these openings Giasone Trotta’s heavy riders broke in, swinging their ponderous maces. From a rearguard action on Theodore’s part, the thing grew rapidly to the proportions of a general engagement, and for this Theodore could not have been placed worse than he was with his left, now that he had swung about, upon the quaking boglands of Dalmazzo and his back to the broad waters of the Po. He swung his troops farther round, so as to bring his rear upon the only possible line of retreat, which was that broad firm land between Corno and Populo. At last his skilful manoeuvres achieved the desired result, and then, very gradually, fighting every inch of the ground, he began to fall back. At every yard now the front must grow narrower, and unless Bellarion’s captains were very sure of their ground, some of them would presently be in trouble in the bogs on either side. If this did not happen, they would soon find it impossible, save at great cost and without perceptible progress, to continue the engagement, and with night approaching they would be constrained to draw off. Theodore smiled darkly to himself in satisfaction, and took heart, well pleased with his clever tactics by which he had extricated himself from a dangerous situation. He had won a breathing-space that should enable him to marshal his men so as to deal with this rash enemy who came to seek him in the open.
And then suddenly, a quarter-mile away, from the direction of Corno, towards which they were so steadily falling back, came a pounding of hooves that swelled swiftly into a noise of thunder, and, before any measures could be taken to meet this new menace, Ugolino da Tenda’s horse was upon Theodore’s rear.
Ugolino had handled his condotta well, and strictly in accordance with his orders from Bellarion. From Balzola, whither he had been moved at noon so as to be in readiness, he had made a leisurely and cautious advance, filing his horse along the very edge of the bogland so that their hooves should give no warning of their approach. Thus until he had won within striking distance.

===Chinese===

可步兵配不上他们的统帅，又欠这套战法的操练。马是有被长矛戳倒的，可几乎每一匹倒下的马，都等于人墙上开了一个口子；贾索内·特罗塔的重骑就从这些口子里砸进来，抡着沉重的大锤。一场后卫战在西奥多这边迅速涨成全面会战的规模；而论处境，再没有比他更糟的了：左翼——此刻他已转过身来——陷在达尔马佐震颤的沼地上，背抵波河的宽水。他把队伍又转了转，把后队摆上唯一可能的退路——科尔诺与波波洛之间那道宽实的干地。末了，他那套巧妙的调度得了手；随后，一寸一寸地争夺着地面，开始缓缓后撤。此刻正面每一码都在收窄；贝拉里翁的队长们若不把地势拿得十拿九稳，有些人转眼就要陷进两侧的沼里出乱子。倘若这也不发生，他们很快就会发觉：再打下去，除了大损兵马而寸步不进，别无所得；夜一临，便只得撤围。西奥多暗暗得意地笑了，抖擞起来，很满意自己这套巧计，把自己从险境里摘了出来。他赢得了一口喘息，尽够他重整人马，收拾这个胆敢来旷野寻他的莽撞敌人。

就在这时，四分之一英里外，从科尔诺的方向——他们正稳稳退往的那个方向——传来一阵马蹄的擂动，转眼涨成雷声；不等采取任何应对这道新威胁的措施，乌戈利诺·达·滕达的马队已经砸在西奥多的后队上。

乌戈利诺这一手兵团带得好，严格照着贝拉里翁的军令。他从巴尔佐拉——正午移驻到那里待命——从容而谨慎地推进，马队沿着沼地的边沿衔枚而进，蹄声不至预警。就这样一直进到打击的距离。

===Original===

And the blow he now struck, heavy and unexpected, crumpled up Theodore’s rear, clove through, driving his men right and left to sink to their waists in the marshes, and scattered such fear and confusion in those ahead that their formation went to pieces, and gaped to Bellarion’s renewed frontal attacks.
Less than three hours that engagement lasted, and of all those who had taken the field with Theodore, saving perhaps a thousand who fled helter-skelter towards Trino after Ugolmo’s passage, there was not a survivor who had not yielded. Stripped of their arms and deprived of their horses, they were turned adrift, to go whithersoever they listed so long as it was outside of Montferrat territory. The maimed and wounded of Theodore’s army were conveyed by their fellows into the villages of Villanova, Terranova, and Grassi.
It was towards the third hour of that November night when the triumphant army, returning from that stricken field, reentered Casale, lighted by the bonfires that blazed in the streets, whilst the bells of Liutprand’s Cathedral crashed out their peals of victory. Deliriously did the populace acclaim Bellarion, Prince of Valsassina, in its enormous relief at being saved the hardships of a siege and delivered from the possible vengeance of Theodore for having opened its gates to Theodore’s enemies.
Theodore, on foot, marched proudly at the head of a little band of captives of rank, who had been retained by their captors for the sake of the ransoms they could pay. The jostling, pushing crowd hooted and execrated and mocked him in his hour of humiliation. White-faced, his head held high, he passed on apparently unmoved by that expression of human baseness, knowing in his heart that, if he had proved master, the acclamations now raised for his conqueror would have been raised for him by the very lips that now execrated him.
He was conducted to the palace, to the very room whence for so many years he had ruled the State of Montferrat, and there he found his nephew and niece awaiting him when he was brought in between Ugolino da Tenda and Giasone Trotta.
Bareheaded, stripped of his armour, his tall figure bowed, he stood like a criminal before them whilst they remained seated on either side of the writing-table that once had been his own. From the seat whence he had dispensed justice was justice now to be dispensed to him by his nephew.

===Chinese===

此刻他砸下的这一记又重又意外，把西奥多的后队砸得蜷了起来，一刀剖穿，把人赶得左右奔散、齐腰陷进沼里；又在前方的人心里撒下那样的恐惧和混乱，阵形散了架，给贝拉里翁正面的新攻豁开了口子。

这场会战打了不到三个钟头；随西奥多上阵的人，除了大约一千在乌戈利诺穿插之后抱头鼠窜奔特里诺的，没有一个不曾降服。他们被解了兵器、夺了马匹，放归自去——去哪里随便，只要出蒙费拉托的地界。西奥多军的伤残，由他们的同伴运进了维拉诺瓦、泰拉诺瓦和格拉西几座村子。

到那个十一月的夜的第三点钟，得胜的大军从战场回城，街道上篝火熊熊照路，柳特普兰德大教堂的钟撞出得胜的连声。全城如痴如狂地欢呼瓦尔萨西纳亲王贝拉里翁——他们大大松了一口气：围城的苦难免了，为着他们开门放进西奥多的仇人、可能遭到的报复也免了。

西奥多步行，傲然走在小小一队被俘贵人的前头——俘他们的人为着赎金把他们留下了。推推搡搡的人群，在他蒙辱的时辰朝他喝倒彩、咒骂、嘲弄。他脸色惨白，昂着头，一路走过去，对这副人类的卑劣显然无动于衷；他心里明白：倘若得胜的是他，此刻为他得胜者响起的欢呼，会从如今咒骂他的这几张嘴里喊出来。

他被押到宫里，押到那一间——多年来他治理蒙费拉托国的屋子；被乌戈利诺·达·滕达和贾索内·特罗塔夹带进来时，他见他的侄子和侄女正在等他。

免盔卸甲，高大的身子伛着，他像个罪犯立在他们面前；他们分坐在那张曾经属于他的书桌两边。从他发号施令施行审判的座位上，如今他的侄子要对他施行审判了。

===Original===

“You know your offence, my lord,” Gian Giacomo greeted him, a cold, dignified, and virile Gian Giacomo, in whom it was hardly possible to recognise the boy whom he had sought to ruin in body and in soul. “You know how you have been false to the trust reposed in you by my father, to whom God give peace. Have you anything to say in extenuation?”
He parted his lips, then stood there opening and closing his hands before he could sufficiently control himself to answer.
“In the hour of defeat, what can I do but cast myself upon your mercy?”
“Are we to pity you in defeat? Are we to forget in what you have been defeated?”
“I ask not that. I am in your hands, a captive, helpless. I do not claim mercy. I may not deserve it. I hope for it. That is all.”
They considered him, and found him a broken man, indeed.
“It is not for me to judge you,” said Gian Giacomo, “and I am glad to be relieved of that responsibility. For though you may have forgotten that I am of your blood, I cannot forget that you are of mine. Where is his highness of Valsassina?”
Theodore fell back a pace. “Will you set me at the mercy of that dastard?”
The Princess Valeria looked at him coldly. “He has won many titles since the day when to fight a villainy he pretended to become your spy. But the title you have just conferred upon him, coming from your lips, is the highest he has yet received. To be a dastard in the sight of a dastard is to be honourable in the sight of all upright men.”
Theodore’s white face writhed into a smile of malice. But he answered nothing in the little pause that followed before the door opened upon Bellarion.
He came in supported by two of his Swiss, and closely followed by Stoffel. His armour had been removed, and the right sleeve of his leather haqueton, as of the silken tunic and shirt beneath, had been ripped up, and now hung empty at his side, whilst his breast bulged where his arm was strapped to his body. He was very pale and obviously weak and in pain.
Valeria came to her feet at sight of him thus, and her face was whiter than his own.
“You are wounded, my lord!”
He smiled, rather whimsically. “It sometimes happens when men go to battle. But I think my Lord Theodore here has taken the deeper hurt.”
Stoffel pushed forward a chair, and the Swiss carefully lowered Bellarion to it. He sighed in relief, and leaned forward so as to avoid contact with the back.

===Chinese===

「你的罪状你自己知道，大人。」吉安·贾科莫向他开口——一个冷淡、尊严、有丈夫气的吉安·贾科莫，几乎认不出就是那个他曾在身心两路谋害的孩子。「你知道你怎样辜负了我父——愿上帝踢他安宁——托付给你的信任。你有什么可说的，从轻么？」

他张了张嘴，随后立在那里，双手攥了又松、松了又攥，才勉强按捺得住，答出话来。

「败军之际，我除了投身你们的慈悲，还能做什么？」

「败了就要我们怜惜？就忘了你败在什么上头？」

「我不求这个。我在你们手里，一个囚徒，无告无助。我不要求慈悲。我也许不配有。我指望它。仅此而已。」

他们打量他，看出这人的确垮了。

「审判你不是我的事，」吉安·贾科莫说，「我也乐得卸掉这副担子。因为你尽管忘了你我同血，我忘不了你与我同血。瓦尔萨西纳殿下在哪里？」

西奥多退了一步。「你要把我交到那个懦夫的刀下？」

瓦莱里娅公主冷冷地看着他。「自那日他为抗击一桩恶行、假意做你的细作以来，他已经挣得了许多头衔。可你方才赏他的这一个，出自你之口，是他到如今领受的最高一个。在懦夫眼里是懦夫的，在一切正直人眼里便是君子。」

西奥多惨白的脸扭出一个恶毒的笑。可他没答话；随后不久门开，贝拉里翁进来，小小一停里他什么也没说。

他由两名瑞士人搅着进来，施托费尔紧随在后。甲已经卸了；皮军衣、连同底下的绸衣和衬衫，右袖都撕裂了，空空地垂在身侧；胸前鼓着——胳膊捆扎在身上。他极苍白，明显虚弱而作痛。

瓦莱里娅一见他这样，站了起来，脸比他的还白。

「您伤了，大人！」

他颇为诙谐地一笑。「人去打仗，有时免不了。可我想，这里的西奥多大人，伤得更深。」

施托费尔推过一把椅子，瑞士人小心地把贝拉里翁放下去。他松了口气地一叹，把身子前倾，避开椅背。

===Original===

“One of your knights, my lord, broke my shoulder in the last charge.”
“I would he had broken your neck.”
“That was the intention.” Bellarion’s pale lips smiled. “But I am known as Bellarion the Fortunate.”
“Just now my lord had another name for you,” said Valeria, and Bellarion, observing the set of her lips and the scorn in her glance as it flickered over Theodore, marvelled at the power of hate in one naturally so gracious. He had had a taste of it, himself, he remembered, and perhaps she was but passing on to Theodore what rightly had belonged to him throughout. “He is a rash man,” she continued, “who will not trouble to conciliate the arbiter of his fate. My Lord Theodore has lost his guile, I think, together with the rest.”
“Aye,” said Bellarion, “we have stripped him of all save his life. Even his mask of benignity is gone.”
“You are noble!” said Theodore. “You gird at a captive! Am I to remain here to be mocked?”
“Not for me, faith,” Bellarion answered him. “I have never contemplated you with any pleasure. Take him away, Ugolino. Place him securely under guard. He shall have judgment tomorrow.”
“Dog!” said Theodore with venom, as he drew himself up to depart.
“That’s my device, as yours is the stag. Appropriate, all things considered. I had you in my mind when I adopted it.”
“I am punished for my weakness,” said Theodore. “I should have left Justice to wring your neck when you were its prisoner here in Casale.”
“I’ll repay the debt,” Bellarion answered him. “Your own neck shall remain unwrung so that you withdraw to your principality of Genoa and abide there. More of that tomorrow.”
Peremptorily he waved him away and Ugolino hustled him out. As the door closed again, Bellarion, relaxing the reins of his will, sank forward in a swoon.

===Chinese===

「末一冲里，您的一位骑士砸碎了我的肩。」

「我倒愿他砸断你的脖子。」

「那正是他的用意。」贝拉里翁苍白的嘴唇笑了。「可我的诨名是幸运的贝拉里翁。」

「方才大人还赏了我另一个名字。」瓦莱里娅说。贝拉里翁看着她唇边的线条、看她扫向西奥多的眼里的轻蔑，惊叹恨在一位天生这样仁厚的人身上竟有这样的大力气。他自己也领教过一回，他记得；也许她不过是把本该从头到尾归他的那份，如今转赠西奥多。「不肯费神去安抚自己命运的仲裁人，」她接着说，「是莽撞的人。西奥多大人的狡诈，我想，同其余的一起丢掉了。」

「是，」贝拉里翁说，「我们剥光了他的一切，只留了命。连他那副仁厚的假面也剥掉了。」

「您真高贵！」西奥多说。「揶揄一个囚徒！还要我留在这里受辱么？」

「不为我，真的。」贝拉里翁答他。「我从没怀着什么愉快看过你。带走，乌戈利诺。严加看管。明天审判他。」

「狗！」西奥多衔着毒说，挺身要走。

「那是我的纹章；你的纹章是鹿。方方面面看，都相称。我采它的时候，心里正想着你。」

「我这是为我的软弱受罚，」西奥多说。「当初你在这卡萨莱做司法的囚徒时，我就该由着它绞断你的脖子。」

「这笔债我还你，」贝拉里翁答他。「你自己的脖子保住不绞——只要你退回你的热那亚公国，安分待在那里。明天细谈。」

他不容分说地挥手赶他走，乌戈利诺把他押了出去。门再关上时，贝拉里翁一松那意志的缰绳，向前一晕，昏了过去。

## XV The Last Fight / 第十五章 最后一战

===Original===
When he recovered, he was lying on his sound side on a couch under the window, across which the curtains of painted and gilded leather had been drawn.

An elderly, bearded man in black was observing him, and someone whom he could not see was bathing his brow with a cool aromatic liquid. As he fetched a sigh that filled his lungs and quickened his senses into full consciousness, the man smiled.

“There! It will be well with him now. But he should be put to bed.”

“It shall be done,” said the woman who was bathing his brow, and her voice, soft and subdued, was the voice of the Princess Valeria. “His servants will be below by now. Send them to me as you go.”

The man bowed and went out. Slowly Bellarion turned his head, and looked up in wonder at the Princess with whom he was now alone. Her eyes, more liquid than their wont, smiled wistfully down upon him.

===Chinese===
当他苏醒过来时，正用未受伤的那一侧身子侧卧在窗下的一张软榻上；窗上垂着彩绘描金的皮革帘幕，严严实实地拉拢着。

一位蓄须的黑衣老者正俯身端详着他，另有个人站在他视线之外，正用清凉芬芳的药液轻轻拭洗着他的额头。待他深深吸进一口气，肺腑舒张，神智随之完全清明起来，那老者便露出了微笑。

“好了！这下他总算无碍了。不过还是该扶他上床歇息。”

“这就办妥。”替他拭额的女子轻声答道，那柔和而低婉的嗓音，正是瓦莱里娅公主的声线，“他的随从此刻想来已在楼下了。您出去时顺道叫他们上来见我吧。”

老者躬身退了出去。贝拉里翁缓缓转过头，望着如今只剩二人的室内，满怀惊异地仰面看向公主。她那双素来清澈却比往日更加莹润生光的眼眸，正带着几分怅惘与柔情俯视着他，微微含笑。

===Original===
“Madonna!” he exclaimed. “Do you serve me as a handmaid? That is not﻿ ﻿…”

“You are thinking it an insufficient return for your service to me. But you must give me time, sir, this is only a beginning.”

“I am not thinking that at all.”

“Then you are not thinking as you should. You are weak. Your wits work slowly. Else you might remember that for five years, in which you have been my loyal, noble, unswerving friend, I, immured in my stupidity, have been your enemy.”

“Ah!” he smiled. “I knew I should convince you in the end. Such knowledge gives us patience. A man may contain his soul for anything that is assured. It is the doubtful only that makes him fret and fume.”

“And you never doubted?” she asked him, wondering.

“I am too sure of myself,” he answered.

===Chinese===
“小姐！”他惊呼道，“您怎能像婢女一般侍奉我？这可万万……”

“您一定觉得，比起您为我效命的功劳，这点照料实在微不足道。不过请宽限我些时日，阁下，这还只是个开端。”

“我压根儿没有这么想过。”

“那便是您思虑不周了。您眼下身子虚弱，思绪也转得迟钝些。否则您早该记得：整整五年来，您始终是我忠贞不二、高义凛然、矢志不渝的友人，而我却作茧自缚、愚昧蒙心，一直把您当作死敌。”

“啊！”他笑了笑，“我就知道终有一天能叫您回心转意。这份笃定使人沉得住气。只要结局十拿九稳，人便能安守心神、静待时日；唯有捉摸不定之事，才会教人焦虑难安。”

“而您竟从来不曾怀疑过么？”她惊叹地问道。

“我对自己向来极有把握。”他答道。

===Original===
“And God knows you have cause to be, more cause than any man of whom ever I heard tell. Do you know, Lord Prince, that in these five years there is no evil I have not believed of you? I even deemed you a coward, on the word of that vain boaster Carmagnola.”

“He was none so wrong, by his own lights. I am not a fighter of his pattern. I have ever been careful of myself.”

“Your condition now proves that.”

“Oh, this, today﻿ ﻿… That was different. Too much depended on the issue. It was the last throw. I had to take a hand, much though I dislike a rough-and-tumble. So that we won through, it would not much have mattered if the vamplate of that fellow’s lance had brought up against my throat. There are no more fights for me, so what matter if I left my life in the last one?”

“The last one, Lord Prince!”

“And that is not my title any more. I am a prince no longer. I leave the rank behind with all the other vanities of the world.”

===Chinese===
“天主明鉴，您确实有十足的把握，比我生平听闻的任何人都更有把握。亲王阁下，您可知道，这五年来，凡是加在您头上的恶名，我几乎没有一桩不曾轻信？我甚至偏听卡尔马尼奥拉那个狂妄吹牛之徒的一面之词，把您当成个贪生怕死的懦夫。”

“依他自己的眼光来看，倒也没全看错。我本就不是他那一路的猛将。向来我都十分珍重自己的性命。”

“您此刻这副模样可真能证明这一点呢。”

“哦，今天这回……今天这情形不同。这一战干系太大了，已是孤注一掷的最后一搏。我虽素来厌恶近身肉搏的混战，也不得不亲自下场一试。只要能赢下这一仗，就算那家伙骑枪上的护手盘直顶到我咽喉上，又有什么要紧？此后我再无仗可打了，便是把性命留在这最后一战里，又有什么打紧？”

“最后一战，亲王阁下！”

“而且那也不是我的封号了。我不再是什么亲王。连同尘世间一切其他虚荣浮名，我都一并抛在身后了。”

===Original===
“You leave it behind?” She found him obscure.

“When I go back to Cigliano, which will be as soon as I can move.”

“What do you go to do at Cigliano?”

“What? Why, what the other brethren do. *Pax multa in cella.* The old abbot was right. There is yonder a peace for which I am craving now that my one task here is safely ended. In the world there is nothing for me.”

“Nothing!” She was amazed. “And in five years you have won so much!”

“Nothing that I covet,” he answered gently. “It is all vanity, all madness, greed, and bloodlust. I was not made for worldliness, and but for you I should never have known it. Now I have done.”

“And your dominions, Gavi and Valsassina?”

“I’ll bestow them upon you, madonna, if you will deign to accept a parting gift from these hands.”

===Chinese===
“您抛在身后？”她听得一头雾水，不明其意。

“等我一能动弹，我便要回奇利亚诺去了。”

“您回奇利亚诺去做什么？”

“做什么？自然是做别的修士们做的事。*Pax multa in cella.*（斗室之中多安宁。）那位老院长说得一点不错。既然我在这世上的唯一重任已然圆满功成，我此刻渴求的，便是修院那方的宁静。这尘世间已再无属于我的东西。”

“再无属于您的东西！”她惊愕不已，“可这五年来，您赢取了何等赫赫功业！”

“没有一样是我贪恋的，”他温言答道，“全都是虚空，全都是癫狂、贪婪与嗜血杀戮。我本不是为了这滚滚红尘而生的；若不是为了您，我这辈子断不会涉足其间。如今，一切都了结了。”

“那您的领地——加维和瓦尔萨西纳呢？”

“小姐，只要您肯屈尊收下这双手奉上的临别赠礼，我便将它们全数赠予您。”

===Original===
There was a long pause. She had drawn back a little. He could not see her face. “You have the fever, I think,” she said presently in an odd voice. “It is your hurt.”

He sighed. “Aye, you would think so. It is difficult for one reared in the world to understand that a man’s eyes should remain undazzled by its glitter. Yet, believe me, I leave it with but one regret.”

“And that?” The question came breathlessly upon a whisper.

“That the purpose for which I entered it remains unfulfilled. That I have learnt no Greek.”

Again there was a pause. Then she moved forward, rustling a little, and came directly into his line of vision.

“I hear your servants, I think. I will leave you now.”

“I thank you, madonna. God be with you.”

===Chinese===
屋里陷入一阵长久的沉默。她微微往后退开了些，他看不清她的面容。“我想您是发烧了，”过了一会儿，她用一种奇异的语调说道，“是伤口引起来的。”

他轻叹一声：“是啊，您自然会这么以为。在尘世中长成的人，很难理解一个人的双眼竟能不被红尘的浮华炫目所惑。然而请信我，我离开这尘世，唯独只留下一件憾事。”

“那是什么？”这一问微若耳语，几乎带着急促的喘息。

“那便是我当初踏入尘世的初衷至今未能如愿——我终究没能学成希腊语。”

室中又是一阵沉寂。随后她莲步轻移，衣袂发出轻微的窸窣声，走上前，正正落入他的视野之中。

“我想我听见您随从们的脚步声了。我这就先告辞了。”

“多谢您，小姐。愿天主与您同在。”

===Original===
But she did not go. She stood there between himself and the fireplace, slight and straight as on the first evening when he had seen her in her garden. She was dressed in a close-fitting gown of cloth of silver. He observed in particular now the tight sleeves which descended to the knuckles of her slim, tapering hands, and remembered that just such sleeves had she worn when first his eyes beheld her. Over this gown she wore a loose houppelande of sapphire velvet, reversed at throat and wide gaping sleeves with ermine. And there were sapphires in the silver caul that confined her abundant red-gold hair.

“Aye,” he said wistfully, dreamily, “it was just so you looked, and just so will I remember you as long as I remember anything. It is good to have served you, lady mine. It has made me glorious in my own eyes.”

“You have made yourself glorious, Lord Prince, in the eyes of all.”

“What do they matter?”

Slowly she came back to him. She was very pale and a little frown was puckering her fine brows. Very wistful, and mysterious as deep pools, were those dark eyes of hers. She came back, drawn by the words he had used, and more than the words, by something odd in his gently musing tone.

“Do I matter nothing, Bellarion?”

He smiled with an infinite sadness. “Must you ask that now? Does not the whole of my life in the world give you the answer, that never woman mattered more to a man? I have known no service but yours. And I have served you﻿—*per fas et nefas*.”

===Chinese===
然而她并未迈步离去。她就那么亭亭玉立地站在他与壁炉之间，身姿纤细而挺直，恰如当初那个傍晚他在她花园里初见她时一般无二。她里面穿了一袭贴身的银线织锦长裙；他此刻尤为留意到那双紧窄的衣袖一直垂落到她纤长玉手的指节处，记起她头一回映入他眼帘时，所穿的也正是这般样式的窄袖。长裙之外，她披着一件宽大的蓝宝石色天鹅绒乌普朗德长袍，领口与阔大敞开的袖口翻折出洁白的银鼠皮衬里。而束住她那一头丰沛赤金色秀发的银丝发网上，亦缀着颗颗璀璨的蓝宝石。

“是啊，”他神思恍惚地怅然道，“您当初正是这副模样；只要我一息尚存、记忆未泯，我脑海里便将永远铭记您此刻的模样。能够为您效命，实乃莫大的幸事，我的小姐。这让我在自己眼中也显得光彩照人。”

“您已在全天下人眼中成就了无上荣光，亲王阁下。”

“世人又算得了什么？”

她缓缓转回他身旁。她面色苍白如纸，两道秀眉微微蹙起。她那双深褐色的眼眸满蕴怅惘，幽深莫测得宛若潭水。她走了回来——与其说是被他方才那几句话所牵引，不如说是被他那温柔沉思语调里某种奇异的意味所牵动。

“那我呢，贝拉里翁，我难道也算不了什么么？”

他露出一抹带着无尽哀伤的微笑。“事到如今，您还要问这句话么？难道我在尘世度过的这全部岁月，不正是现成的回答——世上再没有哪个女子在一个男子心头占有过更重的分量？我平生只知为您一人效命。而且我侍奉您——无论正邪曲直（*per fas et nefas*）。”

===Original===
She stood above him, and her lips quivered. What she said when at last she spoke had no apparent bearing upon the subject.

“I am wearing your colours, Bellarion.”

Surprise flickered in his eyes, as they sought confirmation of her statement in the azure and argent of her wear.

“And I did not remark the chance,” he cried.

“Not chance. It is design.”

“It was sweetly and generously courteous so to honour me.”

“It was not only to honour you that I assumed these colours. Have they no message for you, Bellarion?”

===Chinese===
她垂立在他榻前，双唇微微颤抖。当她终于开口时，说出的话却仿佛与方才所谈风马牛不相及。

“我今日穿的是您的徽色，贝拉里翁。”

他眼中闪过一丝讶异，目光循着她的话音落到她一身蔚蓝与银白两色的衣饰上，似在印证她所言不虚。

“我竟没有留意到这一巧合！”他脱口道。

“并非巧合，而是有意为之。”

“您肯如此垂青赐荣，实在温婉大度、礼数周全。”

“我披上这身徽色，并不仅仅是为了尊崇您。难道这颜色里，就没有半点传给您的密意么，贝拉里翁？”

===Original===
“Message?” For the first time in their acquaintance she saw fear in his bold eyes.

“Clearly they have not; no message that you look for. You have said that you covet nothing in this world.”

“Nothing within my reach. To covet things beyond it is to taste the full bitterness of life.”

“Is there anything in the world that is not within your reach, Bellarion?”

He looked at her as she smiled down upon him through her tears. He caught his breath gaspingly. With his sound left hand he clutched her left which hung at the level of his head.

“I am mad, of course,” he choked.

“Not mad, Bellarion. Only stupid. Do you still covet nothing?”

===Chinese===
“密意？”自两人相识以来，她还是头一回在他那双向来胆大无畏的眸子里看见了怯意。

“显然是没有了——至少没有您所期盼的那种密意。您方才说过，这世上没有任何东西是您贪恋的。”

“力所能及之物，我一无所求。若去贪恋力所不能及之物，只会尝尽人生的苦汁。”

“这世上难道还有什么东西，是您贝拉里翁伸手够不到的么？”

他仰望着她——她正噙着泪水，低头朝他微笑。他倒抽一口凉气，气息陡然一窒。他用那只完好的左手，一把攥住了她垂在自己头侧高度的左手。

“我一定是疯了，”他声音哽咽地说。

“不是疯了，贝拉里翁，只是犯傻罢了。您如今还是一无所求么？”

===Original===
“Aye, one thing!” His face glowed. “One thing that would change into a living glory the tinsel glitter of the world, one thing that would make life﻿ ﻿… O God! What am I saying?”

“Why do you break off, Bellarion?”

“I am afraid!”

“Of me? Is there anything I could deny you, who have given all to serve me? Must I in return offer you all I have? Can you claim nothing for yourself?”

“Valeria!”

She stooped to kiss his lips. “My very hate of you in all these years was love dissembled. Because my spirit leapt to yours, almost from that first evening in the garden there, did it so wound and torture me to discover baseness in you. I should have trusted my own heart, rather than my erring senses, Bellarion. You warned me early that I am not good at inference. I have suffered as those suffer who are in rebellion against themselves.”

He pondered her, very pale and sorrowful. “Yes,” he said slowly, “I have the fever, as you said awhile ago. It must be that.”

===Chinese===
“不，我所求唯有一件！”他面庞霎时焕发出光彩，“唯有这一件，能把尘世华而不实的浮光点化成鲜活的荣光；唯有这一件，能让这一生……天主啊！我究竟在胡说些什么？”

“您为何把话咽回去了，贝拉里翁？”

“我害怕！”

“怕我么？您为侍奉我倾尽了一切，这世上难道还有什么是我能回绝您的？非要我主动把自己拥有的一切奉上作为报答才行么？您自己难道就半点不敢开口索取么？”

“瓦莱里娅！”

她俯下身，轻吻他的双唇。“这么多年来，我对您那彻骨的怨恨，原不过是乔装掩饰的深情。几乎从花园里初遇的那个傍晚起，我的心魂便已奔向了您，正因如此，每当我以为从您身上窥见卑劣行径时，才会那般肝肠寸断、备受煎熬。贝拉里翁，我本该信奉自己的本心，而非我那屡屡误判的耳目。您早就提醒过我，我不擅推理揣度。这些年来，我一直承受着与自己内心为敌之人的苦楚。”

他面色苍白、神情带着几分忧戚地凝神望着她。“是的，”他缓缓说道，“正如您方才说的，我确是发烧了。准是烧糊涂了。”
